reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, nice to walk along the promenade and there are loads of shops restaurants and pubsEasy to get to via Ferry from Circular Quay

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful walk and a nice trail/walkway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was such a nice walk and trail.  We wandered for about 6 miles.  The sites were lovely, lots of people milling about but not crowded.  Manly beach was bigger than I thought and quite nice.  We birded the whole way and found many cool birds along the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach via passenger ferry from Circular Quay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the passenger ferry from Circular Quay area (near the Opera House) for a quick 45 minute ride to the Manly Beach wharf area, which is conveniently located walking distance from the town and beach area.  The ferries are frequent and huge, accommodating hundreds of people both commuters, locals, and tourists alike. The beach at Manly beach is a short walk from the ferry stop, and there are lots of stores, restaurants, and bars along the way, along with street musicians.The beach is lively, and there is a nice paved walkway along the beach passing by hills, cliffs, and multi-million dollar homes.A nice siop for a brewski, burger and people watching is the pub at the historic Steve Hotel, which sits along the beach area and is a fun place to relax for a cold one or lunch.We spent the day at Manly Beach as tourists and loved it!  We took the ferry back, and timed it so it was early evening, offering stuffing views of the Sydney Harbor Bridge and Opera House.  Highly recommended by us1

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit to Manly beach by ferry from Circular Quay in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On our next-to-the-last day in Australia, advised of temperatures reaching 105 F, we decided to visit Manly, where the harbor and ocean beaches are only two blocks apart, so that it is a major center for surfing and surfers' culture in New South Wales. We took the public ferry from Circular Quay and the fast ferry back. The town was lovely, and exceedingly tourist-friendly, and there were some very interesting architectural gems along the main street between the two beaches. The ocean beach was closed due to a recent shark sighting, but both beaches were a beautiful sight to see. Don't miss Manly when you visit the Sydney area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a good place to visit with family or friends, you can just chill out or play in the waves as they are not too strong, very fun

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach for dining and ocena experiences
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach with up to 200 shops and restaurants nearby. It si best to arrive here - away from the weekends - by Uber or public transpiration. The beach umbrella/beach chair rentals are surprisingly affordable ($10 AUD per day) and worth every penny. The sand is perfect and the water is clear (no seaweed), but do pay attention to daily restrictions on swimming areas because riptides are a real danger. Also, be sure to walk to the far north end of the beach to explore the "Manly Wormhole" -  a natural tunnel between the Manly Beach cliff area and the next beach to the north.Finish the day if you like with a 15-minute ferry boat ride ($9 AUD) over to downtown Sydney for great views of the Sydney Opera House at Circular Quay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Classic suburb and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit to Sydney is not really complete if you have not visited Manly with its beaches and promenade along the water and from/to the ferry. Nice restaurants, pubs, hotels and so on so go there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful as ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The first ever surfing competition in the world was held here at Manley Ocean Beach. The 2 kilometer wide and open sandy beach is lined with tall pine trees, which is quite unique. At sunrise, with some people walking about and the sound of the waves, it's soporific. During jam-packed weekends, it's a great place for people-watching. If you're going to bring food here, just make sure the hungry seagulls don't grab your food first. We visit Manley Beach every time we visit Sydney. The 20-minute ferry from Circular Quay is inexpensive and wonderful. It affords you great views of the Opera House and the Sydney Bridge and much much more!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Mandy beach. Use the ferry and bus lines
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and walk through Mandly. Use the ferry; you see the opera and the bridge perfectly, only for 5 or 6 euros (on exchange).If you go for a few days, a different card per person is required to pay for the ferry. Economy price, but identify the passenger by associating them with their card.On the ferry you only have to cancel at the entrance.The bus in the city works very well, but there it is mandatory to cancel it on the way in and out. Starting at a maximum daily amount, you are no longer charged, even if you continue to use it. Example: a 333 circular line journey from Brisbane street to the end of the line at the jetties, 0.60 euros.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: ***Ocean breeze. Sunlight. Pure comfort at Manly Beach Guesthouse***
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach Guesthouse sits in a unique corner location where you can enjoy the refreshing ocean breeze from one of Manly Beach's most beautiful spots. Every room is newly upgraded with high-quality, ultra-comfortable beds and mattresses to ensure a perfect night's sleep. Natural light fills the entire property - every room and space has its own windows, creating a bight, airy and welcoming atmosphere. Cleanliness and comfort are our top priorities, and guests consistently appreciate the fresh, spotless environment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cute costal town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is absolutely a must-visit when in Sydney. The moment you step off the ferry, you’re greeted with that classic Aussie coastal vibe—relaxed, friendly, and full of energy. The beach itself is stunning, with wide golden sand, rolling waves, and plenty of space to stretch out, swim, or surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice outing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a 40 minute ferry ride from circular quay to Manley .. we walked on the Main Street to the end of the road which takes you to the waterfront and the beach . Lots of shops and restaurants on the way .. once you are at the beach .. you find nice sand and swimming + surfing opportunities.. or just sit back and admire the views of the ocean .. restaurants + pubs along the boardwalk are found .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely vibes here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth a visit as it has a lovely feel there. The lay out is simple but effective with a beautiful high street full of charm leads to a most beautiful beach with golden sand.It’s a magic formula

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surf surf surf baby
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of Sydney’s iconic beaches it was great to visit it during our recent stay. Gee it was busy around both the beach and town area. But that didn’t stop me from venturing in for a little swim and a play in the waves. The waves are huge and I was knocked over twice but that’s part of the fun right. Whilst we sat on the beach we witnessed a surf rescue. Those guys are superb at what they do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Graceob1,

Thank you for sharing your experience. We’re thrilled to hear you enjoyed the ferry ride, stunning views, and the shops at Manly. It’s great to know you found the beach a must visit while in Sydney, and we hope to welcome you back soon.

Kind regards 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach lived up to expectations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is one of those iconic beaches around the world and it lived up to its reputation when we visited. Sand for ever, plenty of sun (even is Aussie winter when we visited), plenty of people enjoying the water. A short ferry ride from Circular Quay in Sydney Harbour,  Manly is really easy to access. Once you have disembarked from the ferry, it's a short walk across to the beach. On this walk you will find plenty of options for food and drinks, from takeaway to sit down meals. There are plenty of shops too, and better than I expected. Not just the usual touristy stuff, but shops still serving the local community too. The beach itself is gorgeous... long, clean and stunning.  Plenty of 'friendly' gulls so be careful with your chips if walking along. It really is one of those places that you wish you could spend more time at

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunrise Vibes & Coastal Adventures in Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is absolutely magical at sunrise.Stretching wide and long, it offers plenty of space, even on busy weekends you can usually find a quiet spot further up the beach away from the crowds. Most visitors arriving by ferry head straight down the Corso to the main oceanfront, unaware that Manly is home to 14 other ocean and harbourside beaches waiting to be checked outBeyond the beaches, Manly boasts a vibrant selection of cafes, bars, and restaurants to suit every taste possible. For something truly special, take the scenic walk around to Shelly Beach via Fairy Bower. Its a awesome spot to snorkel and it’s a local favourite for good reason. And if you're feeling adventurous, the bushwalks around North Head offer breathtaking views of the city and a dose of nature right on the edge of the city.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very beautiful place where you can find peace and quiet I will repeat it again as soon as possible I recommend it
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 994marcoantoniol,

Thank you for your kind review! We’re so happy to hear you had such a wonderful time and found the place peaceful and beautiful. It’s lovely to know it left such a positive impression on you. We hope to see you again soon!

Thank you again for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly is a MUST stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi David B,

We really appreciate your thoughtful review. Manly is a beautiful place to stay, and it’s great to hear that you made the most of your visit—from the diverse beach options and excellent snorkeling to the scenic walks and lively weekend markets. The short ferry ride from Sydney certainly adds to its charm. We're so pleased you had a memorable experience and hope to welcome you back again soon.
Thank you again.

Kind regards 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Over Bondi - Beach, Rainforests, and Natural Swimming Pools, Oh My!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi inspiruption, 

Thank you so much for your lovely review. We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed your day in Manly and had the chance to experience its many highlights—from the scenic nature walks and natural rock pools to the beautiful architecture. We're so glad you took the time to explore everything Manly has to offer!
Thank you again

Kind regards 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach ever!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ClarkeyFamily,

Thank you so much for your kind review. It sounds like you had a truly memorable six weeks in beautiful Manly with your family! We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed your stay and found plenty of activities to keep everyone entertained. We’d love to welcome you back again in the future.

Thank you again for taking the time to write a review. 

Manly Visitors Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dreaming in Blue: The Allure of Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi kerry b

What an amazing testament to the attraction of Manly - that you would love to live here. And we would love to have you if ever that came to pass. We happily welcome all-comers, whether as a short-term visitor or as a permanent move.

We live here, and everyday we still marvel at the beauty of the place.

We'd love to welcome you back soon.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferry to Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The ferry ride itself is short but scenic, offering beautiful views of the harbor. Once we arrived, we found plenty of great eateries and shops to explore. The beach was clean, relaxing, and perfect for a leisurely stroll or just soaking in the coastal vibes.Manly has a laid-back, fun atmosphere that makes it a must-visit while in Sydney. I highly recommend making time for this little getaway across the wateryou won’t regret it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Do the Spit Bridge Walk to Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Someone had told us to take the ferry from CBD to Manly. However, instead we did the Spit Bridge Walk to Manly, a gorgeous 10 kilometer walk along the North Harbour, and we were very glad we did. The views are spectacular.To get to the trailhead at Spit Bridge, we took a bus from Wynyard station. We weren't sure how to get from the Spit Bridge bus stop to the trailhead because there was no signage, so we just followed some other people who looked like hikers.After walking around Manley, we had lunch at Garfish, which was very quiet and a step up from the fish-and-chips eateries elsewhere.Then we took the ferry from Manley Wharf back to Circular Quay.You can Google how to do this walk, since I'm told I can't post links here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent Beach, but not on a cold July day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a short walk from the Manly wharf where you get off the ferry. Manly beach is a sweeping curve of sand almost tropical.july is not the best time for beach visiting in Australia. only a few hardy individuals were in the water.However it is still a great beach. There are lots of varying places to get something to eat and drink, just back from the beach. Also not far to walk to the shopping area of Corso.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Scenic
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi lucycan

You've pointed out one of the great things about Manly - the beach is basically part of the village, both in proximity as well as culturally.

As the host of the first World Surfing Championship in 1964, surfing and swimming is in Manly's DNA.

Emerge from the water, wander across the sand and find yourself in the heart of downtown Manly, with it's shops, cafes, restaurants and pubs. It's convenient, it's fun and most of all it's so very Australian. 

Thank you for the review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice nice nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi francescoc501

While there's no commercial fishing going on in Manly, there is certainly a lot of fish and chips.

Grab some takeaway and set up at the beachfront for an alfresco lunch with a view, or take a table in one of the many restaurants and cafes that also serve up this popular fried fare, from fine dining establishments to casual eateries.

Thank you for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferry to Manly Recommended
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi grascots

The ferry ride is certainly a highlight on a day trip to Manly.

Once here, the beautiful views continue, whether beach-side over stunning Manly Beach and pretty little Shelly Beach, or from the clifftop at North Head's stunning Fairfax Walk or on the lovely Manly Scenic Walkway.

Thank you for your review.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A famous spot to visit and well worthwhile
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Z587YQ

Thank you for your review.

Manly is the perfect day trip from the city, making it extremely popular among visitor's to Sydney and locals who live in our surrounding suburbs.

You're right to recommend sunscreen, especially during the hot months when the UV index is at it's peak.

We also have plenty of shaded areas along our beaches thanks to our beautiful Norfolk Island pine trees, meaning you can still enjoy this area while staying cool and limiting sun exposure.

Please come again. 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Pretty Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi luvtravel88

Thanks for the review.

While we're sorry you didn't enjoy the Manly village area, we're pleased Manly Beach made up for it.

It's a lovely long stretch of sand and surf broken up into three areas - South Steyne (at the end of the Corso), North Steyne and Queenscliff - each with its own lifesaving club and lifesavers.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Umar T

So nice of you to give our beach such a great 5-star review.

It does turn on the charm, particularly on a blue sky day when the water is clear and warm.

The waterside walk around to Shelly Beach is a must-do, while the beachside dining at the Boathouse is as close as you'll get to picnicking on the sand.

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach for wave lovers. Manly is generally worth a visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 261gens

Thanks for your review.

It sounds like you had a great time here in Manly and enjoyed the most prominent of our many beaches, that being Manly Cove as well as world-famous Manly Beach.

Fun fact - we actually have 8 beaches here in Manly, with some tucked away in the national park but just as stunning as our glamourous namesake.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great waves when we went!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi CaesarBrutus

While it's a shame you couldn't swim on the day you visited, the best thing about those big surf days is watching the incredible waves as they roll through and the surfers brave and talented enough to take them on.

Sit and admire their talents from Manly beachfront, and then wander around to Shelly Beach and up onto the headland to look down onto the more extreme breaks named Deadmans and Winkipop.

There are many beautiful swimming days as well, so please come back and see us next time - with time to let your swimmers dry :)

 Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great day trip to beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi familyoffour50

Thanks for the review.

As you rightly point out, while there are many Northern Beaches tours to join from the city - from motorcycle experiences to plane trips - it's very easy and quick to simply go it alone and catch the beautifully scenic Manly Ferry across the harbour for the perfect day trip to Manly and beyond.

We're glad you enjoyed our beaches - we have so many there's something for everyone. Choose from surfing and swimming in the waves at famous Manly Beach, hiring a SUP at Manly Cove or exploring underwater with snorkel and goggles at Shelly Beach.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing beaches minutes away using the ferry
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi PourJF

Thanks for the great advice regarding how to pay for our public transport and the requirement for one credit card per person.

If this is not possible, Opal Cards are widely available from outlets located around the city.

Both credit cards and Opal Card have the same benefits, with daily and weekly maximums applied to travel costs.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at manly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a stunning beach, clean sands, lifeguards on hand, plenty of eateries near the beach front and some really nice shops a short walk from the beach. There was a market on in the main shopping area with lots of stalls offering all kinds of things including local arts and crafts.Don’t worry if you have no towel or sunshade as these can be rented on the beach at very reasonable prices.We got the ferry from darling harbour, inky takes about 20mins so you get to see more stunning scenic views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: full and clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Pavolc434
Visitors to Sydney are spoilt for choice when it comes to famous beaches, with Bondi on one side of the harbour and Manly on the other.
We're so pleased you decided to travel to Manly, regularly voted among the top beaches in the world.
It's not only beautiful, it's also very versatile, catering to most water pursuits from high-energy surfing through to relaxed sea swimming, gentle paddling, and underwater snorkelling adventures.

Thank you for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach and Town.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Tammye89
We're glad you discovered Manly as the perfect day trip from the Sydney CBD, being only a 20-minute ferry ride across one of the most scenic harbours in the world.
Cafes and restaurants abound, the pace is relaxed and beachy, and the beautiful blue ocean beckons.
Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly beach is definitely worth a day trip from Sydney. Only 20 minutes away by ferry, the view ont he way to Manly is already worth the trip. Once in Manly strolling down the Corso is really cool. Plenty of shops and restaurants in the area, either on the wharf, the Corso or the streets around it. Beautiful beaches all around Manly, my favourite Manly Beach for its beautiful sand, its location close to the Corso and the quality of the water. If you go for more than a day, I suggest doing the Spit bridge to Manly walk. Its a wonderful walk on the coast with lots of scenic views and beautiful beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed 10 beautiful days in Manly! The weather was delightful.We stayed five days in a VRBO that was right off the Corso (shopping plaza that doesn't allow cars)and five days in Manly Pacific hotel facing the ocean. Both were clean, quiet and near the beach, restaurants, and shopping!  We enjoyed happy hour on the rooftop of the Styne hotel, many desserts at Yo-Chi, every breakfast at the Pacific  Manley, dinner with an ocean view at The Pantry Restaurant and the shopping on the Corso!  There was a street fair on Saturday and we purchased several souvenirs from local artists to bring home. We walked to Sandy Beach, did the hike from Shelly Beach to Spit and went to the Taranga zoo! We found Manley Beach to be a great spot to stay and use as a home base and explore the area. We did a day trip to the Blue Mountains via the train and hired a guide to hike the Grand Canyon. We went to the Fish Market and the Aquarium. It was easy to catch the ferry to Sydney Harbor and Circulare Quay (20 minute ferry ride) to visit the Sydney Opera House and Barangaroo. Two weeks in Sydney and a lifetime of memories!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach to spend the day
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Luisa R,

Thank you for your kind words! We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed the scenic ferry trip to beautiful Manly and had the chance to explore the wide range of activities and shops available.

Thank you again

 Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Mobile46721920866,

We’re delighted to hear that you enjoyed the area, took in the beauty of our stunning beach, and discovered some wonderful dining spots among the many options Manly has to offer. Thank you for sharing your experience!

Thank you 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold Winter Breeze at Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Jermummy, 

Thank you for taking the time to write a review. So glad to hear your kids had a fun time playing in the sea even though it was June and fairly cold.  We are lucky that there is also plenty of shops and places to eat and enjoy the views at that time of year. 

Thank you again. 

Manly Visitors Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach - good ambiance
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Neat place to go. Little bit of everything to do here. Lots of shops to see. Beach is nice and huge. Catch a wave and do some surfing. Nice places to grab a drink or something to eat. Next time in Sydney I’m going to spend more time here. Only downside is actually getting here. Wasn’t bad when we were there - didn’t have to wait for a ferry. But if they get busy I can see how it would take away from the desire to come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beats Bondi beach by quite a margin
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 69albertz
You've summed up very nicely the comparison between these two world-famous beaches, with Manly coming out on top.
We also find Manly has a lovely relaxed coastal Aussie vibe that isn't always evident at the more "city" beaches, and this feeling becomes even more obvious as you travel north from Manly along our beautiful Northern Beaches peninsula.
Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This would be a five star if it were not for the dead jellies that we found.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is not getting five stars because we saw quite a few dead blue bottles on the shore. They could be the non-stinging variety, but I don’t like worrying about jellyfish when I’m in the water!That said, they were plenty of families playing in the water. It’s a beautiful beach with nice, clear, warmish water and soft sand that also features a wonderful beach-walk where you can take dramatic photos on the rocks (See photos).Fantastic, well-paved beach walk that also features a delightful beachfront, free swimming pool. (Also, see photos).The surrounding town has a great deal of cute little restaurants and shops to pop into as well!Just a little worrisome that there were jellies.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What’s better than a manly beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So a friend and I were visiting from the states and had to try out at least one beach in Australia. Our Aussie friends highly recommended Manly beach. The beach is clean and lively, pet friendly. There was so much a person can do at the bench. A lot of restaurants and there was even a market going on where artist were selling merchandise. I really enjoy manly beach and I recommend going.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: so many seagull, but this is a beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi rlahuddin
As you rightly point out, the seagulls can be quite persistent in their pursuit of food. Unfortunately many people feed them, which encourages this behaviour.
We're glad you saw the funny side of it.
Our best advice for people who don't want to deal with this is to eat in one of our many lovely cafes and restaurants, or for those who want to enjoy their takeaway in the great outdoors with a beautiful beach view, don't feed the seagulls and keep your eyes peeled.
Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take the ferry
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Nicholas G
Even on a busy day, Manly certainly has a more relaxed vibe than some of our more "city" beaches.
The Northern Beaches in its entirety exudes that quintessential Aussie coastal ambience, from Manly in the south to Palm Beach in the north.
And there's definitely plenty to do beyond the beach, ranging from stunning bush walks and history tours, to stand-up paddle boarding on the harbour and wind-in-your-hair beachside cycling.
Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, Sand, and Sydney Charm
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach charmed us with its sunny, mild climate and stunning natural beauty. We felt safe and comfortable thanks to the clean, well-maintained beach and friendly atmosphere. Whether strolling along the Corso, surfing the waves, or simply relaxing on the sand, Manly offered the perfect blend of relaxation and activity for our couple's escape.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi SeeTheW0rld62
You're right, Manly Beach is great fun on a warm day! Whether you're swimming, surfing, snorkelling or simply strolling the beachfront and shopping in the Corso, Manly has so much to offer.
Even through the cooler months this area is perfect for scenic walks and exploring by bike.
We hope to see you again soon.
Thanks
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lot to do and see at Manly.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 116damiens, 

Thank you very much for your kind review. We are very happy to hear you had an enjoyable day at Manly. Taking in  beautiful Manly beach, the shopping and eateries on offer. 

Thank you again for your review.

Manly Visitors Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Surprised by beautiful, sweeping ocean beach.To be honest, wasn’t aware Manly on a peninsula.As tourist given the advice for a spectacular ferry trip, do CQ to Manly.Randomly walked up the “Corsi” and wowed a little by huge seascape & beach.Walked a while on pathway and enjoyed the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Novotel at Manly Beach a great location with amazing beach during the day and a great nightlife.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Lots of cafes and restaurants in walking distance. Accommodation is a little high if you’re in peak season. I recommend the Novotel for its location and views of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Even in southern winter (August) it's worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After 25 minutes crossing by classic ferry (not the fast, more expensive) we arrive at Manli.Head to the famous beach where brave surfers and swimmers - the water must be 16 degrees in this month of August, are in the water. After setting foot in the water, watching the beach volleyball players and sitting in the sun, we took the very well marked paths to discover part of the island and the Australian flora and fauna in this beautiful nature park.Beach and / or hiking, small restaurant by the sea, there is no shortage of activities!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach is lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi tommomelbourne, 

Thank you very much for taking the time to write a review and sharing your thoughts on Manly Beach. It's great to hear that you enjoyed spending time here. Manly Beach indeed offers a unique charm with its low rise architecture and relaxed atmosphere.

Thank you again for your review.

Kind Regards 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Chris S

How great to hear that Manly Beach is being recommended by our fellow Sydneysiders.

A day out in Manly definitely deserves a place on any Emerald City itinerary, being a quick, easy and beautifully scenic ferry ride from the CBD and offering stunning beaches, scenic hiking and historical adventures.

Thanks for the accurate advice about the use of a credit or debit card for travelling on public transport - they offer all the same benefits as the Opal Card for adult travellers, but be sure to check your bank fees. Travel passes for children can be purchased from authorised sellers, while the senior's card is available from Circular Quay for Australia citizens. 

Kind regards

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach, plenty of action
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have just had a week staying opposite the Manly beach.A great spot for water activities, always people swimming, surfing, playing beach volley ball on the courts set up on the beach.Plenty of toilet and shower facilities.It is a lovely spot for a walk anytime of the day but especially in the morning when it can be very busy.The beach is well maintained and always looks clean.Beautifull Norfolk Pines line the walkway between the beach and road.All in all a beautiful spot to spend time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Views
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi B2167ZTalanb

We're glad to hear you enjoyed your visit to Manly, and that while you did experience some rain, you could still enjoy the beauty of our village.

The trip across Sydney Harbour is definitely one of the best in the world, showcasing some of Australia's most well-known landmarks and giving visitors amazing views of our craggy harborside cliffs and beautiful national park.

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach just outside the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly.After passing through the streets of Manly town from Manly Wharf, you will see the beach on the other side of the sea.The ferry takes less than 30 minutes, there are many cafes in Manly town, and it's great to have a beautiful beach so close to the city.It was early autumn, and if the weather had been good we could still have gone swimming, but unfortunately the weather was bad so we just strolled along the promenade on the right side of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfer's Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 1998V70,

Thank you so much for your review.

The ferry is indeed a really quick trip, we hope you really enjoyed the ferry trip. We hope you also had the opportunity to walk around to Shelly Beach, that's also incredibly beautiful!

Come and see us again soon.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly, beach and beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When choosing a beach in Sydney, we opted for this one, first because of its proximity, ease of transportation (ferry) and comments about its beauty.Although it is not just a beach, almost a city, more extensive than we assumed, it is the beach that makes it so visited.Extensive beach, we had a sunny day, so its beauty increases, many people but that does not prevent us from walking through it both inside and along its coastlineYou can spend a nice day visiting its small center and going down to the beach or walking around it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach is wide, scenic, with few tourists, creating an excellent atmosphere overall.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi cyfu98

Thank you for your review.

Manly is a great place to stay when visiting Sydney. It's perfect as a stand-alone destination, while as the 'Gateway to the Northern Beaches' it is a great base to explore all the peninsular has to offer, with it's long list of stunning beaches extending all the way north to Palm Beach.

A short 20-minute ferry ride from Manly will land you in the heart of Sydney, allowing for a great day trip.

Come and see us again soon.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: U stole my heart manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ET3121,

Thank you so much for your kind words! We are thrilled to hear that you enjoyed your day at Manly. It's truly a place that captures your heart.

It's great to hear that both the protected kids beach near the ferry wharf and the main beach with its inviting waves and golden sand were such a hit with your family. Manly truly offers an idyllic setting for families to relax and make cherished memories by the water.

Thank you once again for sharing your experience with us. We hope to welcome you back to Manly soon for another unforgettable day of sun, surf, and relaxation by the sea!

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just a great way to spend time in afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Grandpa356

Manly Beach is certainly a lovely way to spend an afternoon, or a whole day for those with more available time in their diary.

As Tripadvisor's recently named seventh best beach in the world, Manly has plenty to offer in terms of surf, sun and magical views.

It also has a delightful little village centre with a range of shops, some of the best walking trails in Sydney and an interesting and visible history ranging from our First Nations heritage through to quarantine and wartime challenges, surfing glory and Olympic success stories.

Manly also stands as the Gateway to the Northern Beaches, providing a launch pad to further adventures along our 32km stretch of peninsula.

Thanks and hope to see you again

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: On the beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi smiler1956

Thanks for taking the time to share your experience of Manly, where you can have yourself a very merry - and beachy - little Christmas.

While Northern Hemisphere Santa traverses snowbound landscapes, here on the Northern Beaches of Sydney the sun shines bright and hot while we celebrate all the holidays traditions with decorated trees, carols and plenty of amazing light displays.

Even our winters don't put paid to beachside enjoyment, with surfing and other water sports enjoyed year round, and our crisp weather perfect for enjoying waterside walking and scenic bushland hikes.

Manly is definitely a year-round destination.

Thanks

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Y415IZmichellen

Thank you for your 5-star review.

The Northern Beaches is renowned for its beautiful beaches stretching from here in Manly all the way up to Palm Beach 32km north. 

As I write this, the water temperature sits at a balmy 23 degrees Celsius, which is perfect for swimming, snorkelling and all the many water sports we enjoy here in Manly.

Thanks for visiting

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi heatherp5088AZ,

We are so glad to hear you had such a wonderful visit to Manly. We agree it is well worth the visit and taking your time to enjoy what Manly has to offer. Thank you so much for taking the time to write this review. 

Many thanks 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take the ferry from Sydney to Manley Beach the place is incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You dream of surfing beaches and places to swim, Manley is the placeNo need for a parasol, there is just a team on the left who welcomes you and rents you deckchairs, tents (or gazebos) to relax with your familyIncredible sunscreen at the entrance to the beachYou have everyone there to eat but Australians love picnics (barbecue available)The ocean is very rough but you can go to the right of the beach there is a calm cove which will allow you to swimWe preferred to swim near the first aid station between the two flags because an army of lifeguards ensures your safety.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice day activity
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi rochelleforster

We're very sorry to hear your visit to Manly was impacted by an accident and hope the outcome was a positive one for those involved.

So pleased to hear you found Shelly Beach, which not only provides some respite from the wind, sitting as it does behind a little headland. It is a beautiful beach with amazing snorkelling and scuba diving within the Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve.

Thank you for visiting and reviewing

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice area
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Gerry K,

We're glad that you enjoyed your trip to Manly. We really are spoilt for choice with all the different shops, cafes and restaurants around here. We hope to see you here in Manly again in the near future.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: During my first visit to Sydney - took a ferry out to Manly for a lovely morning at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While visiting Sydney for the first time, decided to take the Manly Ferry to Manly on an early Sunday (to beat the afternoon crowds) on a nice sunny day.  The ferry ride was nice and relaxing. Upon arriving at the Manly Wharf, I just followed the crowds that were heading to the beach.  The beach was pretty nice, especially with the crescent moon coastline and the tall pine trees along the beach.  There is a walking trail that runs along the beach for a nice walk.  There are several shops and restaurants between the wharf and the beach, so plenty of things to do.  If traveling to Sydney for first time, I would recommend a ferry ride over to Manly, it was about 20 minutes on the fast ferry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly has it all!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For both  exiting Sydney Harbour &  entering Sydney Harbour on returning  from Manly, the trip on the boat is  worth it alone for the fantastic views .!  Manly has a delightful beach  and fashionable shops that  entice you in.  Anita Gelato ice cream before you board the boat on the way back to Sydney harbour will make you want to return again to beautiful Manly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family Friendly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:

 Thank you very much for your lovely, detailed review.  We're delighted you enjoyed the family-friendly beach, its calm bay, and the surrounding amenities. 

Thank you again
Manly Visitor Information

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous for a visit..... don't forget the suntan lotion
reviewsWithKeywords.text:

Thank you again

Manly Visitors I formation Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place and animals roaming free
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi MelibeeB,

Thank you again
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Inner peace
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took ferry from Circular Quay, one way ticket is AUD 10. The ride is about 20min. Its very scenic and comfortable journey and you are passing the Opera house so also great views. In Manly station there is an information center with super friendly staff who will explain anything you need. Its also easy to find your own way to Manly beach. We walked to Manly Wormhole which is about 20min walk one way. Its a small cave at the end of the beach with stunning views and peace vibes. The beach is great for surfing or other sports activities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:

Thank you for your review. We're so pleased you enjoyed Manly Beach.

Thanks for pointing out the lifeguards - it's really important for visitors to know that we have a large contingent of these skilled surf technicians who ensure all beachgoers are safe and can fully enjoy their time in the water.

Manly Beach actually has three surf clubs along its length - Manly, North Steyne and Queenscliff.

Regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach, Steyne Hotel/pub nostalgia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fast-ferry to Manly, pedestriansed The Corso, little boutiques, cloudless blue sky - fab.  Manly wharf through the town to the oceanside - gelati, giant Christmas tree, water-fountains – cool. The Steyne pub/hotel still there, offers iconic awesome views of Manly beach.  We haven't visited Sydney for many years. Stunning beach, met friends for lunch - our trip to Manly was fantastic. (I have gait/walking challenges (stroke), wear a legbrace.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For the waves and the walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi turboostmatt

It sounds like the wind might have whipped up some great surf, which is fantastic to watch even if you don't surf.

And isn't Shelly Beach a lovely little spot? So great for swimming, snorkelling and scuba diving within the protected marine area known as Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice boat trip with good views.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi jarmot2013

Thank you for your review.

While it's disappointing that you were a little underwhelmed by Manly Beach, we're pleased to hear you enjoyed your visit on the whole.

Manly has so much to offer in terms of views, bush walks, an intriguing history, great hospitality and beautiful beaches that sparkle on our many sunny days and provide no end of adrenaline-fuelled entertainment when the big surf rolls through.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauty and the Beast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited here on a Sunday. Very crowded streets and beach. Lots of people to watch and lots of stores. Paid $59 for 3 hours of parking when we took the ferry into Sydney. We had an OK time but we found Bondi beach the next day to be less crowded and less commercial. If you can only visit one, my vote is with Bondi. Oh, and don’t park near the ferry wharf at Manly if you don’t want to get ripped off for $59.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful MANLY Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches in the world, hands down. Very clean and a great place for kids as there are lots of parks and playgrounds behind the beach. The waves were good when we were there and we enjoyed walking along the corridor.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After catching the Manly ferry from Circular Quay it took 20 minutes to get to Manly beach. It's a beautiful area. Countless shops, restaurants, fast food outlets, Gift shops and shops of all types are everywhere. On the day we visited there was a street Market with many lovely items to choose from. The beach itself is wonderful. There is also a trail where people can walk along the shore and enjoy panoramic views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had said that Cronulla was the most beautiful but Manly was certainly much better… beautiful place with a nice coastline and a perfect stretch of sand. Many people playing sports such as footvolley, volleyball and beach tennis.Lots of people surfing and plenty of options for eating nearby.There are no tents on the beach like in Brazil.But there are restaurants in the nearby streets.Public bathroom ok and people polite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi misletten,

Thank you for for taking the time to right your lovely review about Manly, we are so pleased you enjoyed your visit. 

Thank you 

Manly Visitor Information

reviewsWithKeywords.title: spit bridge to manly walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is a beautiful city with a lot to do. For example, you have to do the spit bridge to manly walk. It’s wonderful and you will discover beautiful places… My favorite was Delwood beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Easy beach trip from Sydney  for snorkeling.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the Manly Ferry from Circular Quay for a 30 minute trip through the harbor to Manly Beach. When we arrived, we stopped by the information station, where we got very helpful suggestions and directions, including the best places to snorkel. A short walk across the island took us to the beach. We looked for umbrellas or chairs for rent, but did not see any. There was about 1 - 2 meter surf and many surfers. We walked some more to Shelly Beach for snorkeling.  There was a little surge and visibility was 2-3 meters. Water was about 18 Celsius, so we wore wetsuits. We saw many fish including blue groupers, wrasses and several other types. There is an ID board at the beach for the different species.  There is not much shade but a few places to sit or picnic. A rinsing area is near the path back to Manly Beach. We had dinner at Wahlburgers and took the ferry back to Sydney. It was a beautiful beach day during our stop in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi reeceyb,

Thank you very much for your review, we hope you can return another day to enjoy a swim and sunbathe.

Thank you 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My friend's son who has been residing in Australia for the past 10 years, strongly recommended that we visit this beach attraction while in Sydney. I was initially undecided whether to go to Bondi Beach or this Manly Beach.But Manly Beach was easy and more direct to travel from our apartment at Kings Cross. On our very first day in Sydney  we had already purchased an Opal card with a top up value of $50/-.  We can have unlimited rides once we clock $17/- spent rides and we could use the Opal card on trains as well as ferry. From Kings Cross station, we took the train to Circular Quay and took the ferry at one of the wharves terminal direct to Manly Beach. The journey is about 22 minutes. It was a smooth cruise ride.  Once we reached our destination, I sought advice from the Manly Visitors' Information booth on the way to the beach and the attractions. It was highly recommended to take the walk along the beachfront from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach or visit the village center for some shopping and food.Instead of heading to the beach  the ladies in our group were attracted by a shop 'Reduce  Reuse and Restore' selling second hand clothing. The garment were very fashionable and stylish though they were second hand. One of the ladies bought a jean for only 10 bucks. I was fascinated by the Manly War Memorial erected in front of the rows of shops. A salute to the ANZAC soldiers who perished during the two world wars.While the ladies in our group were still engrossed in their window shopping, I decided to take a stroll along the beach from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach. It was an awesome walk and it reminded me of the long stretch of the bathing beaches in Xiamen. Manly Beach was crowded but the walk along the beach walkway was relaxing and meditative as my ears were tuned to the splashing rhythm of the waves and my eyes staring at the long horizon of the blue ocean. As I approached Cabbage Tree Bay and Shelly Beach,  I could see young picnickers playing or lying near the beach enjoying the sunbath. It is school holidays and many came here for their vacation.There were monitor lizards appearing here and there but there were signages that warn visitors from touching these water dragons.At the end of Shelly Beach, I walked up the stairs to the Bower Street and was amazed by the picturesque seaview and the cliff edge at the entrance of Sydney Harbour National Park.Great beach. No wonder it was voted by TripAdvisor as the Best among the best beaches in 2023.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very fast access from CBD
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 113alin

Thanks for your review.

The ferries are a fast and beautiful way to make the journey from the CBD to Manly and the Northern Beaches. Running every 20 minutes up to midnight, they are also a very convenient way to travel.

Once here,  Manly Beach and the village centre are very accessible, being flat and with many paved walkways.

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: ONE OF THE GREATEST BEACH IN THE SYDNEY
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi odkhuum

Thank you for your feedback. Sounds like you had a great time in Manly.

There are always amazing restaurant specials on offer. Pop in to see us at the Visitor Information Centre on Manly Wharf Forecourt for a full list of meal deals as well as happy hour specials in our local watering holes.

Kind regards

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach that was very quiet on our visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Realistic_travellers

With a wide walkway along the entire length of Manly Beach and around to Shelly Beach, there is plenty of space for casual ocean- and people-watching, as well as ample opportunity for sand-free beachside days and dining.

If you'd prefer table service with your meal, there are many restaurants and cafes along the beachfront that afford great ocean views.

Thanks for visiting and sharing your thoughts.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Who could ask for more.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was wonderful weather, it probably always is.  The trip across to Manly was exciting across the bay in one of the traditional ferries even though quite short.  When you arrive it is already like being on holiday and the beach is a delight.  Wonderful sand, lovely shops, trees and warm water.   Who could ask for more.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi M622POjoshh

Thanks for such a glowing review of Manly Beach.

It's certainly a great place to visit with kids.

Nearby Shelly Beach, a short and scenic walk from Manly Surf Club, is also wonderful for the young ones as the swimming is safe and calm. It also hosts a colourful array or underwater life and sights, sitting as it does within the protected marine park Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve. Pack the snorkel and goggles or hire locally to enjoy all this area has to offer.  

Thank you
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful setting and in the heart of Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Joel K

Thank you for your review.

With a village centre that is flat and easily accessible, and with a position overlooking our famous beach, Manly is perfectly situated for visitors looking to experience our beautiful surroundings.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi danmY5870PP

We're so pleased you enjoyed Manly, and even discovered the Worm Hole.

Did you know it was carved out by fishermen more than 100 years ago? 

For those seeking to find it, turn left at the end of the Corso and walk along the beach to Queenscliff, then walk around the ocean rockpool and voila!

The best time to visit is in the morning in order to catch the sun. But take care at high tide and if there are large waves as the rocks can be slippery.

Thank you
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for a Day Trip or a Stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had great luck during our visit to Manly Beach and saw a lot of dolphins as we walked along the beach. We stopped and had an excellent breakfast, some gelato and did a couple of short hikes in the area as well. If it was warmer we would be up for a swim but we did see a lot of people surfing and snorkeling in the area.We took the Manly Ferry from Circular Quay at Wharf 2. It was a 30 minute ride and gave us an excellent view of the harbour even though it was very windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Rajiv, 

Thank you very much for taking the time to write a review on your trip to Manly. We are very lucky to have this beautiful area just a short ferry trip away from Sydney. 

Thank you again for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Une_Bella,

We are really happy to hear you had an enjoyable day at Manly and beautiful Shelley Beach. It is always lovely to hear of peoples experiences. 

Thank you for your review.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Michael-4551

Sounds like you're a bit of regular to Manly. We're so pleased that you enjoy our beautiful beach and ferry journey.

Next time you visit perhaps drop in to see us at the Visitor Centre and we could recommend some other walks around Manly and into our national parks.

Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi razza61,

We're so glad that you enjoyed your time in Manly.

I think you've discovered the wonders of Manly being a peninsula with beaches all over!

Thank you for taking the time for leaving this review, we hope you visit Manly and the Northern Beaches again.

Cheers,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Special Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly has a very homey feel. As soon as you get off the ferry and head down the Corso, there is an anticipation that you will soon see the wide expanse of ocean at the end. The sight never disappoints and is always breathtaking. We keep coming back here and enjoy walking along the beachfront. You can walk all the way to Shelly Beach on one end or else walk all the way up to Queenscliff on the other end. A very special place no matter what time of the day or what season of the year.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach is a favorite holiday destination
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach has been a favorite of mine, ever since I first visited the Beach as a teenager. Manly Beach is known as the birthplace of surfing in Australia. The Beach has an expanse of white sand, perfect for a picnic. The Norfolk Island Pines, sometime called Australian Pines, are a feature of Manly Beach. Manly Beach is one of Sydney's  best Pacific beaches. Getting to Manly by ferry from Circular Quay is easy. Manly is 17 km (11 miles) north-east of Sydney. Manly is a favorite holiday destination.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi wiseguy1282005

Such a nice observation - that Manly Beach feels more "natural" than Bondi. 

This side of the Harbour tends to have a more casual vibe than the city-side beaches.

Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts on Manly.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly doesn't disappoint!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is well worth a visit. While Bondi is more famous, I think Manly is more beautiful. You can catch a ferry from Circular Quay and they seem to run pretty regularly, maybe every 30 mins or so  - it's about a 40 min ride. I strolled from the harbor thru the streets to the beach. I have to say it was pretty busy (late mid-March on a 36C-degree day).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Marvelous Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beautiful ferry ride from Sydney's Circular Quay to Manly is well worth doing! There's a fast ferry and a slower one (for a few more AUD). I took the slow one over to Manly, 40 mins. The view was lovely, and it was so easy on arrival to walk to the beach. There's a main street lined with shops and restaurants and on a Saturday in March, there was a marketplace.Would definitely go again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly over Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi BarbB416

Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts on Manly Beach.

We hope you also got to enjoy the water - it's the perfect way to cool down on a hot day.

Thanks again
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having only been to Bondi beach I didn't know what to expect.For me this beats Bondi by miles.A great promenade walk around a crescent shaped bay. A few little shops and cafes to break the walk.Lovely beach with a salt water pool nestling in the rocks of the bay.Stunning!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi D7270IDlizg

Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts on Manly.

We agree the walk from Manly to Shelly Beach is a lovely one,  meandering along Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve.

Regards

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Recently Rated in the Top 25 Best Beaches in the World
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have travelled the world extensively and seen a lot of beaches. So many positives with fine clean sand kept clean and tidy by the local Council, no rocks and just pure golden sand, patrolled by lifesavers with flags indicating where to swim safely with shops, cafes and restaurants on the opposite side of the street. A very popular boardwalk with seating and tables. Along the full length are 3 separate beach areas. The only issue is parking as it is very popular so allow extra time to find a parking spot or pay for parking in the car parks. Include a walk to Manly Wharf as it has a great hotel, more good restanrants and watch the ferries come and go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Highly recommendable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Following a local recommendation, we took the ferry close to the Opera House, to Manly Beach. Very pleasant 15-20 minutes journey especially to watch Sydney's skyline from the distance. Once in Manly, you discover a small village plenty of shops, restaurants, etc... and a magnificent beach to stay quite longer. Highly recommendable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi takes all the credit and attention but Manly is equally good. I took the fast ferry to the port. Manly has a very chill vibe to the area. I visited in may and it was windy and cold but it didnt stop hundreds of people from enjoying  the beach. A lot of options regarding food and drinks qroujd the area with cool and trendy cafes and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Wonderful Sunny Day at Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi matthewhN8108XK

Thanks so much for taking the time to write a review about your visit to Manly.

We're so pleased you got to enjoy a beautiful sunny day - Manly is always at its best basking in the sunshine.

And great words about what to pack - swimmers and sunscreen are a must if you want to fully immerse yourself in the Manly Beach experience. But if you happen to pack a bit light, we've got plenty of surf shops and other stores on hand to help you out.

Thank you
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Retro beautiful seaside location
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ACathy3

Thank you for taking the time to write a review. Sounds like you had a great day in Manly.
The path you walked is a very popular one for visitors and locals alike, extending through the vibrant Corso shopping area and around to lovely little Shelly Beach, which happens to be one of the only west-facing beaches on the Australian east coast. Such a shame you didn't have your swimmers because with its protected position and abundant marine life, Shelly Beach is the perfect place to swim and snorkel. It is actually part of the marine protected area of Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve. 

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A memory to hold
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi amsafari

Thank you for such a great review. We couldn't have said it better ourselves, especially regarding the ferry ride, which is surely one of the most scenic in the world.

While we agree Manly can feel like an island with its harbour crossing, it's actually part of mainland Sydney and the gateway to Sydney's Northern Beaches - a 30km stretch of beautiful beach suburbs extending north of Sydney Harbour. If we're lucky enough to welcome you as a visitor again, pop into our centre on the Manly Wharf forecourt and our staff can advise on other areas of the Northern Beaches you might like to visit.

Thank you
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Highlight of our trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi melhop

Thanks for your description of Manly as a "highlight" of your trip to Sydney!
Many visitors are surprised to find such beautiful beaches and relaxed coastal ambience so close to Sydney CBD.

The walk you enjoyed so much - from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach - is one of our favourites too. The views are amazing, the walking easy and the destination one of the loveliest little beaches around, offering calm waters for swimming and abundant marine life for those keen to snorkel of scuba dive.

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Drizzle
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi heichiuu

Thank you for your review.
While Manly really shines in the sunshine, we're pleased to hear that a little cloud and rain didn't put a dampener on your visit. The occasional inclement weather often brings with it some spectacular surfing conditions which make for great viewing from the shoreline - or out in the surf from those skilled on a board.
Thanks 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry from Circular Key, after about 25 minutes we arrived at Manly. It’s a short walk through the local High Street to get to Manly Beach. It was actually quite similar to a typical British seaside town, with various shops selling tat and lots of pubs and takeaways. We arrived at the beach and it was absolutely packed, being a sunny Sunday afternoon. It was stunning though, lovely golden sands and blue sea. We chilled on the beach for a while before deciding to head back to central Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Magic
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
HI banksie2-0,

Thank you very much for your wonderful review. We are very lucky to have so many beautiful beaches and options available in Manly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly North Head Sanctuary Hike
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having been to Sydney many times before, I thought it was time I ventured out of the CBD this time and so I visited Manly. I’m not that much of a beachgoer, so it was great there were hiking trails available that I could do on my day trip there.Getting to Manly was incredibly easy; the Manly Ferry from Circular Quay is quite regular with the ride taking about 30min and costs less than $10 one-way on the Opal Card (and you don’t need to touch off at Manly). Note, there is also the Manly Fast Ferry which I believe is a bit more expensive and I don’t think the ride to Manly is that much faster than the normal ferry.There are toilets onboard the ferry, otherwise there is one at Manly Wharf. Head towards the wharf exit and then on your right side look for a sign that says “Carpark Toilets”. You can take the lift down but the stairs are faster. The toilets are cleanish a bit like those I would expect at the beach. If you’re along The Corso shops (the main shopping area in Manly) there is also another set of toilets opposite the Fishmongers Manly restaurant.I started off at The Corso and made my way down to Manly Beach, going clockwise. Many stops were made during my almost 3hr hike including Cabbage Tree Bay, Shelly Beach, then following the Shelly Beach to Barracks Precinct Walk path, visited City Lookouts, Third Quarantine Cemetery, North Fort, Memorial Walk, and unfortunately North Head was closed during my visit early December even though the signage said construction until November. Arriving at Q Station, I followed Scenic Drive which becomes Darley Road and walked all the way back to The Corso. Overall, it was enjoyable hike, got to see a different Sydney but remember to bring sunscreen, hat and water.=TIPS=•	There are 2 ferries that go to Manly – one normal, cheaper and the other is the Manly Fast Ferry which is slightly more expensive and I think maybe 5 or 10 minutes faster than the normal ferry.•	There are signs throughout the hike but why not drop by the Information Centre just outside the Manly Wharf to have a chat to staff to find out more and also grab a map to see where you’re going?•	A short while after Shelly’s Beach, if you keep hiking up, you’ll come across a little gate with a sign that says no dogs. This is the gate you can go through to continue your hike. The guy at the Information Centre told me people are hesitant going through the gate but it’s open.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good pub food at reasonable prices

There are so many activities on offer, from lazing on the golden sands, surfing the waves or exploring the underwater world whilst snorkelling or diving. You can also explore the surrounding area by renting a bike, or walking one of the many walking tracks on offer. When its time to refuel, there are many restaurants, cafes and pubs where you can sate your thirst or hunger!  Make sure you call in at the Manly Information Visitor Centre, located on the wharf forecourt, as you exit the ferry terminal. Here you can pick up your free map as well as handy tips from the local staff. We look forward to seeing you soon.

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is my favorite beach, when I visit Sydney it's a must to make a trip to Manly at least once. It's a wonderful place with a nice pedestrian zone, beautiful beaches and walkways. It is part of a huge city but the natural beauty is near and easy to reach. Take your time and leave the most visited place. Walk further on and don't stop at Shelly Beach walk further on to the lookout and enjoy the fantastic panoramic view. I enjoyed my last visits and enjoyed swimming at the guarded beach, walked to the lookout near Shelly Beach and strolled through Manly. It was great and worth to visit again even. The easiest way to go to Manly is by ferry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Every trip to Sydney, we make at least a few trips over to Manly by ferry. Arriving in Manly Cove is lovely and protected swimming beaches. Walk through the main mall to Manly Beach which is fabulous. My favourite is to walk around to Shelley Beach and have lunch and drinks at the Boathouse Restaurant. Keep an eye out for happy hours. Another great place is the Manly 16’ Skiff Club, especially Monday, Tuesday and Thursday nights. Make sure you book, it’s very popular. In saying that there is so many great places to eat, relax and take in the scenery. Manly has everything, great walks along the harbour and ocean sides.

It was lovely!Manly Beach is not very broad, it's a rather narrow stretch of sand, but flanked by the lovely trees, it's a sight for sore eyes. The water is crystal clear and on sunny days, the sea seems so inviting. Whether to take a swim or surf or to sit and observe the fun and frolic around, the Manly beach is an awesome place; i prefer it to the more famous Bondi Beach.There are a number of decent places to grab a meal nearby. There is also Shelley Beach, which is smaller but no less inviting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better than Bondi!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I grew up on Manly Beach and I think the setting beats Bondi hands down with the picturesque Norfolk Island pines. Catch the ferry from Circular Quay and after the delightful 30 minute ride to Manly, stroll along The Corso to the ocean beach. Even if the waves are big there is usually a calmer, safer swimming spot at the very end of the beach where it is more protected. However, always swim between the flags so you are always under the protective eyes of the Life Savers on duty. There are restaurants and cafes all along the beachfront catering to all appetites and pockets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don‘t miss Manly Beach and visit also Shelly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The trip on the big ferry from Circular Quai to Manly takes about 30 minutes and is already an experience in itself.  In Manly you walk through the car-free Corso towards the beach.  The walk to the large beach takes a maximum of 10 minutes, if you don't get too distracted by the many shops, coffee shops etc. The mile-wide beach is overwhelming.  "Swimm between the flags" is rightly said here and guarded beach sections are available!  A walk to Shelly Beach, about 20 minutes away, is particularly nice.  A well-developed foot and bicycle path leads there.  Shelly Beach (picture 2) is located in a nature reserve, is protected from the big waves and is particularly suitable for swimming and snorkeling.  Cloakrooms and a restaurant are available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy surfing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long even stretch of beach with many beach volleyball courts set up in one area. Very large waves popular with surfers. Lots of restaurants and bars across the road from the beach, where you can sit and watch the surfers. Easy access to beach from Manly Wharf, where the ferry docks. There is a nice walk round to the next bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Far from the best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly gets massive crowds, due to its fame as well as the infrastructure (ferry, restaurants, etc). However, I don't go to beaches to be surrounded by massive crowds. It is hard to enjoy yourself when you have to fight to get your patch of sand or  spot in the surf.Positives: + My wife preferred the option of sitting under the shade of the trees, something you don't get at many beaches. + Plenty of options for getting lunch.Negatives:- The aforementioned crowds.- Good luck finding a parking spot anywhere near the beach.- The sand is very uneven, both on the beach and in the water.- Lots of doof doof music being played.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A good swim on a windy day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the beach the last day on having the hop-on-hop-off ticket for a ferry. It was a bit overcast, but warm weather, so had our swimming suits with us.There was a netted area for swimming and the waves were reasonable size, so had a good swim.The beach wasn't crouded at all, maybe because of a bit cloudy day. Water felt a bit chilly at first, but not too bad to enjoy the swim.There were signs warning about penguins around, but didn't see any.There were changing rooms for swimmers down by the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manley beach, Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is by far one of the best beach areas I've been to - better than Bondi - huge beach, great waves, very safe, lifeguards on duty and a lovely walk along the bay ending at another small beach and two very nice restaurants. The shopping area in Manley is also worth looking at. When you get off the ferry at Manley don't think the beach is there, you have to walk straight ahead through the town and come to it on the other side.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great to watch the surfers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very popular island and beach easily reached from Sydney by boat..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is a beautiful island with a shopping street of small stores, a picturesque crescent-shaped beach, and walking paths. I've been here before during the week. This time, I went on a Sunday in January. I urge that, if you have the flexibility, visit on a weekday for a wonderful day on this very pretty getaway a half-hour by boat from Sydney. Manly is extremely popular with locals and visitors in summer and primarily on weekends. On Sundays, Sydney public transport (which includes the ferries) has a maximum charge for the entire day's transport of less than $3 for those with an Opal magnetic transit card. The Manly boats, which run every 20-30 minutes on weekends, the island, and its beach overflow to capacity. Regardless of when you go, it's a great way to escape the busy city for a day of island breezes, lunch along the water's walkway, lifeguard-protected swimming, easy hiking, and an exuberant friends and families energy. Sit or stand in the rear upon departing Sydney (in the front on the return) for superb photography of the Harbour Bridge, the Sydney skyline, and the Opera House.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Underwhelmed i'm afraid.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With this being our first trip to Australia we were of course keen to see the many amazing beaches that it has to offer and Manly was one that was often recommended to us,well i have to say that it really didn't impress me much.We had taken the ferry over from Circular Quay which was a pleasant journey and the  town itself was nice enough to stroll around but for me the beach itself was not really what i had expected.Yes it has a lovely long stretch of sand and the view of the waves crashing in was pretty impressive but the sight of a long waste pipe going into the sea and not being able to enter the water due to the conditions sort of spoiled things,i get the safety reasons for not being able to go in the water but for me that sort of defeats the point of a beach.I have to add that we also visited Bondi during our stay and for all 4 of us that visited that would win hands down every time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Spot for lunch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have only ever visited Manly during the day. It's a great spot to have lunch or a few drinks at the many bars and restaurants on offer and they also have weekly markets where you can find some unique items. It's also a short lovely stroll to Shelley beach which is a great place to swim with the kids or enjoy a refreshing drink or lunch at the cafe/ bar. Manly has a lot of souvenir shops along with boutique shop and you'll never be short of a chemist. There are also some rooftop bars overlooking the water with lovely food choices on the menus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can travel to Manly beach by taking a ferry from Circular Quay. Depending on if you have an Opal card or paying for a single ticket, a will cost you $5.65 to $9.40.The journey to Manly wharf is nice and takes you past the Sydney Opera house.Once you get to Manly wharf, it's about a 5 to 10 min walk to the beach past a number of food, souvenir, clothes and other shops.The beach itself is beautiful smooth sand and warm water. There are life guards who  duty. When I visited, they had the southern end set up for swimmers and the other areas for surfers. This was due to some strong rips on that day.You can also hire some beach gear. Along the other side of the road, are eateries that you can sit at and enjoy the view. I can imagine how busy this place can get on the weekends.You could spend a lot of time here or just a couple of hours.

Hi RexieByronBay

Shame that you caught us on a busy day, with the warmer weather and the great love for Manly Beach we are getting busier and busier every season.  

Summer is peak season all round Sydney but it doesn't have to be touristy!

Next time you visit, take the back streets rather than The Corso, or explore a little further afield towards Queenscliff Beach to discover some of the other great local beaches which are far less busy.  

Manly is a gateway to the Northern Beaches peninsular, so there is oh so much to explore. We can guarantee you can always find a quiet hidden gem,  where you can enjoy peace and quiet down at the beach.  

Next time please just pop in to see us and ask us for some hot tips!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visiting Manly N S W Australia.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Getting to Manly is a journey in itself!Manly is located on the North Shore of the Sydney CBD and is a coastal city within itself. Manly is accessible by road, however if visiting and you do not have access to a vehicle the most popular way of visiting Manly from Sydney if by water. “The Manly Ferry” runs at approx 20 minutes intervals from Circular Quay going to Manly and the same again leaving Manly heading back to Circular Quay. Once on the Ferry the views you get from the outside deck are some of the most spectacular in the world, Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Opera House, Luna Park, Cruise Ships, beautiful yachts spectacular Homes including Kirribilli House, our “Australian White House” A Fast ferry also services Manly.Once in Manly, if arriving by Ferry you walk out from the Manly Wharf onto the “Corso” Which is a mall that leads to the Manly Esplanade. Walking the Corso you will encounter many cafes, restaurants, gift shops and swim wear & surf shops, if you decide to go for a swim or go body surfing.Manly is known for its surf, sun bathing, outdoor exercising & beach sport. Once you have reached the end of the Corso u have the option of turning Left or Right. My suggestion is if looking at the ocean turn right and if you are up to taking a stroll you can walk all the way along the esplanade up over the hill and view “Shelly Beach” which is a marine sanctuary and on most days home to many scuba divers checking out the marine life. Once finished your stroll head back to the main section of the cafe strip and enjoy a meal of local Seafood or anything else of your choice.The climate is tropical and shorts and tee shirt are normally the standard dress. Manly is a beautiful part of the world and well worth a full days visit as part of your holiday in Sydney NSW Australia
