reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, sand and surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With sand stretching from Queenscliff Rock Pool at the north end to Manly Life Saving Club at the south end, Manly Beach looked pleasant enough. I'll leave it to others to compare it to Bondi Beach (see my review, "Bondi's up!"). At Manly, shoppers were taking advantage of the beach's proximity to The Corso (see my review, "Sign me up!"), and surfers were taking advantage of a nice break. We quickly broke for North Head Sanctuary, though, and its spectacular ocean, cliff and Sydney skyline views (see my review, "Incredible skyline view"). TIPS:--We took a Sydney Ferries public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly Wharf; the trip is a tourist destination in itself (see my Sydney Ferries review, "Truly a top attraction").

reviewsWithKeywords.text:

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t debate it, visit Manly!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We heard from a lot of locals that Manly was the place to go, so we did our research between Bondi and Manly and found Manly fit more with what we were looking for. We took the fast ferry from Circular Quay to Manly, very easy ride, and once dropped off it was literally a straight shot (short walk) to Manly beach. The sand is lovely, the views are great, not too many people! There was a lifeguard on duty because of strong currents and he was very engaged and ensured everyone stayed safe... we loved the walk from Manly to Shelly (about 15 mins) and found an awesome salt water pool right by the beach where we could enjoy the water even though currents were strong... it’s a really lovely place! We are glad locals told us to do this!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In my opinion, its prettier than Bondi beach. El Corso boulevard has places for shopping and eating for all pockets. The sand is white and fine. Waves not as big an Bondi and that's a plus for me. There's a path parallel to the shore that is a pleasure to walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on a Monday after taking the ferry from Sydney. Easy to get to the beach from the ferry terminal. The beach was busy but not too crowded. We had a very nice walk along the promenade towards Shelly Beach and the nature reserve. Both Manly and Shelly beaches were beautiful and not spoiled by over commercialisation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exciting and busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited BOndi by getting off the hop on hop off double decker bus. Had a delicious lunch at the local hotel. Ice cream from a specialty ice creamery! People everywhere, lots of shops and a beautiful, busy beach. Then back on the bus! A great day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I won't say that this is the best beach in Sydney since I only visited Manly and Bondi, but I really enjoyed Manly Beach. It is gorgeous, and there is a lot more going on here than there was at Bondi. There's a better selection of food and shopping at Manly, and there's a small park about a block from the ferry that is nice for people-watching. I also had some of the best fish and trips here that I had during my entire 3 weeks in Australia (and I ate a lot of fish and chips during those 3 weeks). If I am back in Sydney again, I will definitely return to Manly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: There is more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visit Manly beach. Take the boat from Wharf 3. Go strait to Manly beach, watch the beautiful beach and leave this beach which is mostly overcrowded except in spring weekdays. Take a hike to North head Sanctuary! It takes 1.5 hours: beautiful trip, stunning views of sea, beaches and far away Sidney. Half way visit restaurant Bella Vista. What a spot! Walk down to Manly, but take the direction to Collins beach. A secret, most beautiful and deserted. Toen back to the boat in Manly in 15 minutes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had limited time in Sydney as it was just a stop over for us, so we decided to take the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly.  The ferry took about 30-40 mins and we were able to take in the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Sydney Opera House and the Sydney skyline. It’s a lovely scenic trip. Once in Manly we made our way towards the beach. It’s not as big as I imagined but there were a few surfers, the sand was golden and the whole area had a magical vibe about it. The shops were ok but along a sea facing stretch of road were numerous sea food restaurants. We ate in one and it was excellent.  Manly is a beautiful place to visit and I would recommend that this should be every visitors to see list.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip to Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get the Ferry to Manly from Circular Key and walk down the corso to beach at opposite end of Ferry to hit Manley Beach. Stunning long beach with great public toilet facilities. Enjoy a gelatto .... yummy as you enjoy the local shops on the corso!! I also had some barramundi and chips in Manley local fish shop/market just off the corso . It is a well known fish shop that also cooks fish to eat or take away. Great little spot to check out while in Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Excursion to spend a day
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi bdg100

Thanks for the review - the ferry is a great way to travel here, either take the public ferry or if you are in a hurry, the private ferry takes only 18 minutes. There are several restaurants where you can enjoy seafood, either sit down or take-away. Watch out for those pesky seagulls who will literally steal the food from your mouth!!

Hope to see you back here one day!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quay ( buy the Opal Card and use for travel on ferry ) $ 7.50 each way was worth just the view of Sydney harbor . Very enjoyable couple of hours on Manly Beach .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great area. Interesting shops and eateries. Surf school and miles of beautiful clean beach. Manly has so much more to offer than Bondi and is an absolute must if visiting Sydney. Easily reached by ferry from circular quay no need to book. The ferries run regularly and can be paid for with your  Opal card which covers you for bus, rail and light railway (tram). Do it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney's BEST beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Oh well, I could be as it was my birthplace but the sweeping circular golden beach friinged with the stately Norfolk pines is just stunning. Walk around thee point near the Manly Surf club to experience an beautiful walk to a hidden wonder, Shelley Beach which is a marine sanctuary. A fabulous place to snorkel!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi  E8119SCchristopherk,
So glad you loved our beautiful beaches - did you know there are a number of harbour beaches that you can visit as well. 
We would thoroughly recommend calling into the Manly Visitors Information Centre when you arrive on the ferry where you will be met by friendly locals and much information about the area. 
Thanks for reviewing Manly Beach!
 Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely Sunday visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While staying in Sydney we went to Manly and spent some time walking the foreshore.Being a lovely sunny Sunday it was quite busy, lots of surfers in the water doing their thing and kids playing beach volleyball, looks like you could have lessons there.Only early spring but plenty of people in the water.Had not been there for many years and I was interested to read that surfing in Australia started here at Manly.Have to visit here when in Sydney, plenty of places to eat and a good market on the Sunday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry from Sydney Harbour to Manly Beach  and I as so glad that we did. What a beautiful little gem of a place. The tree lined espleanade is great for a shopping spree and the beach at the far end is just stunning. A beautiful bay of golden sand, attracting surfers, sun bathers and beach volleyball players. We had lunch just across the road, which was perfect. There is such a relaxed vibe here,  I could have easily stayed far longer. A must visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So romantic and relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the ferry to Manly is one tap on only,no need to tap off very easy walk down to the beach just sat there to eat fish and chips. don’t let the seagulls  have your food they will pursue everyone’s food. friendly locals the shopping was quite reasonable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean place for adults and families
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Roger W,
So glad you loved our beautiful beaches! 

We would thoroughly recommend calling into the Manly Visitors Information Centre when you arrive on the ferry where you will be met by friendly locals and much information about the area. 

With more than 150 cafes and restaurants,  you have  lots of options!

Thanks for reviewing Manly Beach! Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking alone
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Saintjoan2001

It sounds as though you enjoyed the Manly to Spit Bridge harbour walk which is a 10km walk along the coastline. Next time you come to Manly you will have to call in at the Manly Visitors Information Centre where the friendly staff can give you a map and explain some of the other walks to you.

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi cannylass72

Thanks for your 5* review - it sounds as though you walked from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach along the Cabbage Tree Bay Coastal walk which gives you some amazing views of the coast and the northern beaches. So happy to hear that you found it clean! Hope to see you back in Manly again one day.
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly a Slice of Heaven!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is a ferry ride across Sydney Harbor from downtown Sydney. Gorgeous enclave plenty of beach walks and hiking abound!! Great restaurants and shopping and convenient to everything. A must stay for several days to get away from the bustle of Sydney yet close enough to enjoy all the surrounding area offers!! People are friendly and not too expensive!! Top three beaches in Australia!! Good On Ya Mate!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Furnman61

So glad you loved our beautiful beaches - did you know there are a number of harbour beaches that you can visit as well. We would thoroughly recommend calling into the Manly Visitors Information Centre when you arrive on the ferry where you will be met by friendly locals and much information about the area.
Thanks for reviewing Manly Beach!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Joythornely

Great to hear you experienced an awesome day in Manly and you managed to discover a variety of restaurants and cafes to visit. Also good to hear that you found the beach clean, many people are aware these days that we can no longer afford to pollute our oceans by discarding litter. We look forward to seeing you again in Manly one day!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views but cold water
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ryanschock

Winter water temperatures can be a lot cooler than summer and one option if you would like to swim is to hire a wetsuit and you will then be super snug! Make sure you call in at the Manly Visitors Info Centre where the friendly staff can organise wetsuit hire and more!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful 1 mile long crescent beach with active promenade.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the crowded noon Manly Ferry($5 US each) for its 1/2 hour scenic cruise through Sydney's harbors. After arriving at Manly wharf, we crossed over the 500 meter 'Corso' to the beach, realizing we had come on the final day of the yearly Jazz Festival. Strolling the Marine Parade promenade, we discovered the south half was also filled with an extended weekend craft market. We continued to the Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve for its beautiful view of secluded Shelly Beach.Returning we stopped to use the public restrooms at the Manly Life Saving Club but the queue was far too long.  A nearby restaurant was the answer as was Ben & Jerry's for ice cream before returning to the wharf for the every 1/2 hour ferry back to the Circular Quay. Wonderful afternoon in active Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Australia Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi sherone1958

Thanks for taking time to write a great review. It is so good to hear that people love coming back to Manly and what more could you want for a wonderful day out - beach, ice-cream, good coffee and a beautiful ferry ride!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the popular beaches in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi DeshmukhV

Glad you enjoyed your trip to Manly - the promenade walk to Shelly Beach is one of the most beautiful walks in Sydney! Manly itself has a huge variety of cafes, bars and restaurants to choose from. Next time you visit Manly, make sure you call in at the Manly Visitors Info Centre to get some tips from the friendly local staff on where to go!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tremendous Magnetic Appeal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Once you disembarked at the Manly Wharf, you can sensed the magnetic appeal of the  beach. Girls in their bikinis and boys wearing their swimming trunks and roller skates are walking to and fro along the boulevard. The beach itself are full of sun worshippers lying on the sun while others are swimming against the waves. It is a sight to watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very peaceful holiday vibe
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi genelow16,

Thanks for visiting Manly Beach. If you come on the right day you might be lucky and escape the crowds, which is what it sounds like happened to you guys!

Come back soon,

The Hello Manly Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lounge, Walk, and People Watch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, long beach (plenty of space to spread out when we were there). Even if you don't plan to swim, you can get beautiful views walking the shoreline with your toes in the ocean. Watch the surfers or the kiddos making sandcastles. Easy access to public restrooms. Can rent your own surf experience if interested as well. There are water washing stations to get all that sand off your feet as well!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: simply the best!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: YOU want sun?? You got it at Manly and ice-creams...mmmmm!With all the bronze curves and tiny clothings!!! I can't resists the temptation of the waters to cool myself...Ladies loves being admired like in european beaches here on Manly!!Fish and chip highly recommended and a few night-life romantic restaurants to chew before retiring to my rented room also at reasonable price.The atmostphere you would want to take home to remember those photos you took backing you to come back time when you're in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach, a Must
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Kreuzlingen1,

Thanks for visiting Manly Beach and writing such a great review. We're proud of our many restaurants, cafes and shops and especially the ferry. The fast ferry is 20 minutes compared to the normal ferry which takes 30 mins. Sometimes it's nice to enjoy that extra time getting to the beach before everyone else!

Much love,
Hello Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Underwhelmed
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Diana B,

Unfortunately Sydney's weather is all over the place at the moment, so one day will be freezing, while the next is a perfect summers day. Although the surfers are here no matter what!

In regard to the pipes, they are actually storm water run off drains which means they are only used when we have an excess of water from rain. 

We're sorry that you were unable to find many restaurants with gluten free options, sometimes you just need some help to know where to look! Around the back of the library on Market lane are a couple good ones such as Verd, Banana Blossom, Momo Bar and more. We also have some more formal restaurants with gluten free, vegan and vegetarian options such as Garfish, Hugos and The Pantry.

We hope you visit again and have a better experience,
The Hello Manly Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi saveoursouls999,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the great review. So great to hear you enjoyed your time here. The ferry ride from the Sydney harbour is beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazingly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a short boat ride we arrived at Manly Beach. Don’t be fooled the arrival area is not the beach, you have to walk about a 1/3 of a mile to get to the amazing beach area. We walked up and down the boardwalk area in both directions, the sun was shining, but it wasn’t hot at all. It was perfect weather. We walked to Shelly Beach, which was not far at all. There was the cutest restaurant called the Boat House, the menu looked inviting, but we had already had breakfast elsewhere. This area is a must see when visiting Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely clean beach and plenty of facilities and harbour ferry os a must.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi  Dreamer53103662910,

We are happy you and your family enjoyed staying in our little paradise on Earth :)

If you ever come back to Manly please visit us at Hello Manly Visitor Information Center at the wharf for some invaluable tips about the area.

Thank you,

Hello Manly VIC's Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm and sunny time! Enjoyable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed our ferry to Manly beach. Even though it was bright and sunny the pleasant wind made the walk to the beach worthwhile. The small bistros and charming restaurants on way were so inviting ; difficult to resist .Beach was clean and safe with families enjoying time out. Near the ferry stop the tourism centre is super friendly ,ready to offer advice and support. Even gives a clean matter of fact map to walk around.The movenpik ice cream parlour serves yummy ice cream.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 837cherif

So glad you had an amazing time in Manly, one of the most popular beaches in Sydney. It sounds as though you chose a couple of our most popular eating places, I'm so glad both experiences were great! Manly has a large variety of shops to browse, ranging from popular surfbrand stores to exclusive boutiques.

Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ChenisaMiniThai,

We are happy you liked our little paradise on Earth :)

Make sure you visit us at Hello Manly Visitor Information Center at the wharf next time - we'll give you some invaluable tips about Manly and Northern Beaches area.

Thank you
Hello Manly Visitor Information Center

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Roadtrip to Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We've planed this road trip for a long time since we were too busy recently to went on a holiday. We rent an MPV from @EasyRentCars and drove to Manly. Stayed there for 2 nights. Had a great weekend with my wife and kids. Manly is the best place for a short getaway holiday near Sydney city. Warm sunshine and soft surfing. Kids love this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great area
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi leonardokirkg

Thanks for your 5* review of beautiful Manly Beach - it is true, you will always find someone in the water where it can be warmer than the air temperature and winter can bring great surf and water clarity!  You can also take a number of ferries from Circular Quay, the public ferry takes 30 minutes whilst the fast harbour cat only 18 minutes. Hope to see you again in Manly one day soon

Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Aussie Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi bevenh

Thanks for the very good tips and advice especially regarding swimming between the flags, the importance of which many people are unaware! If you are looking for a safe beach to swim at, Shelly beach is tucked away in the eastern corner, about 15 minutes walk along a beautiful coastal walk. It is protected from the swell and there are showers and changeroom facilities there as well.

Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi L H

Manly is certainly a very popular beach and easy to access, being a short 5 minute walk down the Corso. There are many different restaurants, cafes and pubs where it is possible to enjoy a variety of cusines  from Japanese noodles to fine dining. If you are feeling adventurous, there are many beaches further north which are accessible either by bus or on foot. Make sure you pop into the Manly Visitors Information Centre to have a chat to the friendly staff who can give you a map or local advice on where to go.
Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 7 miles from sydney & thousand miles to care.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Rusty W

Thanks for your great review - the ferry trip across from Circular Quay to Manly is a fantastic way to get to Manly in either 30 minutes with the public ferry or 18 mins on the fast harbour cat. The Corso is a wide treelined street/pedestrian area which takes you down to the beach in 5 minutes and then there is a beautiful 20 minute stroll along a coastal pathway to beautiful Shelly Beach.

Hope to see you back in Manly one day.
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly gone a little seedy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic trip over and back on the ferry Freshwaterfrom circular quay. Adele and I are both pensioners now so enjoy tripping around for two dollars fifty  a day on our public transport system.  Manly beach still a fantastic beach.The local eateries are now a bit over the top price wise.  How about one dozen oysters au naturale for forty eight dollars.   But they will sell you 4 oysters for sixteen dollars, a bargain, I think not. We gave the oysters a miss and settled for whoppers and chips from Hungry Jacks.  We did have excellent ice  creams from manly wharf, excellent and reasonably priced.Manly has now sprouted a proliferation of those seedy souvenir shops.   The ones we all love to hate, selling overpriced stuffed koalas and boomerangs made in China.I used to live in Narrabeen back in the late 60s early 70s.    We used to frequent the various  reasonably priced restaurants in the area, and enjoyed our 23 cent Schooners of Reschs at the Steyne Hotel.   Yes I know, inflation, but still it is a shock. Five dollars used to get you a good feed and 6 or more ice cold frosty scooies. Thats schooners or glasses of beer for people not from NSW.Tomorrow we are going to Sydney fish markets where we can have a good feed of prawns and oysters at a reasonable price.  Not the four dollars per oyster they charge in Manly.Roy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi gilly s

The Bluewater cafe is a great place for breakfast and very popular with the locals. So glad you found the beach clean and tidy, that is what we love to hear. The ferry is a great way to visit Manly, a 30 minute boat ride from Circular Quay on the public ferry, or if you are in a hurry, the harbour jet cat takes only 18 minutes.  We look forward to welcoming you back to Manly again one day.

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach even on an overcast day.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Bill291

So glad you had a fantastic visit to Manly - sometimes those overcast days can be very special, especially in winter when the waters are calm and there aren't so many people about. It is also a good time to hire a bike and venture up to North Head to take in the fantastic views of the City and the northern beaches. Maybe even spot a humpback or southern right whale on their migratory path.

Hope to see you back in Manly one day soon.
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Jandp768

Glad you enjoyed your visit to beautiful Manly beach. It is certainly good advice to watch out for the seagulls who are also very partial to free fish and chips! The ferry is a great way to visit Manly, no traffic or petrol fumes, just a beautiful scenic boat trip which can be taken in 30 minutes on the public ferry or if you are short of time, the fast ferry takes only 18 minutes. Next time you come to Manly, make sure to pop in to the Visitors Information Centre to grab your complimentary copy of the Manly map and the friendly staff will share some of the local's secret tips.

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have time, the ferry ride to Manly Beach is worth it. The ferry ride is nice and from the wharf it is a short walk to the beach along the Corso (directly across from the wharf). Passing several blocks of shops on the way, but the walk is nice. Once at the beach you are greeted with a clean beach walk and beach. The vastness of the pacific and the continuous  rolling waves coming to the nice sandy beach. The beach walk and the beach go both directions for a long ways and is nice to walk after putting your feet in the water. Lots of eateries along the beach walk area make this a nice afternoon trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Surfing Beach but Don't go during Bad Weather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I went to Manly when it was raining and grey, so we weren't able to experience its full glory. Despite this, there were numerous surfers out having a great time and I could tell the beach would a completely different experience if it had been warm out.Along with the beach, there is a great walking path and nature path that leads up to a fort. There are also plenty of little shops and restaurants to choose from, with prices ranging depending on what you feel like.The easiest way to get to Manly is by ferry from Circular Quay, but there is also a roundabout bus route.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a great walk!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Marytimich

So glad you had a great time at Manly Beach, we would definitely agree with the recommendation. The surfers can be very entertaining, especially when the swell is up. Next time you visit Manly, be sure to call past the Manly Visitors Info Centre for more information about all the activities, shops, restaurants etc which Manly has to offer.
Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sooooo Relaxing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife & I come to Sydney at least once a year for a long weekend & we always spend one day at Manly beach.From the moment you get off the ferry you feel relaxed and like your on a long holiday.A walk along the main drag to the beach is always interesting with such a diverse range of people doing their thing.Once you hit the beach you can sit in the sun on the steps and watch the world go by.There are water stations to fill your bottles and so much to see and enjoy.We always walk around to the right onto shelly beach to a little restaurant there called the Boathouse.It's one of our favs.Whilst walking along the path again you have so much to look at and people watch.When you get back onto the ferry back to Circular Quay you feel like you have been away for a week.If you're in Sydney for a short stay make Manly a priority.You won't regret it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach- can get to by public transit - long stretch
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi LL-CA-Nevada

Glad you enjoyed your stroll down the Corso and got to explore the back alleyways where some of the shops and restaurants are hidden. Manly Beach is easily reached by a 20 minute ferry ride from Circular Quay, Sydney - they run every half an hour until midnight so plenty of time to enjoy the village.
Thanks for your review.
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Shane Y

Thanks for your great review - we agree with you that Manly is a world-class beach and certainly the 20 min ride with the fast ferry or 30 mins with the public ferry is definitely the way to travel!  There are beautiful beaches are both the harbour and ocean side of Manly as well as several ocean pools. A great way to explore is to rent a bike at the Visitors Information Centre on your right as you exit the ferry terminal.
Hope to see you back here one day soon.
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Probably better when sunny
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi learningand diving

Such a shame you had to visit Manly on a rainy windy day (we don't actually suffer from too many of those!). That can be a good day to visit the local Art Gallery or settle down in one of the many cosy cafes. We hope that next time you visit us, you will be blessed with sunny skies and be able to see how wonderful the beaches are when the sun is shining!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely beach without the crowds and hype of Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Lissel A

Thanks for the great review - renting a bike from Hello Manly is certainly a fantastic way to explore Manly Beach as well as the North Head. The view from there is superb and it is great to jump in the water to cool off after a long bike ride. Winter/Spring time is certainly a great time to visit, less people and the restaurants/bars on the harbourside are an excellent location to watch the sun go down.
Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach close to shopping and great restaurants
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi NorthStar161904

You were very fortunate to be able to stay so close to Manly Beach. Winter/Spring time can actually be a very special time of year to visit Manly, fewer people around, clean waves, clear water and the chance of spotting a whale from the shores!

Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Becs_London_UK

Glad you enjoyed Manly Beach - such a special place to visit in the winter months when there are not as many people about! There are certainly many cafes and first class restaurants to visit, both on the high st (The Corso!) or tucked away in the back lanes. Be sure to try some of the great fish on offer to complement those chips!

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect wrap up
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the public ferry to Manly and it was a great way to wrap up our trip.  The ride over took less than 30 minutes and we sat and watched the beautiful views.  Once we arrived, we walked in/out of shops and ended up sitting on the beach and people watching.  We grabbed lunch and Ben & Jerry’s ice cream and made our way back to the ferry.  I would estimate we spent a little over 2 hours here.  The visit was nice and relaxing and exactly what we wanted.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferry to Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Yolande, 
We are glad you had a lovely day in Manly! 
You are right the views back to the harbour are beautiful! 

Hope to see you in Manly again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place for resting
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Somabolo, 
Thank you for the review! 
We are glad you enjoyed relaxing on the beach. 
Hope to see you back again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited Manley with a few friends on my recent visit to Sydney.  We caught one of the early fast ferry's from circular key at Sydney harbour direct to Manley Wharfe soaking up the views on route there.  When we arrived everyone seemd to head straight to the beach which was just a short walk straight across the road from the ferry terminal and along the main Street past lots of good clothes shops and quite a few restaurants and bars.  The beach is gorgeous with lovely clean soft sand...which reminds me of lots of carribean beaches I have visited.  What made it even better was the fact that it was winter there but still 23 degrees.  Well warm enough to lounge about on the beach for a few hours and soak up the sun.  We had breakfast in a lovely bar on the beachfront and the chef was actually from Birmingham and we had a good chat with him and he made us a great breakfast and then actually paid for us all a drink on him. thanks pal. We had a good walk up and down and had a drinks in a few of the bars.  As the sun was going down we went into a fish restaurant had lovely fish chips and mushy peas.  The fish was Hoki I belive from New Zealand...very nice white fish and very tasty.We all purchased a few aussie shirts and tee shirts and even a couple of jackets. We rounded the visit of nicely with a few more drinks in a nice bar next to the Ferry terminal and then caught the ferry back around 9.30pm.  I would recommend a visit here in fact I would love to holiday here and then catch the ferry in reverse to visit Sydney itself.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manley Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Heatherjeannette, 
Thanks for the review! 
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 

Glad  you enjoyed to walk along our beautiful beach with Golden sands :) 
Hope to see you again! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Age old weekender and holiday haunt
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Any excuse to go to Manly Beach, a place that brings back sweet childhood holiday memories for my children and I.  World famous, bit more low key than Bondi, probably only because it is not on the Eastern Suburbs.  Great natural beauty, you can go for a walk around to Shelley Beach afterwards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must do when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is one of our best beaches far better than Bondi in my opinion. We live on the other side of Sydney but often go to spend a weekend at Manly. It’s just like being on holidays beautiful beaches great restaurants shops and things to do. There is also Shelly beach and Manly wharf beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach and great walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi MichelleO1313, 
Thank you for the lovely review! 
We are glad you enjoyed your trip to Manly Beach! 
Hope to see you again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Mob Scene
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we went on a sunny winter Sunday when the R/T ferry fare was a$ 2.80 on the travel cardFerries were packed (pay the extra for the fast ferry) - town was packed and in our opinion, had little offer- very touristyMay be better during the week

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful day trip with visitors
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not only is the beach beautiful and full of activity, from board riders to body surfers, but there is a superb view of the coastline north and of numerous other beaches. Arrival by ferry from Circular Quay is dramatic and provides an excellent tour of the Harbour and views of the Heads.We walked across the narrow neck of land from the ferry to the sea and ate fish and chips watching the surf. There are rocks to climb and a wonderful walk around the bay to Fairy Bower.This excursion renews the spirit and is a perfect introduction to Australia's best beach for overseas visitors.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although it was  a rainy day when we went to Manly beach, it is a not to be missed beachThe fun begins with the ferry ride from Sydney harbour to Manly. The beach is a good ten minute walk through  beautiful road liked with shops.The walking trails Along the beach are very beautiful and scenic. We enjoyed our walks along the coast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nooo
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Alessia, 

Thank for taking the time to leave us a review! 
We are sorry you didn't enjoy your time in Manly. 
Hopefully you also took the time to walk over to Manly or Shelly Beach. 

Both are absolutely beautiful! 
Hope to see you again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Nicola, 
Thanks for taking the time to leave Manly Beach a review! 

We are glad you and your daughter enjoyed your time on the ferry and in Manly! 
Hope to see you again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to swim and relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi John M

Thanks for your great review - Manly Beach has recently been voted one of Sydney's top beaches on Trip Advisor. Make sure that when you visit you either swim between the flags or at Shelly Beach which is unpatrolled but very safe. There are a myriad of restaurants, cafes and pubs to visit and many different shops tucked away in back alleys and on the main route (the Corso) to the beach.
Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: eating fish & chips on the sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we got the ferry over to Manly which was a great ride...great way to see the harbour.  Walking down the mall to the beach was very touristy, but we got some nice fish & chips and went and sat on the beach in front of the water....we loved that...very casual...there are restaurants around, in case people want to sit down to eat

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can get to Manly on the regular ferry (using the same ticket as for the train) and one advantage is that this gives you views of the Harbour without having to go on a harbour tour. It's a fair trip to Manly, but you do find a seaside town that then faces out on to the ocean and has a feeling of being cut off from big city Sydney. The town itself is a little run-down (though I was there out of season) but the area around the beach is lively and I walked along the front to Shelly Beach and there was plenty of interest. I imagine that at the height of summer it would be packed.I underestimated how much I could do and see there and so it is the one place in Sydney that I wanted to go back to as I had not had enough time to explore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi petsiep,

Who doesn't love Manly? Beautiful place, beautiful people, amazing coffee and super yummy food.
We are happy you liked it! 

Make sure you visit us at Hello Manly Visitor Information Center at the wharf next time - we'll give you some invaluable tips about Manly and Northern Beaches area.

Thank you :)
Hello Manly Visitor Information Center

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice atmosphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, with a nice relaxed atmosphere. Surfers, young people with kids, elderly people, good mix. On the boulevard people are jogging, taking a relaxed walk. Personal trainers with sporters, yoga classes, or people just enjoying the sunshine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: On a fine and windless day, so much to 'sea' and do. On other days with a warm jacket, still lots to do and discover.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Cathie0411

Thanks for your very informative review of Manly! Hope you had a fantastic time discovering Manly and the many walks that are available. Next time you visit Manly, make sure you pop into our office located on the wharf as you exit the ferry terminal and collect a couple of maps detailing other walks that are available such as the Manly Scenic Walk to Spit Bridge and the North Head Walk! And don't forget to try out some of our delicious restaurants and cafes that are tucked away in back streets and on both the harbour and ocean sides.

Thanks
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful little beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 828leahw, 
Thanks for taking the time to leave us a review! 

We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 
Hope to see you again! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A stunning beach and MORE - The place is Electric
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take the Ferry from Circular Quay to get here, takes about half-hour.  After the short walk from the dock, the beach itself is amazing.  I came in August (middle of the winter right) but it was still fairly crowded (60F-70F temps) and surfers were still doing their thing, and lots of swimmers too (in wet suits sometime). I didn't come prepared for a beach, but that's ok because there were many concrete steps to sit at while watching the beach goers and surfers.  I can only imagine how crowded this place gets during their summer.There's more to do here than the beach, as the town is fun to walk around (very touristy) with kiosks/crafts, restaurants/food, souvenir shops, etc.  I also recommend the walk around the right side of the beach, nice walking/jogging trail and in 10 mins you'll hit Shelly Beach that you can see across the way as you walk.Would love to come back here in the warmer months and spend a few nights at Manly - fun youthful environment and a beautiful beach to center your time around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: make sure you go at the right time
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi pioletdefusta

Glad you discovered Shelly Beach, hidden at the end of a spectacular coastal walk. Manly can become crowded during the weekends but if you arrive on a weekday, you may be very surprised at the peaceful beach scene you will find and of course the cafes and restaurants will be quiet as well. You may miss out on the wonderful markets though which are held on the weekends in Sydney Road.
Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but packed !
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi C1086TIrichardb

Glad you enjoyed your trip to Manly which can be a very busy spot on the weekends. Next time you visit us, try to come during the week, you will be amazed how quiet it is although you will miss the very popular weekend markets held on Sydney Road.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Despite being out of season for a ‘beach day’ we were very keen to come here, I have been once before many years ago – however, the memory must be fading as I can’t recall the sand being as gorgeous as it was or is it now that I’ve been visiting beaches in Europe for so many years lately & having to put up with the relative mediocrity that seeing decent golden soft sand again seemed such a luxury. Despite the cold July day, it was encouraging to see surfers enjoying the waves as well as others swimming or messing about in the breakers (braver than I was feeling though) – Great Beach, Great Location & kept so lovely & clean too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like it more than Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Hobi01

Yes!! We do agree with you - Manly is a very beautiful beach with a unique village-like atmosphere, lots of interesting shops and boutiques tucked away in back lanes. If you are in a hurry, you can always take the private fast ferry which speeds along from Circular Quay to Manly in 18 minutes.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extensive walking path along the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is large and clean, with a very long walking path along the beach and up around a bend.  The area seemed very friendly to dogs.  Note that swimming is not recommended for 24 hrs after heavy rain, as drainage from the surrounding area dumps right in the middle of the beach.  When we visited, however, there had not been rain for about a week, and the water was clear.  We found that Manly beach was much less crowded, and the area and facilities cleaner, than Bondi beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi bmray,
Thanks for coming to Manly beach. Sounds like you had a lovely time. It's a shame you didn't bring your swim suits, although in desperate times we do have plenty of swim stores along the Corso. It sounds like you did the Manly to Spit walk which is very popular and beautiful. Next time maybe try out our North Head walk.

See you soon,
Manly Information Center

reviewsWithKeywords.title: top spot to take in the sun on a warm day
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi iprice5, 

Thanks for taking the time to write a review. 

We agree, it's barely winter over here! The beach is lovely and it is the best time to come to avoid tourists. 

We have a range of different restaurants and cafes; over 150! 

To end the day off getting a ferry ride back to the city is always lovely. 

Hope to see you soon, 
Hello Manly Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice evening walk watching the surfers
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
hi Cookstove

Glad you recently experience a fantastic evening with your family in Manly. The lifeguards would have finished their beach patrol which takes place during daylight hours and dusk is never a good time to be out in the water so you were wise to heed the signs. Fortunately the Cabbage Tree Bay Coastal Walk is one of the most beautiful walkways in Sydney so you don't need to go into the water to enjoy Manly and there are many restaurants and bars to sample some of Manly's fine food, wine or craft beer.
Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi travaller60

Glad you had a great day in Manly, the ferry is definitely a unique way to travel to Manly, especially on these amazing winter days we are experiencing right now! Opal cards can be purchased from most newsagents as well as machines placed on the wharves and an all day travel card is capped at $16.10 including ferries, buses and trains.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It has everything
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was tempting to write about each of the elements but that’ll take too much time. It has space for exercise, fantastic food and bar, markets, great beach and lots of great cafe like Roller.Beautiful scenery and a wonderful place to visit should plan on spending 3 hours here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Manly.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My favourite spot in Manly is the promenade walk which ends at Shelly Beach in Cabbage Tree Bay.  I think the lovely thing about Manly is that it's close to suburbia and within reach to everyone living on the northern beaches around Balgowlah, Fairlight and Manly.    The beaches and suburbs are as one and living there,  one would feel as if always on a holiday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Even in winter the beach is stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First visited it in 2003 when there for the Rugby World Cup in Spring, still an amazing beach and getting there by one of the fast ferries crossing the largest natural Harbour in the world enhances the visit. water was busy with surfers and bathers with plenty of space to accommodate both. Plenty of options to eat in or outside and temperature was 21 degrees even though it was winter

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach- great food
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the ferry to Manly and walked along the beach walk. Beautiful beach- kept clean and a pleasure to walk along. Lots of places to eat and ate in a great organic juice bar. Well worth a day trip when you are visiting Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly popular
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Tania,

We're so glad that you enjoyed your time in Manly. We take pride in our many shops, restaurants and especially our beautiful beach! Maybe next time you should try one of our gorgeous walks such as the North head or Spit walk. You can stop into Hello Manly to find out more about them. 
We hope to see you soon! 

Love, 
Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect Beach Spot for Families
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is much larger with more restaurants and shops than Bondi. There is a small coastal walk, not like by Bondi, but if you’re just looking for a beach day, I’d choose here over Bondi. Our boys dug in the sand and played in the surf all day. There is a small downtown pedestrian shopping area with plenty to see. The beach is clean with several life guards and flags marking the safe swimming areas. It’s much easier to access than Bondi as the ferry from the Rocks takes you straight here, no bus or transfers needed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beautiful place to spend a day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very easy to get to, which is important with my mobility issues. There are very nice, shaded benches to sit and admire the views. The boardwalk had a very nice selection of shops and eateries. We rode the ferry over, and what a beautiful ride that was....we came home with nice pictures of the Sydney Opera House and Sydney skyline.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice day for a walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited Manly Beach on in June, during the Sydney winter. The weather was comfortable—high 50s F—and would warm into the low 70s later in the day. I took the fast ferry to Manly—the farthest point of the harbor from downtown, out toward the ocean—for $18 AU round trip from Circle Quay, Only $2 more than the city ferry that takes 15 minutes more each way.When you walk out of the nice ferry hub and cross the street you enter a pedestrian mall with many types of shops. I stopped at a grocery for food, intending to each lunch at the beach. Great idea. Plenty of picnic tables available. Sat and ate while watching a small group of surfers trying to catch the small waves that day. Being winter, the beach wasn’t crowded, even though the water was fairly warm.There is a paved walking path all along the beach that leads up into and through the Sydney Harbor National Park. If you have 3-4 hrs, decent shoes, and are able to hike, I encourage you to make this trek. In addition to the flora and fauna, you can learn about the Quarantine station that was originally there—it would be similar to America’s Ellis Island, where immigrants would be off-loaded and held in quarantine until they proved healthy or died. The park—which includes North Head, with its fabulous views—was also a military base during the two world wars and a gunnery school.A great day at the beach and more.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Oh My God! Such a beautiful piece of Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi AngelaSandhuRealtor

So glad you loved the best beach in Australia!! Hope you didn't eat too much sand! Next time you visit our beautiful beachside village, make sure you call in at the Visitors Information Centre so we can give you some of the local tips on where to eat and drink!

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and great place to learn to surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had an amazing three day holiday here including surfing lessons at Manly Surf School (ask for Leon - a great instructor for beginners!). Absolutely beautiful water and the area has lots of restaurants and bars. Felt far nicer than Bondi Beach (less commercial). We also did the Spit to Manly walk - gorgeous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top beach - for an out of peak hours walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Sydney icon offers peace and quiet that is best enjoyed after the crowds have left. Better still pick a day that is wet and wild for a fantastic beach walk. Just do not dive in in those conditions.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Popular, fascinating, magnetic.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The ferry ride is a visual delight, the short isthmus of Manly is bright and busy shopping area and then the magnificent beach and ocean are revealed. Manly is always busy but it never seems overcrowded. It is well overseen by life guards and everyone has a battle with the surf - surfers are here but more for show I suspect.  It is good to follow the coast path - farther on south there are smaller beaches and you can also easily reach North Head for great views of the gap between headlands where harbour meets ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful place to visit on a sunny day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took two overseas visitors to Manly on the normal ferry and we took a walk around the the surfing beach and the beach where we got off the ferry.  It was a wonderful walk and was thoroughly enjoyed by my visitors.  We stopped and sat down on the seats by the foreshore before continuing our walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get there early to enjoy it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Steve and Amy,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for your awesome review :)

We totally agree - Manly is beautiful all year round! We are happy you enjoyed your time here. 

Next time you visit our little paradise make sure you pop into our information centre at the wharf  - we'll give you the best tips about Manly and the Northern Beaches area!

See you soon!

Much Manly Love

Hello Manly Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Weekend Out!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Tomas D

Yes you are so right!  The ferry is a fantastic trip across the Harbour to Manly and if you purchase an 
Opal Card, you can travel on all public transport at reduced rates. Manly has a variety of beaches to offer, the surf beaches of Manly, South Steyne and Queenscliff, or the quiet calm Shelly Beach, a 15 minute walk along a stunning coastal marine walk way. Make sure you pop into the Visitors Information Centre for a few of the local tips on where to eat on a budget!

Look forward to seeing you again one day soon.

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Sam M

Manly has much to offer to both children and adults, as well as the beach volley ball courts, there are several playgrounds for children to play in. There is also fantastic snorkelling throughout the year in Cabbage Tree Bay where the Manly to Shelly Beach swim takes place!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful visit - worth a half day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I probably would not have sought out Manly Beach for itself, had we not combined our visit here with a hike through North Head Sanctuary which gave us stunning views of the harbor and coast.  The beach was nice, but pretty crowded on a Tuesday lunch time in May.Our day started with North Head (easily accessible from the ferry terminal by bus) and we hiked down the Shelley Beach and then onto Manly.  The beach was nice to walk on for a bit, but again it was pretty crowded with a mix of tourists and locals.  We got some fish and chips at the fish market nearby which we enjoyed at a picnic table near the beach.  The corso was okay to walk down, and I'd love to come back and try some of the restaurants in Manly.All in all we spent about 4-5 hours in North Head Sanctuary and Manly and were back in the CBD by 2pm, allowing us time to hang out and do other things.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great atmosphere on a sunny winters day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just great to sit and watch the beach life, the wind was blowing strong so a cold wind but the surfers were out having fun, we had Fish & Chips (pricey) and walked to Shelley Headland with lots of ever changing views of the beach. The beach is a short walk from the Manly ferry pier, only 30 minutes from Circular Quay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very cool!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi photogirlwhotravels,
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly and Shelly Beach! 

You are right the snorkeling at  Shelly is amazing. It is super clear at the moment! 

Hopefully you come back again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is so beautiful and I would recommend visiting it if you go to Sydney. You can get the ferry from Sydney Harbour to Manly Beach. It is a short walk from the ferry port. The beach has beautiful soft sand and the sea is so blue and clear. There are plenty of shops and places to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MANLY BEACH.........EASY TO GET TO.........BEST IN SYDNEY !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hello Daf57,
Thanks for your great review!

 Here in Manly we all love Manly Beach just as much as you do!

As well as shopping, eating and fantastic views, there are also some stunning walks to try, such as the Manly Scenic Walk to Spit Bridge or the North Head Walk which includes idyllic Shelly Beach, the beautiful sandstone cliffs and views from them at North Head plus a small detour to historic Quarantine Station.

Pop in to visit us for more info at Hello Manly Visitor Information Center, outside the Manly wharf.

Best regards,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had Manly Beach on my places to go while in Sydney . I was so amazed by how clean this beach was that i did a small video clip to show my friends and family . the beach was the cleanest beach i have ever been too in my 60 years of living . no rubbish , no glass , no litter , no broken bottles or cans . And I watched a guy raking the beach for an hour . the sand even smelt clean . I could go on and on  but you need to go there to see this marvelous wonder for yourselves . Manly has a great ferry service  and great bus service once your there. lots of nice places to eat and great shopping as well .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cycling and walking
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Huzefac

So glad you loved your visit to Manly and enjoyed the walk up to North Head which can be spectacular in winter for many reasons: keeping warm, keeping fit, great views and the chance to sight a whale or two heading north!  Also a great place to cycle to as well, next time you come to Manly, make sure you pop into the Visitors Information Centre for some local tips!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect day out from Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi SuzannahA

Thanks for your 5* review of Manly - it is truly a wonderful place to relax, as they say "7 miles from Sydney and a 100 miles from care!!" The water is still warm, hovering around 19C - and there have been some fantastic waves to catch!

And the best way to get here is by the ferry of course!!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach..Soft sand and cool Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Kim,

Thank you for your beautiful review :)

Yes, for all the reasons you mentioned we all love our spectacular Manly Beach! Have you walked all the way to Shelly Beach as well? Or Freshwater Beach, past Queenscliff? 

Next time you visit make sure you do the North Head walk (impressive cliffs and nature) and pop into the Q Station (old Quarantine Station, where you can take an interesting history tour of the premises or a super scary ghost tour in the evening). 

And don't forget to pop into our Hello Manly info centre at the wharf - we'll give you great tips on what to see in Manly area and the Northern Beaches!

Much Manly Love

Hello Manly Team

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Spot -- Great Promenade
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We actually liked Manly more than Bondi.  Found the beach itself better with a lovely promenade.  Loads of fun people (and dog) watching.  Bath house was limited (no showers in the ladies) which is a minus -- but the beach itself makes up for this short-coming.  (Take the fast ferry to maximize the enjoyment for the day!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool vibes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach has a really cool and relaxed vibe to it. Feels almost disconnected from the busy hub of Sydney city itself. Great restaurants and cafes here as well. Love it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi txkate92

Thanks for your great review - here in Manly we all love Manly Beach just as much as you do - and as well as shopping, eating and fantastic views, there are also some stunning walks to try, such as the Manly Scenic Walk to Spit Bridge or the North Head Walk which includes idyllic Shelly Beach, the beautiful sandstone cliffs and views from them at North Head plus a small detour to historic Quarantine Station.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hostel city
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hello Cheesey Bugger,

So sorry to hear your visit to manly was not what you expected.

Inner harbor beaches rarely have waves, you will find the surf on the famous Manly Beach 5 minutes away in the opposite direction of the Wharf.

Come and see us outside Manly Wharf for great tips next time you visit.

Thank you,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of our iconic beaches and access to Sydney via ferry.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great beach with lots of interesting activities throughout the year from surfing to beach volleyball or just enjoy the coastal walks. Good shopping through the Corso and the regular markets then over to the ferries to explore the rest of Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi The Nomad 11

I hope you enjoyed watching the surfers - they love those days when the waves are pumping - glad you had a good time wandering around the markets where you can find gifts for friends overseas, many of which are produced by local artists. There is a huge variety of restaurants and cafes to try out - definitely come back soon and be sure to pop into the Visitors Information Centre where we can give you some of the local's insider tips on where to go!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Crowded during a Food and Wine Festival
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hello KimkX819SI,

Manly is loved by all, and yes, can get very busy especially during the Taste of Manly – Food, Wine and Sustainability festival.

It was on Saturday 25th and Sunday 26th May 2019 and it was our 33rd year of this successful festival. 

This festival is a celebration of wine, food and culture here in Manly, with all the best local restaurants showcasing their goods alongside some of the best regional and international wineries, beer and cider brewers.

Along with the mouth-watering food and drink there were also four stages set up with Live Entertainment, amusement rides for the kids, a sustainable hub and the Manly Market Place set up on Sydney Road.

We hope you will visit us again, maybe on week day when it is much quieter to experience our beautiful beaches and life style.

Please visit us, we are located outside Manly Wharf, for great tips.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach and enjoyable walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi glandsb500,

Thank you for the awesome review and so glad you enjoyed your time here. The ferry is a lovely way to get to Manly and the walk to Shelly Beach is beautiful.

Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family visit January 2019
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi sofia12june,

So glad you made it to Manly Beach and enjoyed our beautiful beach. Thank you for the great review. We hope to see you again on your next visit to Australia.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tranquil....
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Brownleys24,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the wonderful review. We love that you got the relaxed vibe on your visit to Manly. The ferry is a great way to get here and take in the Harbour sights on the way. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach is a real buzz
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Escape08412101809

Thanks for your review - you have hit the nail on the head! Manly beach has been voted No 1 Beach in Australia and it doesn't matter whether you are after a quiet moment on the beach or looking for a bit more action, "it is a wonderful place to visit"!

Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi marzup

Thanks for the great tip - many people neglect to stroll a little further towards Queenscliff where sometimes the waves are better! There are also some great restaurants located across from the beachfront a little off the beaten track.
Hope to see you back in Manly one day!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfing on Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ReneeRuggero

Manly has been voted No 1 Beach in Australia and we pride ourselves on keeping it as clean as possible. Surfing is a great way to enjoy the waves and the surf instructors in Manly have much experience with both beginners and accomplished surfers. So glad you had such a great time!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
hi sohler00

Thanks for your great review - a boat trip is by far the most scenic route to Manly and whilst Manly boasts several hills, there is also a wonderful coastal route that can be done on a bike with no gears!
The waters are still a mild 20C temperature and it is nearly always possible to find someone swimming, snorkelling, surfing or enjoying some other water activity all year round. The local residents truly believe they are some of the luckiest people in the world!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi sarabar123

Glad you enjoyed your visit to Manly and took advantage of all that Manly has to offer; beautiful beaches, spectacular walks and a huge variety of restaurants, bars and shops.
Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferry to Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Joanne74NZ

Thanks for your 5* rating of our beautiful beachside village called Manly. There certainly are many splendid walks incorporating the harbour as well as the Pacific ocean beaches. Make sure that if you visit Manly, you call in at the Manly Information Centre located on the right hand side as you exit the ferry and grab a few of the local maps.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A memory trip to Manly to complete our journey
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Roseteagardens

So glad you had a fantastic trip down memory oceans to the iconic Manly beach which remains beautiful, rain, hail or shine. Fish and chips is a great way to enjoy the seaside vibes and we have a variety of take-away or restaurant options.

Hope to see you back here one day!
Cheers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely day spent in manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi paraman97

Thanks for your first class review - Manly is certainly a great destination for either a day or a lifetime. The ferry takes you away from the hustle and bustle of the city to a quieter destination where you can relax in the sun or snorkel your way down to Shelly Beach. There are so many restaurants and be sure to check out Hello Manly's cheap eats guide on their website to discover the many winter specials and laneway delights!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand sea and sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Murray A

Thanks for your great review - Manly boasts a 1.5km beach with various spots to surf, swim or paddleski. The ferry ride is certainly a spectacular way to visit from the City. The food and wine festival is usually held in the middle of May so make sure to coincide your visit with this event and you will get to experience a variety of the different cuisines offered by the many restaurants in Manly.
best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come & visit earli during a weekday morning....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is one of he best beaches in Sydney. It is clean, generally the surf is safe and a nice walk from Queenscliff to Manly and Shelley Beach.Come during the week as its too crowded on weekends and try to come early to see the sunrise. There are lots of good cafes and even restaurants & pubs to eat at.A must if in Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Relaxing Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Kurtislee

Manly has recently been voted Australia's No 1 Beach - and we have two different coastlines: the harbour beaches which are safe for kayaking and exploring as well as the surf beaches for surfing and swimming. Both have great views and many different bars and restaurants with a huge variety of cuisines and price ranges.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Gabriel999

Thanks for your 5* review of beautiful Manly beach - the ferry is truly one of the most spectacular routes in the world! There is always something happening on the Corso, the gateway from the Ferry to the beach and no one is ever disappointed when they arrive there!  Make sure you venture further either west to Queenscliff or east to Shelly Beach.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good place for water lovers :)
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi 493srividyar

Manly is much favoured by water-lovers - with clean clear water, great waves, safe harbourside beaches, it's the perfect destinations. So glad you had a great time.

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Had to Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi ScottScooterW
Thanks for your great review of our coastal village of which we are very proud! The fast ferry is a great way to travel but if you are not in a hurry, be sure to try the traditional route on the green and yellow ferry. Manly is enjoyed by families from all walks of life, clean water, good waves and a great vibe. Glad you will return one day.
All the best

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Summers Day in May
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 26 Degrees in the sun, and could not stroll down the walkway  without stopping for a dip in the ocean. Swam with the locals for a good half hour and really enjoyed the medium sized waves of the surf, the warm sun, the salt and sand between my toes. It took me straight back to the days of my youth. After my half hour rejuvenating soak in the sea, we ventured off to our next happy place, across the road, Manly Novotel for a cool beverage. A great place to sit and people watch, have a cold beverage or two and still enjoy the sun and surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: All the Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Thomas V
Thanks for your excellent review which of course we agree with! Manly boasts one of the best beaches in Australia, with great waves, good snorkelling as well as a safe harbour for kayaking or paddle boarding. Hope to see you back here again one day!

Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice ferry trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I took the fast ferry to Manly on the recommendation of a resident of the town. It is a lovely beach town with a strip of a street dedicated to pedestrian traffic with shops on both sides. The beach area has a wide pathway for pedestrians and several restaurants across the street. It was a fun way to spend a little time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect location by the beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I stayed at the Sebel Manly Beach which was a great spot to be . A friendly comfortable hotel with very pleasant young staff,clean spacious rooms and served by the Manly Wine restaurant for superb breakfast of fresh fruit and yoghurt with comb honey plus a wide menu to suit all tastes. Handy to very good shopping area and a fun place to be.  Pleasant walk along the beach to other very good restaurants and cafes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi SusanMiss

Thank you for your great review of our beautiful seaside village of Manly, indeed, one of the best areas to visit. Next time you visit Manly, be sure to pop into the Visitors Information Centre on your right as you exit the ferry terminal and we can let you know some of the secret local's tips!
Best regards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning in our opinion it was well worth the short trip across. Lovely golden sand with restaurants overlooking it. manly is a lovely place visit seriously  recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely ambience
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Lawrence,

So glad you enjoyed your time in Manly. The ferry is a very relaxing way to get here and the Norfolk Pines along the beachfront are beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy and worth the visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Llewellyn53,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the great review. So great to hear you enjoyed your time here. The Norfolk Pines along the beachfront are beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunday hang outs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had friends over from France and we decided to go to Manly for a few hours.We all know it’s best to go to the beach when it’s a sunny and slightly more warmer day - but the day we went, it was pretty chilly and with some clouds.Nevertheless, Manly is a pretty beach - does remind me of Bondi but a lot more chilled.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Really Fun and Relaxing Area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to Manly Beach twice during my business trip to Sydney in April 2019.  I took the fast ferry from Circular Quay and walked on The Corso.  Manly Beach is a really fun and relaxing place.  There are many restaurants on Steyne Street which is near the beach.  I enjoyed sitting on a bench and watching the beach and people passing by.  It was very relaxing.  There were many people on the beach and many surfers.  There was an area full of people playing volleyball.  I also enjoyed the pathway which is parallel to the beach and ocean.  I have been now to both Manly Beach and Bondi Beach.  Bondi is a beautiful place with a famous hiking trail.  But Manly Beach is the place to go if you want to have fun and just relax.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most enjoyable beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was very clean and the waters inviting. Had a great time playing in the water along with kids. The sand on the beach is lovely and wants you to be there all day. It was buzzing with life and also had a small wedding taking place. But the place is so big for everyone that you can still find your place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is a very beautiful beach.  It‘s beautiful sands fill most of the bay.  Just accross the street are a number of coffee houses and small restaurants, along with shops and bars.  It’s a very nice beach town atmosphere and would recommend experiencing it to my family and friends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi SteveandVince,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the fabulous review. The ferry is a lovely relaxing way to get here and see Sydney Harbour on the way. So glad you enjoyed your time here and hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: fun at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Gary, 
We are so happy you enjoyed your time exploring Manly and you had a great time playing in the waves. 
Thanks for the awesome Review! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ok, But
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself was nice. But there was no place to sit except in the sand.  The waves that day were small, so not surfers.Went across the road to Manley Wines restaurant, food was awful, tasted of propane (the bar-b-que) service was not to say the least.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worthwhile
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There were 3 things I liked about Sydney: 1) the Waterfront, 2) Blue Mountains, and 3) Manly Beach.  Manly Beach has it all--a beautiful beach, a walking path to Shelly Beach (which is another beautiful beach!), and a sea coastal town.  The boat ride from Sydney's harbor to Manly Beach was great too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Irene, 
Thanks for the review! 
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best Beach, great location. Walking trails close by, food and bars are of abundance and is a lot more chilled than the eastern suburb beaches. More calming especially after jumping off a ferry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its a hidden gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It starts with a ferry ride, or a long way car journey. The boat takes you past the opera house, up close and personal, and all the bays along the way to the heads. Then you walk through the streets a short distance, past the gelato bars etc, then cross the beach front road and you're on the sand. It has sun and surf, the lifesavers are out looking out for bathers. Its got the pavillions and old style milk bars. A great place to have a swim and spend the day. You can stay overnight right at the beach if you want to. I was tempted.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Stephen
Thank you for the awesome review! 
We are proud of our beautiful beaches and we are glad you enjoyed your time here in Manly. 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can travel all around the world and then hefe in our backyard is the most lovely beach with excellent restaurants and such a magical atmosphere.  Buy and ice cream and some fish n chips and sit down and watch the serenity of this lovely area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: use the ferry to go to manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: to go to manly beach you can catch the bus from chatswood station or the ferry from circular quay.The Many beach has a good Place for Swimming and has excellent Hotel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love my day at manly beach, it is stunning to vist via the ferry from sydney.  the beach is long and beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent long stretch of beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Mark,
We are happy you enjoyed Manly and our beautiful Manly beach!
Next time pop into our Information Centre at the wharf and we will give you some great tips about the best walks and coffee shops in the area ;)

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manley beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Yes, the views of Sydney Harbour from the Manly ferry are definitely amazing! Did you know that our beautiful Manly beach has been voted the number 1 beach in Australia two years in a row? 

We are happy you enjoyed your time here and hope to see you back soon :) 

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take a ferry here!
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Yes, yes, yes! Manly is definitely a perfect place to admire the views on our beautiful Sydney Harbour! 
We hope you enjoyed the beaches as well: the impressive Manly beach, the cosy Shelly beach (perfect for snorkeling), the secluded Collins beach, the haunted Quarantine Beach and many more.
If not, make sure you come and visit us soon again!

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, Sand & Surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took a day out to Manly and what a fantastic day it was. Great town and a lovely promenade to stroll along and stop to watch all the surfing activity on the pristine beach. Had a coffee or three on the front and Fish & Chips for lunch. Took the harbour City Ferry from Circular key which took 30 minutes and cost $15.oo return. One of the highlights of my stay in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Beatrice,
You are so right! Our beautiful Manly beach is the best place to relax and connect with nature while having a nice coffee or lunch. Have you walked to Shelly Beach? It's only 20 minutes from the Manly wharf on the way to North Head - another amazing place to visit. Maybe you will feel like exploring it next time?

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a stopover.
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Fathimad,
You had a very good idea with hiring bikes - it is a great way of visiting Manly! You can ride along the beach side or/and explore North Head: beautiful views and exercise all in one. Our Manly ferry is iconic to us - we are happy you enjoyed the ride :)
Make sure you visit our information center at the wharf next time you're in Manly! We promise to give you some great tips on how to best explore the area.

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must-do!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A trip to Sydney is not complete without getting the ferry to Manly from Circular Quay!When you arrive and get off the ferry, head up through the main  pedestrianised street towards the ocean and the beach.It’s a very chilled beach in my opinion. Tree lined and plenty of room to sit and enjoy the views and the sea.Lifeguards patrol the beach and watch the swimmers swimming between the flags.Plenty of places to get food and drink or take a picnic!
