On the far side of the Corso from Manly Wharf, this beach has a long stretch of sand with a row of pine trees stretching out along the foreshore. There is a surf club there and the beach is patrolled by surf lifesavers as well as lifeguards. The waves are generally well formed here and the beach is great for people of all ages. Bluebottles can be a hazard here from time to time, but I've only been stung here once in all the years that I have come here. There are plenty of cafes and take away places around here. Be careful if you decide to get hot chips as the seagulls are very aggressive and will happily snatch food from right out of your hand!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place in the pacific
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very nice to see all the surfers in Manly beach. It was like in the movies! Also there is a nice walk to other beach. Locals are very easygoing and they would tell you more about the curiosity about the place if you talk to them

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A fun little beach town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited with the family. It’s nice to see how Sydneysiders cut loose. Nice high street between ferry and the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quite impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even if you are not a swimmer, you will enjoy seeing Manly Beach.  Today we watched as dozens of children were taking surfing lessons, we walked along the beach to Shelly Beach and came back to do more people watching and sight seeing along the beach.  It is a beautiful site and there is lots of room to accomodate even those like us, who do not dare tackle the waves.To get to the beach, ride the ferry to Manly and then walk straight up the pedestrian walkway (ask for directions at the Info Centre if needed).  The beach is right there within 5 mins of the ferry terminal.  You will shuckle as you see the many youth walking around with their surf boards.The beach is lovely and is surrounded by all sorts of eating establishments.  A great way to spend a summer day in Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to surf (or even to just watch)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A popular place yet the beach is so long that it's never crowded. Just chill out wandering along the promenade watching those of a more energetic nature out in the surf. Pretty There's not just the beach though, the town area is pretty with lots of little coffee outlets too. Use the Manly Fast Ferry from Circular Quay to get there in around 20mins or use the Captain Cook HOHO Ferry for a more leisurely trip which visits a couple of places on the way yet still only takes 40-45mins.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like the beech this is the place to come too manly has an old feel to it but modern excellent walks along the front loads of cafes and restaurants only wish we had more time to enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The ferry trip from Circular Quay is always lovely and a great way to see some of the harbour, but the crowds on a Sunday can be huge. It's difficult to get into a restaurant and it certainly isn't one of Sydney's best beaches, but it is worth a visit if you are in Sydney and have a few hours to spare.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded and touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a Sunday so the beach was expectedly crowded. We made our way to the Shelly beach which was easy walk. The pubs and bars near the beach was not cheap but those along the manly wharf was more varied. Good experience to experience the feel of a busy beach thronged with tourists and locals

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place for surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly has a lot to give, beaches(Manly, Shelly, Fairlight beaches are the best) Manly and Shelly beaches a bit busier then the Fairlight beach. If you like surfing and playing with waves Manly beach is the best.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach and town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had been recommended to visit Manly beach by many people and glad we made the trip. You can get fast ferries there from multiple places in Sydney and harbour for under 10$. From the ferry dock it's only 5 mins walk along a good shopping street to the beach. The beach is clean and well maintained with good facilities inc showers. It's a lovely area with lots of good restaurants along front and attractive views and walks.Forget Bondai beach this is miles better. Beaches covered by lifeguards too and hire shops for surfboards etc inc lockers at good prices.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Sydney in my opinion – Manly Beach has it all!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is located in a perfect position, 1 min. walk from the Corso, 5-10 min. walk from the Wharf and a short ferry ride from Sydney CBD. The waves are great, the atmosphere is so friendly and warm – people help each other out and keep an eye out for each other's stuff at the beach. Here's everything your beach-heart could wish for. Good for families, couples and friends. Laid back feeling in the afternoon, hardcore swim-workouts in the morning. Would recommend this beach over Bondi – this is where you go to feel that relaxing and soothing beach recreation and surf fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach I have seen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is a surf beach, very safe for swimming or surfing, nice golden sand and picture perfect.This is a must see if your traveling from overseas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not so crowded like Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Due to the missing train line is Manly beach not so packed by backpackers.It offers pretty good surf, however very crowded any time and season. Manly is pretty windy and covered showers, changing rooms and toilet are insufficient. However Manly has the right vibe and plenty shops and walks around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Drunken Party Area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately our recent visit has seen it turn into an area of drunken yobs and depravity. There was many groups of drunken youths that appeared to have an issue with the proper use of the English language swearing at every opportunity whilst families with young children where in their vicinity. On top of this there was a lot of litter around the place. The sand and sea was good but then it is natural. The beauty of this area has been spoiled by commercialism and the clientele. Will not be visiting again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely  beautiful beaches great walks along beach front easy accesd for disabled and elderley to wander along lots of seating to rest at

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the ferry over and walked around the little town and visited the beautiful beach. I also ha lunch on the waterfront and had a delightful fish and chips lunch. Wellworth the visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hey Cloney!
Sunset drinks on the harbour at Manly Cove, and a starlight ferry ride home....What a day, and what a way to enjoy Manly! 
Much more that just a sunny beach side destination.
Next time, book a hotel and stay for the weekend! You'll fund much more to explore...

Much Manly Love

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take a Ferry to Manly Beach and Corso
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hey Scott!
Sure is easier! Ferries galore - take you door to door from Circular Quay to Manly. What a way to ride!

Our super funky markets run every Saturday and Sunday (unless it's raining or super windy), just off The Corso.

Add in 150 bars and restaurants, plus 200 stores to explore.... 40 different walks, beaches and activities, and you've discovered our own little piece of paradise!

See you again (we hope).

Much Manly Love!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It may have been a dull day weatherwise But......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth the 30 minutes journey by ferry from circular quay, and then to find that it was a 5 minute direct stroll from the port to the beach, no one could lost trust me  just walk off the ferry and continue walking in a straight line. You pass some wonderful little shops, but remember to look up at the architecture of some of the buildings it is not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favorite beaches!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take an easy ferry ride from Circular Quay to Manly and you will experiences one of the best beaches in the world. A pedestrian walkway, lined w/ shops and restaurants, takes you from the Manley ferry docks right to the beach, and you can walk along the beach or the boardwalk. The sun is intense (November) so plan accordingly. Water fountains along the path let you fill your water bottle.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Use your Opel card on the public ferry to Manly Beach and shops.what a great day out.great atmosphere,stunning beach.And great to walk along.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While it does not have the whaouh factor bondi beach gives, it is a lovely spot, somehow less busy.The surrounding area offers cool shopping and drinking spot.I found the ferry ride from circular quay so amazing that I would  recommend, if only for the boat!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 1st experience in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a few missteps on obtaining our ferry ticket 🤦🏻‍♂️, we made it Manly Beach. Weather was awesome and caught a sunset in the way back. Definitely hit up The Fish Shack and Yogurtland on the way back if staying on the mainland. Great spot to enjoy food on the beach and chill. Also has a cool walking path along the Pacific Ocean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relax place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 30 mins boat from Circular Quay. Amazing n beautiful beach. Many shop around with bar and food restaurants. Cool worth to go .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful long beach. Not as pretty as Bondi but still worth a visit. It does however have the advantage of having sun loungers to rent.Note Manly beach is not the one by the wharf but a short walk through the centre which is lined with shops and cafes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to be missed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If want to get away from the crowds in Sydney jump on a fast ferry and 20 minutes later you’re in the beautiful manly. Fantastic walks with breathtaking views. All with a very relaxing atmosphere.. walk to cabbage tree bay about 30 minutes walk from the centre and you’ll see the blue water dragons lazing in the sun on the rocks.. plenty of little cafes and bars.. if I could give this place more stars I would..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: can have a fun day at this stop, have a lot of cafes near by and barbeque facility. washrrom and toilets as well

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry to Manly. It was a Sunday so there were many people there. There are plenty of life guards around so it's very safe. when we went the water was super cold though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it! What a lovely place. Get here by ferry out of Sydney harbour. Reasonably priced, cheaper if you use opal card. 20 mins trip. Lovely 10 min walk down to main beach 🏖. Beautiful sand and rolling waves. Watch all surfers and competitions going on. Lovely walks up and down the sea front. Walk around to little beach and up onto top for cliff top walk...lovely. Great coffee shops, bars, restaurants, lots going on. Nightlife too.  Good food. Friendly and lovely atmospheres.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun atmosphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a pleasant ferry ride it is only 200 metres to the beach where lots of people having fun surfing, walking, eating, cruising. You can walk along the seafront, either way, a km or two. Plenty of places to eat, have coffee or a drink. Relatively sheltered from southerly winds which may be cool elsewhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We travel to Manly, several times a year as we love the feel of the place. Beautiful surfing beach, great cafes & shopping. We always stay at either Novotel or The Sebel & are happy with both, especially the Sebel. Easy walk to catch the ferry if you want to go over to Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a half day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even if I do a weekend trip to sydney I will squeeze in time to hop on the ferry to Manly Beach. The ferry ride is fabulous u get great views of the bridge and the oph for photo ops. The beach is bigger and more beautiful than bondi and plenty  of shops and markets to explore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach not so crawdy with a lot of facilities.There is a pool further and an other beach great also where yiu can do snorkeling -> Shelly beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach!  Clear water and not overcrowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love Manly Beach!  better than Bondi Beach...  more laid back.  Great weekend market.  Clean sea water and white sand :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Oh Manly The Only!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rode the SpeedFerry from Sydney to Manly Harbor and enjoyed every minute of it on the way. Manly was all welcoming the moment we stepped on the wharf, till we returned. It was a Saturday eve so the mood among tourists was livelier than usual, and the Whitney Houston’s songs blaring through loudspeakers made the already happy moods happier. Loved the walk from Harbor onto the beach, and alongside the embankment. It's almost like committing a sin if you visit Manly beach but don't try Fish & Chips. Thank god we didn't fall into sinners category. The views are stunning, stroll a blessing, environment grandeur, and the sunset just breathtaking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We ❤️ Manly.The ferry drops you off in a great location and we walked along the Corso to the beach. WOW!We could’ve stayed right there forever, not too busy at this time and there were families, couples, groups of people all doing their own thing, having a real cool time.There are some great looking pie shops and restaurants in the area we were in and the architecture was awesome, a real mixture of new and old.Love this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice ferry ride to this place takes about 30mins and great view's,beach itself tidy plenty of eating places in area a veriety of prices, good clear water and well life guarded,but just like most beaches it depends what you want😎👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my first trip to Manly. Getting across from the city was so easy and nice on the Manly ferry with beautiful views of North Head. The beaches are just beautiful. Heaps of places to swim and the beaches are well patrolled. We had a swim at Shelly Beach and Collins Flat, both were fabulous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved the scenery and expanse of beach and shops.  Easy and inexpensive to get to by ferry--very scenic ferry ride.  Prices are better than Sydney and Bondi Beach. Ate at Guzman Y Gomez just outside of the ferry wharf--good burritos.  Happy to finally find Mexican fast food as we were yearning for some during 9 day stay in Sydney. Great walk through The Corso and see many shops, walk on the beach, watched volleyball games, had beverage at great place on the patio on way back to ferry--Manly Wharf Hotel.  And be careful of the candy kiosk in the ferry wharf--yummy goodies !!!!  ENJOY !!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach can walk around to smaller beaches . Lots of bars cafes and restaurants in the area. Easy to get to from circular Quay on the ferry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great surfing beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very good surfing beaches, packed full of people and easier to get to than Bondi beach in my view. Life guards everywhere to keep you safe on the main beach, but there are lots of little beaches and rocky areas where you can get out to swim. Unfortunately we saw someone drowned in one of the smaller beaches but it was packed full with people so enough people around to notice something went wrong. So please stay mindful. Otherwise surrounding Manly beach there are a dozen other walkways and paths to stroll. You can spend all day here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly has a selection of beaches, one for great waves if you’re a keen surfer or Shelley beach which is part of a marine reserve where it’s possible to snorkel and see the marine life below.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly beach is a must do as it is so easy to get to now. This was my first visit and I will definitely go back again when I am in Sydney.Fast ferry's now get you to Manly beach in only 20 mins.  When you go to Circular Quay you can either pay at the ticket office at each entrance or use your Opal card now. It only costs $9.10 one way.When you get off the ferry, it is only a walk of 5 mins straight ahead once you get off the ferry to enjoy the sand in your toes.Go for a long walk, take your shoes off  and enjoy the sand and surf. If your hungry there are shops on the beachfront too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply beautiful & ideal for a morning run
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For me this is the best of the big beaches in and around Sydney, granted I'm not a local but to run from Manly Creek down to Shelly Creek which is beautiful too and back is wonderful...It's busy on and off the beach itself with so many folks enjoying the great outdoors

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hey Odyssey!
Shame - If its a sunny day, Manly sure can be popular!
The best public transport options, are the ferry's... which connect to bus and train lines throughout Sydney.
There are 4 different services running continuously all day:
The classic Manly ferry, green and gold from Circular Quay
The Manly Fast Ferry, offering the same service, but ten minutes quicker (with beers on-board all day)
The Eco Hopper, which moves around Sydney Harbour.
The Barangaroo ferry, from Darling Harbour area direct to Manly.
Sundays is all day travel on public transport for a super low, maximum fee of $2.70!!
Hope to see you again... with a smooth journey!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ferry to Manley
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must do whilst In Sydney Buzzing mall with tourists everywhere Well worth the trip Great place Iconic beach and it’s exciting Great pubs with history Plenty of shopping for those that love the sport whilst for those who seek experience and adventurous to fill the soul this is good too Great walking opportunities

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wonderful beach indeed👌😀
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take your picnic and relax and take in this breathtaking beach. We opted for fish and chips before walking along the headland. A wonderful day indeed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take City Manly Ferry to beach, a half or day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hop on the famous Manly Ferry and in 30 minutes you are over in Manly. A more relaxed and typical Australian seaside town, easy to reach if you have no car, and want a leisurely boat ride over.Some buskers usually around, some clever kids and remarkable skills, playing,singing what we could never do!Plenty cafes, but stay off the main shopping area from the ferry to the beach, as its a bit run down, and not much unique there. Walk to the beach in about 7 minutes from ferry, and go left or right and find a cafe or eatery along there. Less expensive than Sydney, makes a perfect half day or day out.Relaxed, and kept well, it is truly something very special when visiting Sydney.Don't worry if if it is windy, cloudy, the ferry just gets choppy and many people get drenched with salt water, and it is even more fun!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful day outing especially on a Sunday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Manly Beach yesterday. It was a fabulous day. Using your Opal card, you can travel anywhere on the Sydney bus, train and ferry system for only $2.50 on a Sunday. This includes nonresidents.Manly Beach is a beautiful spot, even if the weather is cloudy. The ferry ride is about a half hour. When you exit from the ferry go to the information booth for information and a map.  This is the major tourist destination and also a residential area. There were dozens of stores, restaurants and tourist facilities. Stroll along the beach and take one of the paths up into the hills where you will be able to see some fortifications from the second world war. Try the ice cream at Royal Copenhagen near the beach (or better yet, the waffle bowl with three scoops, actual melted chocolate and unlimited almonds and sprinkles toppings at no extra charge) — enough for two. We had lunch at The Boathouse restaurant before heading up into the hills. We saw numerous arts and crafts kiosks as well as fresh fruits and organic vegetables.  A ferry leaves from cap circular Quay Every 30 minutes on the half hour and hour. Likewise at the island for the departure is every half hour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: different from Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach and area is more peaceful then Bondi. Many shops and restaurants located in this area and around the beach. The Manly ferry from Circular Quay is awesome and a must do. we had hired a car, so drove around and all the way up the hill for even better views down to water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and peaceful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to relax and to forget about the bustle please go to Manly beach. I like it much more than Bondi beach. Here is the atmosphere of relax and joy. Here is a very beautiful nature and peaceful people. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My Local Beach, Great Surf, Crystal Clear Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great stretch of surf beach from South Steyne to North Steyne. Beautiful and clear, great surf. Great for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyable visit, however I wouldn’t go again at the weekend, as it was extremely busy, and restaurants very full.  Totally different on the Monday, even though the weather was still perfect, it was so much quieter, I felt our day was wasted there on the Sunday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Family Friendly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a family friendly beach. Swim between the flags and you are ok. Other areas for boogie and surfboard riders, Also surfboard riding school there,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: DO NOT EAT NEAR THE BIRDS!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we packed a picnic lunch and a bird LITERALLY flew up behind me and grabbed my sandwich from my hands!!...HOLY CRAP!!...Never had that happen before....They're totally aggressive!!..BE CAREFUL! Other then that...beautiful shops and beach..had a great day!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A trip to the quieter side
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a day in bustling Sydney, we were very relaxed riding in the ferry over to Manly Beach.  The fast ferry takes about 15 minutes.  When you arrive at Manly Beach, you find yourself immersed in a completely different world.  The small town is charming in itself.  The beach walk is absolutely gorgeous.  If you enjoy hiking, you’ll love the beach nature trail at Manly Beach.  It’s a great place for the family to visit, and there are stores where you can shop while heading down to the beach from the ferry.  They have plenty of places to eat, including fast food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, nice area, beautiful boardwalk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry to visit.  Lots of shops and restaurants, and we took a beautiful stroll on the boardwalk up to Shelly beach.  Beautiful sceneries and homes as well as quiet places.  Worth the visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I took the ferry from Darling harbour to Manley and spent several hours walking the beach path.  Wonderful views and well maintained footpath.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a ferry over for the afternoon and picked up lunch at the beach.  Lots of places to buy food and drinks right along the street by the beach.  The ferry ride was also a nice way to see the water side of syndey.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So beautiful, clean and white beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: take the ferry from Cirkular Quey to Manly, evary half hour, enjoy the day there either shopping or swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with plenty to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived on the ferry form Sydney I’d recommend getting the faster boat lovey beach with plenty of surfing going on also plenty of shops and nice markets and sales at the weekend defo worth s venture out from Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney must do !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This trip was arranged  by one of our Australian  friends. I am really pleased he did take us there. Manly beach is amazing  with one of the most diverse  coastal walks you could do in a short period  of time. From beach front, to rugged  protected shore line, houses  perched  on stilts above the path, little gift shops and cafes. Wonderful walk all the way to Shelly Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Atlantic Ocean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked all along Manly beach front and out to Shelly beach. The waves were rolling in and there were surfers to watch. We found sun traps despite the showery weather and watched the waves and surfers and the rescue boat. The sand is so fine and both beaches were reasonably clean. We particularly liked the little sculptures in the rocks close to Shelly beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean sand and clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take the ferry to Manly, as you get a beautiful view of the coast and of Sydney harbour. The beach itself is lovely, but as far as beaches go, it’s not breathtaking or anything. But still a great spot! And there’s a Ben and Jerry’s ice cream shop right on the beachfront for a cool snack. :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly seven miles from sydney and a thousand miles from care
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is a great escape from Sydney city with beautiful beaches and a famous marine reserve at Cabbagetree Bay.  After dark the local nightlife is stifled by aggreive bouncers and ahigh police presence which combines with high drink prices and expensive accomodation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach in Springtime
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walkjng along the Corso onto the beach and admiring the surf was beautiful. Admittedly, the waves were driven by the weather and swell at the time, but the sound of them crashing in and watching a few surfers  was blissful. Dont know what its like in summer, but on a cool dreary spring day it brightened our spirits and made our day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach always clean. Very busy lots of locals and tourists. Nice family beach, close to shops and cafes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Much better than bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a rainy day and it was still lovely. Longer, whiter, more organised for kids/adult activities. Well done all!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Aussies can be weird
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to Manly because I wanted an excuse to take a ferry somewhere. It was a lovely day, so I had lunch at a restaurant with a sunny deck. Because I was the only one eating on the deck, I left a tip. The waitress took umbrage, called me names and threw the tip at me. I threw it back at her and left.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely worth stopping at the beach if you are in Manly. There are loads of eateries just across the road, Park equipment for the kids and footpath so you can stroll taking in the views without getting sandy feet. Nice to just sit and watch the gentle waves rolling in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunny.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After several days of rain and cloud the sun finally came out so we took our chance and got the ferry over th Manly.Wasn't disappointed, long beach with lovely fine sand. Very clean beach.It's a Shame 90% of the beach is closed off to swimmers just so the surfers can have fun. Lots of eating places overlook the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly beach is a long stretch of beach located north of Sydney, it offer plenty of restaurants along the coast and a wonderful view over the pacific ocean where surfing is a common practice by locals and tourists. A beautiful gem in Sydney surroundings!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: just a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: nice trip there by ferry, but disappointing area....mall with so many closed shops looked rundown, rubbish all around, takeaway meals at ridiculous prices, beach closed because of dangerous currents and then blue bottles washing up, (but we know that canso, 't be helped) just a beach, and nothing special or memorable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking Tour of Manly Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Manly Beach was an easy walk from the ferry terminal.  Enjoyed lunch on the waterfront and the walk to the protected cove.  Easy half-day trip from Sydney Harbor.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful setting!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth its reputation! Lovely walk on the path with lots of places to stop and take a few pictures. There’s even a pool that’s quite uniquely shaped right at the beach. You can watch people surfing, Kayaking or paddleboarding. Lots of restaurants and little stores.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches in Sydney, if not the best. Its well maintained, its beautiful and and has awesome surf. Life guards patrol the beach to keep everyone safe. Stroll along the board walk around to Shelly beach. You'll also find numerous places (beach side) to grab a bite to eat or enjoy a beer. Perfect for just about anyone, including the family. Check it out if you can...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Day in a Wonderful Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely spot this is. A visit to Manly is a must for tourists who visit SYDNEY. Great shops, wonderful restaurants and magnificent scenery. The beaches are terrific, both the surf (ocean side) and the harbour side (for those who prefer calmer water). Beautiful walks along paved tree line streets. Public transport consists of either ferry or bus. Both drop you at Manly wharf ... ‘the gateway to Manly’. People of friendly .. a great mix of locals and tourists, both young and old. You won’t be disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect beach for a day in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is definitely worth the visit. You can go there by taking the ferry from the Sydney Harbour (30 min) and then enjoy a beautiful beach, clean, with a lot of people during warm days.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: my favorite beach in Sydney, much more family friendly than the city beaches. Very clean and pristine. Good waves on certain days but a great place to take the kids for the day. Take the ferry if you can.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Away from the city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to this side of the city on a ferry boat, which is a fun ride itself! Beach had a jazz festival going on, Manly Jazz, huge and thrilling! Plenty bars and restaurants with many ATMs around. Beach is clean and well staffed. A lot of things to do here. Also, ferry is the best way to see Opera house from the sea! :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic place to enjoy the waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi patrolman_pete,
You're right, Manly isn't just a beach. We're a community where all are welcome. 
We have many different cuisines and cafes, as well as breathtaking views. 
It's family-friendly and very accessible, with just a 30 minute ferry ride from the city.
Next time, go on one of our many walks to see a new side of Manly.
Much love,
Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a couple of days here over a weekend it was a very nice place we stated at a hotel right across from the beach.There was a good choice of restaurants vlose by and easy to get around.It was much nicer than the heart of sydney and felt a lot more laid back and friendly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with lots to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Manly Beach on a lovely spring day by ferry. The fast ferry was a joy in itself as you get to see the harbour and Manly is a vibrant little place with great bars and restaurants. The beach was clean and well staffed with lifeguards and plenty of showers and toilets. Manly is well worth a visit for those of all ages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to spend a day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I spent the day at Manly Beach. The beach is clean and large and there is a lot of restaurants and shopping close by. I had a great time walking through the shopping area. Definitely recommend making the trip from Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Strong waves and lots of seagulls
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is a direct 30 minutes (approx) ferry ride from Circular Quay Wharf 3 to Manly Wharf. A smaller beach compared to Bondi Beach but the waves seem stronger (on the day I was there) which makes it good for surfing. The nearby Corso has plenty of shops, F&B options and a supermarket (Coles).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hey Rick,
We're proud to say Manly Beach came first in the Travelers Choice Best Beach Award.
Our beach is filled with fun activities such as swimming and volleyball 24/7. 
Manly has almost every cuisine you can think of, as well as pubs and cafes!
Visit soon!
Much love,
Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pet friendly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the nicest beaches in Sydney. Its dog friendly while they are on leashes and everyone is just so happy and friendly. The restaurant on the beach has amazing fish and chips too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Aussie Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Some time ago I lived in the area, whether you’re a local or a visitor... this is a spectacular place.There are oodles of restaurants and bars nearby. Personally I think this place is better than Bondi. There’s plenty of shaded picnic tables for families too. There is a paved walking path between Manly and Shelley Beach... absolutely stunning and also accessible for wheelchairs. Walk is suitable for any fitness level. Would recommend catching a ferry from Circular Quay (Sydney city). The ferry is a beautiful experience in its self. Parking is extremely limited meaning it has very limited time restrictions for locals running errands or reserved for disabled parking. The ferry which back in the city is linked to the train system is so lovely, it doesn’t make sense to try and drive unless you have to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peaceful getaway from city life
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach should be on your must visit list when you go to Sydney. It's half an hour away from the circular quay by ferry and song 50 mins from darling harbour by ferry. So in case you are living around these harbours, take half a day off to see the beach. There are many cafes and pubs so you won't be short of choices. There's a walkway to connect two beaches which is most used by many joggers so you can take a walk along that and enjoy the view. In case you have come in a group , there are some volleyball net setup at the beach which you can use to play.There were also many friendly cockatoos in the park along the beach so we spent the time playing with them.There are many local and branded markets along the walk to the harbour so while going or coming to beach you can enjoy that and collect some souvenirs. In all this do make sure that you return by 7pm as the last ferry to Darling harbour leaves by around 7.15pm. otherwise there are many ferrys to circular quay till 11pm and in case you are from darling harbour then  it would be around 20 min walk to Darling harbour from circular quay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No sharks trust me
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hey scottshlad09,
Thanks for coming to Manly.
We can assure you there's no sharks. The last fatal shark attack was in 1936.
We have many cuisines to offer as well as pubs and cafes.
Visit soon!
Much love,
Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect way to spend the day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and ferry ride.  Fun to walk the corsco and wander through the streets.  Would make it a point to encourage all travelers to check out this lovely area.  Reminded me of where I grew up...manahattan beach ca.  Their nippers are our Jr lifeguards and many many volleyball games in play.  Water was cold but many donned wetsuits and enjoyed the water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MUST GOT TO MANLY BEACH!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly Beach is a must go to when visiting Manly. One of the best places to visit and attraction site. Manly Beach is easily accessible with a short 30 minute Ferry ride from Sydney’s Circular Quay, followed by a casual stroll along the Manly Corso. The staff at Hello Manly Information Center recommended some cool hidden lane-ways for some healthy bites. Banana Blossom was an awesome find! I got the Tokyo Classic, which I highly recommend and close to Manly Beach. If you haven’t been to Manly beach, check it out, it’s a great destination for both locals and visitors which has great coastal vibe and beach front views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chilling out😊
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I've been to Manly beach several times but today is special because my granddaughter is with me, my first grandchild. Manly Beach is a tourist spot. If only I'm a surfer, I will surely love to stay here. I love their boutiques, stores, restaurants, hotels....name it😊. Friendly people most specially.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Average beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is nice enough but did not find the rest of the area to be worth the detour. There are nice cafés and restaurants and some shopping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MANLY BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can catch the ferry from Circular Quay and admire the scenery getting there you get to see the Harbour Bridge and the Opera House. When you reach Manly Wharf there is a great little bar called Hugo's you can stop in there for a nice meal and cocktail. You can walk along the Manly promenade as you reach Manly beach. The view is breathtaking along the beach. You can walk along the beach and you can see the surfers  surfing. Manly is well known for surfing. As you walk along the promenade you come a cross a little beach called Shelly Beach that has little shops along the way and a nice little bar, You can go scuba divng on this little beach. A lot of nice little restaurants on the promenade. So many to choose from. Worth a trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had heard lots of things about Manly but have never been there until today when we took the fast ferry.  What a lovely place.  You get off the ferry and take the road straight ahead of you to get to the beach.  Once you get to the beach walk along to the right and keep going until you come to Shelly Beach it is a lovely coastal walk with lots of interesting things to see and of course the big expanse of sea where there are surfers and body boarders.  You can continue on further but we stopped and turned back once we had climbed up to the top.  It is well worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would recommend taking the ferry to Manly, it is a thoroughly enjoyable trip on the water.  From the wharf you can walk up through the main strip of shops and eateries to Manly Beach at the other end.  We sat on the beach in the beautiful sunshine and enjoyed the world passing by.  There are plenty of options for dining and we found a great coffee shop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Oz trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: great beach, easily reached by ferry from circular quay. we took the fast Manly Ferry, a 10 minute walk from the jetty down the main street gets you  to the beach. Golden sand and surf, but the water was chilly. Lots of people enjoying a sunny Sunday afternoon

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Robert,
We're glad you enjoyed the ferry ride. It really is lovely, especially during sunset.
We pride ourselves on our clean and beautiful beach.
Visit soon!
Much love,
Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi Steve P and thank you for visiting Manly Beach, Sydney Australia. We love that you enjoyed Manly more than Bondi! Manly is beautiful with a relaxed vibe and was voted Australia's No.1 Beach on TripAdvisor earlier this year. There is always something going on with an activity for everyone. Hope to see you again soon. Much love, Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great family beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi Mike B and thank you so much for visiting Manly Beach, Sydney Australia. Yes! Manly Beach is a fabulous beach with a lovely relaxed vibe and it really is wonderful for kids. Shelly Beach and Little Manly Cove are sheltered beaches with no waves and perfect for kids to paddle around. Hope to see you again soon. Much love, Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi Pee b and thank you so much for your awesome review! So glad you loved Manly as much as we do. Did you know that Manly was voted Australia's No.1 Beach on TripAdvisor? With over 150 cafes, bars and restaurants you are spoilt for choice with something for everyone. Hope to see you again soon. Much love, Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well known Sydney beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi JaredYSyd and thank you for visiting Manly Beach, Sydney Australia. Yes! Manly is always buzzing with an activity for everyone and we are so glad you enjoyed your time here. Definately a wise move leaving the car behind and catching the ferry, it's a beautiful way to get here and enjoy the harbour sights on the way. Hope to see you soon. Much lovely, Manly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Much to see and do, casual and upscale both
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Manly is a relatively small and quiet suburb with its own excellent beach.  It has charming shops stores and restaurants, and most of it is nice and clean.  The area around the wharf can be a little tacky.  We have visited several times, and have occasionally seen the area overrun by partiers that were rather intoxicated and obnoxious, but this is infrequent. Late weekend nights would be the time to avoid.Restaurants run from very casual to rather upscale, just like the stores.  The Corso is a fun area to all and shop for all ages.  Unless you decide to walk up to see the Castle on the Hill at the ICMS most of the town is fairly flat and the easy to navigate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I took visitor from overseas, caught ferry from circular quay, it was beautiful day , bought fish and chip, ate near the beach. We walked along the shops (souvenir, chemist, take away food, ice cream, cafe etc) from the ferry wharf to the beach. there is playground for kids to play.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fascinating
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Maryam H and thank you for visiting Manly Beach, Sydney Australia!
All of your suggestions are great, there is an activity for everyone in Manly. From Shopping, hiking, swimming and surfing we have you covered!
Next time you visit why not explore North Head Sanctuary?!
Hope to see you again soon,
Much Manly Love.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text:
Hi Anthony H and and thank you for visiting Manly Beach!
we are so glad that you decide to visit us for the day on your holiday!
Yes! Manly has over 150 bars, restaurants and cafes so your spoilt for choice here.
Next time try our Manly to Spit scenic walk and explore more of what Manly has to offer.
Hope you visit again soon,
Much Manly love.

reviews.title: Favority Australia Location
reviews.text: Fabulous area and place to visit.  Made my top destination after our month long journey through Australia and New Zealand. Would return in a heart beat!  Do walk the various trails and visit the local beaches.   Lots of top places to eat and drink.

reviews.title: Lovely Beach
reviews.text: Great beach, nice to walk along the promenade and there are loads of shops restaurants and pubsEasy to get to via Ferry from Circular Quay

reviews.title: Beautiful walk and a nice trail/walkway
reviews.text: It was such a nice walk and trail.  We wandered for about 6 miles.  The sites were lovely, lots of people milling about but not crowded.  Manly beach was bigger than I thought and quite nice.  We birded the whole way and found many cool birds along the way.

reviews.title: Manly Beach via passenger ferry from Circular Quay
reviews.text: Took the passenger ferry from Circular Quay area (near the Opera House) for a quick 45 minute ride to the Manly Beach wharf area, which is conveniently located walking distance from the town and beach area.  The ferries are frequent and huge, accommodating hundreds of people both commuters, locals, and tourists alike. The beach at Manly beach is a short walk from the ferry stop, and there are lots of stores, restaurants, and bars along the way, along with street musicians.The beach is lively, and there is a nice paved walkway along the beach passing by hills, cliffs, and multi-million dollar homes.A nice siop for a brewski, burger and people watching is the pub at the historic Steve Hotel, which sits along the beach area and is a fun place to relax for a cold one or lunch.We spent the day at Manly Beach as tourists and loved it!  We took the ferry back, and timed it so it was early evening, offering stuffing views of the Sydney Harbor Bridge and Opera House.  Highly recommended by us1

reviews.title: Visit to Manly beach by ferry from Circular Quay in Sydney
reviews.text: On our next-to-the-last day in Australia, advised of temperatures reaching 105 F, we decided to visit Manly, where the harbor and ocean beaches are only two blocks apart, so that it is a major center for surfing and surfers' culture in New South Wales. We took the public ferry from Circular Quay and the fast ferry back. The town was lovely, and exceedingly tourist-friendly, and there were some very interesting architectural gems along the main street between the two beaches. The ocean beach was closed due to a recent shark sighting, but both beaches were a beautiful sight to see. Don't miss Manly when you visit the Sydney area!

reviews.title: Good beach
reviews.text: This is a good place to visit with family or friends, you can just chill out or play in the waves as they are not too strong, very fun

reviews.title: Best Beach for dining and ocena experiences
reviews.text: Fantastic beach with up to 200 shops and restaurants nearby. It si best to arrive here - away from the weekends - by Uber or public transpiration. The beach umbrella/beach chair rentals are surprisingly affordable ($10 AUD per day) and worth every penny. The sand is perfect and the water is clear (no seaweed), but do pay attention to daily restrictions on swimming areas because riptides are a real danger. Also, be sure to walk to the far north end of the beach to explore the "Manly Wormhole" -  a natural tunnel between the Manly Beach cliff area and the next beach to the north.Finish the day if you like with a 15-minute ferry boat ride ($9 AUD) over to downtown Sydney for great views of the Sydney Opera House at Circular Quay.

reviews.title: Classic suburb and beach
reviews.text: A visit to Sydney is not really complete if you have not visited Manly with its beaches and promenade along the water and from/to the ferry. Nice restaurants, pubs, hotels and so on so go there.

reviews.title: Wonderful as ever
reviews.text: The first ever surfing competition in the world was held here at Manley Ocean Beach. The 2 kilometer wide and open sandy beach is lined with tall pine trees, which is quite unique. At sunrise, with some people walking about and the sound of the waves, it's soporific. During jam-packed weekends, it's a great place for people-watching. If you're going to bring food here, just make sure the hungry seagulls don't grab your food first. We visit Manley Beach every time we visit Sydney. The 20-minute ferry from Circular Quay is inexpensive and wonderful. It affords you great views of the Opera House and the Sydney Bridge and much much more!

reviews.title: Lovely Mandy beach. Use the ferry and bus lines
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and walk through Mandly. Use the ferry; you see the opera and the bridge perfectly, only for 5 or 6 euros (on exchange).If you go for a few days, a different card per person is required to pay for the ferry. Economy price, but identify the passenger by associating them with their card.On the ferry you only have to cancel at the entrance.The bus in the city works very well, but there it is mandatory to cancel it on the way in and out. Starting at a maximum daily amount, you are no longer charged, even if you continue to use it. Example: a 333 circular line journey from Brisbane street to the end of the line at the jetties, 0.60 euros.

reviews.title: ***Ocean breeze. Sunlight. Pure comfort at Manly Beach Guesthouse***
reviews.text: Manly Beach Guesthouse sits in a unique corner location where you can enjoy the refreshing ocean breeze from one of Manly Beach's most beautiful spots. Every room is newly upgraded with high-quality, ultra-comfortable beds and mattresses to ensure a perfect night's sleep. Natural light fills the entire property - every room and space has its own windows, creating a bight, airy and welcoming atmosphere. Cleanliness and comfort are our top priorities, and guests consistently appreciate the fresh, spotless environment.

reviews.title: Cute costal town
reviews.text: Manly Beach is absolutely a must-visit when in Sydney. The moment you step off the ferry, you’re greeted with that classic Aussie coastal vibe—relaxed, friendly, and full of energy. The beach itself is stunning, with wide golden sand, rolling waves, and plenty of space to stretch out, swim, or surf.

reviews.title: A nice outing!
reviews.text: It’s a 40 minute ferry ride from circular quay to Manley .. we walked on the Main Street to the end of the road which takes you to the waterfront and the beach . Lots of shops and restaurants on the way .. once you are at the beach .. you find nice sand and swimming + surfing opportunities.. or just sit back and admire the views of the ocean .. restaurants + pubs along the boardwalk are found .

reviews.title: Lovely vibes here
reviews.text: Well worth a visit as it has a lovely feel there. The lay out is simple but effective with a beautiful high street full of charm leads to a most beautiful beach with golden sand.It’s a magic formula

reviews.title: Surf surf surf baby
reviews.text: One of Sydney’s iconic beaches it was great to visit it during our recent stay. Gee it was busy around both the beach and town area. But that didn’t stop me from venturing in for a little swim and a play in the waves. The waves are huge and I was knocked over twice but that’s part of the fun right. Whilst we sat on the beach we witnessed a surf rescue. Those guys are superb at what they do.

reviews.title: Manly beach
reviews.text:
Hi Graceob1,

Thank you for sharing your experience. We’re thrilled to hear you enjoyed the ferry ride, stunning views, and the shops at Manly. It’s great to know you found the beach a must visit while in Sydney, and we hope to welcome you back soon.

Kind regards 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: worth a look but winter not ideal
reviews.text:
Hi Yukiarashi,

Thank you for your review! It’s lovely to hear you enjoyed the shops, food, and the well-kept beach. We hope you’ll have the chance to visit again to experience Manly during the warmer months.

Kind Regards 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Iconic beach lived up to expectations
reviews.text: Manly is one of those iconic beaches around the world and it lived up to its reputation when we visited. Sand for ever, plenty of sun (even is Aussie winter when we visited), plenty of people enjoying the water. A short ferry ride from Circular Quay in Sydney Harbour,  Manly is really easy to access. Once you have disembarked from the ferry, it's a short walk across to the beach. On this walk you will find plenty of options for food and drinks, from takeaway to sit down meals. There are plenty of shops too, and better than I expected. Not just the usual touristy stuff, but shops still serving the local community too. The beach itself is gorgeous... long, clean and stunning.  Plenty of 'friendly' gulls so be careful with your chips if walking along. It really is one of those places that you wish you could spend more time at

reviews.title: Excellent beach to visit whilst in Sydney
reviews.text:
Hi Karzanhughes,

Thankyou so much for taking the time to leave a review.  We're glad you enjoyed the scenic ferry ride, passing the Opera House and Harbour Bridge really does make for a memorable start to a day in Manly. The beach offers so much to enjoy, whether you're looking to swim, surf, relax, or explore. We’d love to see you back again next time you're in Sydney.

Kind regards 

Manly Visitors Information Centre

reviews.title: Sunrise Vibes & Coastal Adventures in Manly
reviews.text: Manly Beach is absolutely magical at sunrise.Stretching wide and long, it offers plenty of space, even on busy weekends you can usually find a quiet spot further up the beach away from the crowds. Most visitors arriving by ferry head straight down the Corso to the main oceanfront, unaware that Manly is home to 14 other ocean and harbourside beaches waiting to be checked outBeyond the beaches, Manly boasts a vibrant selection of cafes, bars, and restaurants to suit every taste possible. For something truly special, take the scenic walk around to Shelly Beach via Fairy Bower. Its a awesome spot to snorkel and it’s a local favourite for good reason. And if you're feeling adventurous, the bushwalks around North Head offer breathtaking views of the city and a dose of nature right on the edge of the city.

reviews.title: A very beautiful place where you can find peace and quiet I will repeat it again as soon as possible I recommend it
reviews.text:
Hi 994marcoantoniol,

Thank you for your kind review! We’re so happy to hear you had such a wonderful time and found the place peaceful and beautiful. It’s lovely to know it left such a positive impression on you. We hope to see you again soon!

Thank you again for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Manly is a MUST stay
reviews.text:
Hi David B,

We really appreciate your thoughtful review. Manly is a beautiful place to stay, and it’s great to hear that you made the most of your visit—from the diverse beach options and excellent snorkeling to the scenic walks and lively weekend markets. The short ferry ride from Sydney certainly adds to its charm. We're so pleased you had a memorable experience and hope to welcome you back again soon.
Thank you again.

Kind regards 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Manly Over Bondi - Beach, Rainforests, and Natural Swimming Pools, Oh My!
reviews.text:
Hi inspiruption, 

Thank you so much for your lovely review. We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed your day in Manly and had the chance to experience its many highlights—from the scenic nature walks and natural rock pools to the beautiful architecture. Thank you again

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: The best beach ever!
reviews.text:
Hi ClarkeyFamily,

Thank you so much for your kind review. It sounds like you had a truly memorable six weeks in beautiful Manly with your family! We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed your stay and found plenty of activities to keep everyone entertained. We’d love to welcome you back again in the future.

Thank you again for taking the time to write a review. 

Manly Visitors Information Centre

reviews.title: Dreaming in Blue: The Allure of Manly Beach
reviews.text:
Hi kerry b

What an amazing testament to the attraction of Manly - that you would love to live here. And we would love to have you if ever that came to pass. We happily welcome all-comers, whether as a short-term visitor or as a permanent move.

We live here, and everyday we still marvel at the beauty of the place.

We'd love to welcome you back soon.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Ferry to Manly Beach
reviews.text: The ferry ride itself is short but scenic, offering beautiful views of the harbor. Once we arrived, we found plenty of great eateries and shops to explore. The beach was clean, relaxing, and perfect for a leisurely stroll or just soaking in the coastal vibes.Manly has a laid-back, fun atmosphere that makes it a must-visit while in Sydney. I highly recommend making time for this little getaway across the wateryou won’t regret it!

reviews.title: Do the Spit Bridge Walk to Manly
reviews.text: Someone had told us to take the ferry from CBD to Manly. However, instead we did the Spit Bridge Walk to Manly, a gorgeous 10 kilometer walk along the North Harbour, and we were very glad we did. The views are spectacular.To get to the trailhead at Spit Bridge, we took a bus from Wynyard station. We weren't sure how to get from the Spit Bridge bus stop to the trailhead because there was no signage, so we just followed some other people who looked like hikers.After walking around Manley, we had lunch at Garfish, which was very quiet and a step up from the fish-and-chips eateries elsewhere.Then we took the ferry from Manley Wharf back to Circular Quay.You can Google how to do this walk, since I'm told I can't post links here.

reviews.title: Excellent Beach, but not on a cold July day
reviews.text: Just a short walk from the Manly wharf where you get off the ferry. Manly beach is a sweeping curve of sand almost tropical.july is not the best time for beach visiting in Australia. only a few hardy individuals were in the water.However it is still a great beach. There are lots of varying places to get something to eat and drink, just back from the beach. Also not far to walk to the shopping area of Corso.

reviews.title: One of my all time favourite city beaches in the world !
reviews.text:
Hi Freewunderlust,

Thank you for your thoughtful and detailed review. You've beautifully captured the spirit of Manly and highlighted the range of experiences on offer. We truly appreciate your kind words and look forward to welcoming you back again soon.

Thank you again.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Scenic
reviews.text:
Hi lucycan

You've pointed out one of the great things about Manly - the beach is basically part of the village, both in proximity as well as culturally.

As the host of the first World Surfing Championship in 1964, surfing and swimming is in Manly's DNA.

Emerge from the water, wander across the sand and find yourself in the heart of downtown Manly, with it's shops, cafes, restaurants and pubs. It's convenient, it's fun and most of all it's so very Australian. 

Thank you for the review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: nice nice nice
reviews.text:
Hi francescoc501

While there's no commercial fishing going on in Manly, there is certainly a lot of fish and chips.

Grab some takeaway and set up at the beachfront for an alfresco lunch with a view, or take a table in one of the many restaurants and cafes that also serve up this popular fried fare, from fine dining establishments to casual eateries.

Thank you for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Ferry to Manly Recommended
reviews.text:
Hi grascots

The ferry ride is certainly a highlight on a day trip to Manly.

Once here, the beautiful views continue, whether beach-side over stunning Manly Beach and pretty little Shelly Beach, or from the clifftop at North Head's stunning Fairfax Walk or on the lovely Manly Scenic Walkway.

Thank you for your review.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: A famous spot to visit and well worthwhile
reviews.text:
Hi Z587YQ

Thank you for your review.

Manly is the perfect day trip from the city, making it extremely popular among visitor's to Sydney and locals who live in our surrounding suburbs.

You're right to recommend sunscreen, especially during the hot months when the UV index is at it's peak.

We also have plenty of shaded areas along our beaches thanks to our beautiful Norfolk Island pine trees, meaning you can still enjoy this area while staying cool and limiting sun exposure.

Please come again. 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Very Pretty Beach
reviews.text:
Hi luvtravel88

Thanks for the review.

While we're sorry you didn't enjoy the Manly village area, we're pleased Manly Beach made up for it.

It's a lovely long stretch of sand and surf broken up into three areas - South Steyne (at the end of the Corso), North Steyne and Queenscliff - each with its own lifesaving club and lifesavers.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Beach sunset
reviews.text:
Hi Umar T

So nice of you to give our beach such a great 5-star review.

It does turn on the charm, particularly on a blue sky day when the water is clear and warm.

The waterside walk around to Shelly Beach is a must-do, while the beachside dining at the Boathouse is as close as you'll get to picnicking on the sand.

Thank you

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Best beach for wave lovers. Manly is generally worth a visit.
reviews.text:
Hi 261gens

Thanks for your review.

It sounds like you had a great time here in Manly and enjoyed the most prominent of our many beaches, that being Manly Cove as well as world-famous Manly Beach.

Fun fact - we actually have 8 beaches here in Manly, with some tucked away in the national park but just as stunning as our glamourous namesake.

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Great waves when we went!
reviews.text:
Hi CaesarBrutus

While it's a shame you couldn't swim on the day you visited, the best thing about those big surf days is watching the incredible waves as they roll through and the surfers brave and talented enough to take them on.

Sit and admire their talents from Manly beachfront, and then wander around to Shelly Beach and up onto the headland to look down onto the more extreme breaks named Deadmans and Winkipop.

There are many beautiful swimming days as well, so please come back and see us next time - with time to let your swimmers dry :)

 Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Dive
reviews.text:
Hi 909rafailm,

Thank you so much for your kind words! Manly Beach truly a spectacular destination, and we’re delighted to hear that you had such a fantastic experience. We look forward to welcoming you back again soon.

Thank you again
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Great day trip to beach
reviews.text:
Hi familyoffour50

Thanks for the review.

As you rightly point out, while there are many Northern Beaches tours to join from the city - from motorcycle experiences to plane trips - it's very easy and quick to simply go it alone and catch the beautifully scenic Manly Ferry across the harbour for the perfect day trip to Manly and beyond.

We're glad you enjoyed our beaches - we have so many there's something for everyone. Choose from surfing and swimming in the waves at famous Manly Beach, hiring a SUP at Manly Cove or exploring underwater with snorkel and goggles at Shelly Beach.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Nice beach 🏖️
reviews.text:
Hi Rog G

While buzzing with energy much of the time, Manly Beach also exudes a casual Aussie coastal vibe; different to the more 'city' flavour of Bondi.

Many people come to Manly as the perfect day trip from the city, accessed via one of the most scenic harbour crossings in the world and taking only about 20 minutes from the CBD.

Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Relaxing beaches minutes away using the ferry
reviews.text:
Hi PourJF

Thanks for the great advice regarding how to pay for our public transport and the requirement for one credit card per person.

If this is not possible, Opal Cards are widely available from outlets located around the city.

Both credit cards and Opal Card have the same benefits, with daily and weekly maximums applied to travel costs.

Regards
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: A day at manly beach
reviews.text: What a stunning beach, clean sands, lifeguards on hand, plenty of eateries near the beach front and some really nice shops a short walk from the beach. There was a market on in the main shopping area with lots of stalls offering all kinds of things including local arts and crafts.Don’t worry if you have no towel or sunshade as these can be rented on the beach at very reasonable prices.We got the ferry from darling harbour, inky takes about 20mins so you get to see more stunning scenic views.

reviews.title: full and clean
reviews.text:
Hi Pavolc434
Visitors to Sydney are spoilt for choice when it comes to famous beaches, with Bondi on one side of the harbour and Manly on the other.
We're so pleased you decided to travel to Manly, regularly voted among the top beaches in the world.
It's not only beautiful, it's also very versatile, catering to most water pursuits from high-energy surfing through to relaxed sea swimming, gentle paddling, and underwater snorkelling adventures.

Thank you for your review

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach and Town.
reviews.text:
Hi Tammye89
We're glad you discovered Manly as the perfect day trip from the Sydney CBD, being only a 20-minute ferry ride across one of the most scenic harbours in the world.
Cafes and restaurants abound, the pace is relaxed and beachy, and the beautiful blue ocean beckons.
Thank you for your review
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Beautiful Manly Beach
reviews.text: Manly beach is definitely worth a day trip from Sydney. Only 20 minutes away by ferry, the view ont he way to Manly is already worth the trip. Once in Manly strolling down the Corso is really cool. Plenty of shops and restaurants in the area, either on the wharf, the Corso or the streets around it. Beautiful beaches all around Manly, my favourite Manly Beach for its beautiful sand, its location close to the Corso and the quality of the water. If you go for more than a day, I suggest doing the Spit bridge to Manly walk. Its a wonderful walk on the coast with lots of scenic views and beautiful beaches.

reviews.title: Amazing place!
reviews.text: We enjoyed 10 beautiful days in Manly! The weather was delightful.We stayed five days in a VRBO that was right off the Corso (shopping plaza that doesn't allow cars)and five days in Manly Pacific hotel facing the ocean. Both were clean, quiet and near the beach, restaurants, and shopping!  We enjoyed happy hour on the rooftop of the Styne hotel, many desserts at Yo-Chi, every breakfast at the Pacific  Manley, dinner with an ocean view at The Pantry Restaurant and the shopping on the Corso!  There was a street fair on Saturday and we purchased several souvenirs from local artists to bring home. We walked to Sandy Beach, did the hike from Shelly Beach to Spit and went to the Taranga zoo! We found Manley Beach to be a great spot to stay and use as a home base and explore the area. We did a day trip to the Blue Mountains via the train and hired a guide to hike the Grand Canyon. We went to the Fish Market and the Aquarium. It was easy to catch the ferry to Sydney Harbor and Circulare Quay (20 minute ferry ride) to visit the Sydney Opera House and Barangaroo. Two weeks in Sydney and a lifetime of memories!

It also has a delightful little village centre with a range of shops, some of the best walking trails in Sydney and an interesting and visible history ranging from our First Nations heritage through to quarantine and wartime challenges, surfing glory and Olympic success stories.

Manly also stands as the Gateway to the Northern Beaches, providing a launch pad to further adventures along our 32km stretch of peninsula.

Thanks and hope to see you again

Manly is definitely a year-round destination.

reviews.title: During my first visit to Sydney - took a ferry out to Manly for a lovely morning at the beach
reviews.text: While visiting Sydney for the first time, decided to take the Manly Ferry to Manly on an early Sunday (to beat the afternoon crowds) on a nice sunny day.  The ferry ride was nice and relaxing. Upon arriving at the Manly Wharf, I just followed the crowds that were heading to the beach.  The beach was pretty nice, especially with the crescent moon coastline and the tall pine trees along the beach.  There is a walking trail that runs along the beach for a nice walk.  There are several shops and restaurants between the wharf and the beach, so plenty of things to do.  If traveling to Sydney for first time, I would recommend a ferry ride over to Manly, it was about 20 minutes on the fast ferry.

reviews.title: Easy beach trip from Sydney  for snorkeling.
reviews.text: We took the Manly Ferry from Circular Quay for a 30 minute trip through the harbor to Manly Beach. When we arrived, we stopped by the information station, where we got very helpful suggestions and directions, including the best places to snorkel. A short walk across the island took us to the beach. We looked for umbrellas or chairs for rent, but did not see any. There was about 1 - 2 meter surf and many surfers. We walked some more to Shelly Beach for snorkeling.  There was a little surge and visibility was 2-3 meters. Water was about 18 Celsius, so we wore wetsuits. We saw many fish including blue groupers, wrasses and several other types. There is an ID board at the beach for the different species.  There is not much shade but a few places to sit or picnic. A rinsing area is near the path back to Manly Beach. We had dinner at Wahlburgers and took the ferry back to Sydney. It was a beautiful beach day during our stop in Sydney.

reviews.title: Great beach walk
reviews.text: My friend's son who has been residing in Australia for the past 10 years, strongly recommended that we visit this beach attraction while in Sydney. I was initially undecided whether to go to Bondi Beach or this Manly Beach.But Manly Beach was easy and more direct to travel from our apartment at Kings Cross. On our very first day in Sydney  we had already purchased an Opal card with a top up value of $50/-.  We can have unlimited rides once we clock $17/- spent rides and we could use the Opal card on trains as well as ferry. From Kings Cross station, we took the train to Circular Quay and took the ferry at one of the wharves terminal direct to Manly Beach. The journey is about 22 minutes. It was a smooth cruise ride.  Once we reached our destination, I sought advice from the Manly Visitors' Information booth on the way to the beach and the attractions. It was highly recommended to take the walk along the beachfront from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach or visit the village center for some shopping and food.Instead of heading to the beach  the ladies in our group were attracted by a shop 'Reduce  Reuse and Restore' selling second hand clothing. The garment were very fashionable and stylish though they were second hand. One of the ladies bought a jean for only 10 bucks. I was fascinated by the Manly War Memorial erected in front of the rows of shops. A salute to the ANZAC soldiers who perished during the two world wars.While the ladies in our group were still engrossed in their window shopping, I decided to take a stroll along the beach from Manly Beach to Shelly Beach. It was an awesome walk and it reminded me of the long stretch of the bathing beaches in Xiamen. Manly Beach was crowded but the walk along the beach walkway was relaxing and meditative as my ears were tuned to the splashing rhythm of the waves and my eyes staring at the long horizon of the blue ocean. As I approached Cabbage Tree Bay and Shelly Beach,  I could see young picnickers playing or lying near the beach enjoying the sunbath. It is school holidays and many came here for their vacation.There were monitor lizards appearing here and there but there were signages that warn visitors from touching these water dragons.At the end of Shelly Beach, I walked up the stairs to the Bower Street and was amazed by the picturesque seaview and the cliff edge at the entrance of Sydney Harbour National Park.Great beach. No wonder it was voted by TripAdvisor as the Best among the best beaches in 2023.

reviews.title: Manly North Head Sanctuary Hike
reviews.text: Having been to Sydney many times before, I thought it was time I ventured out of the CBD this time and so I visited Manly. I’m not that much of a beachgoer, so it was great there were hiking trails available that I could do on my day trip there.Getting to Manly was incredibly easy; the Manly Ferry from Circular Quay is quite regular with the ride taking about 30min and costs less than $10 one-way on the Opal Card (and you don’t need to touch off at Manly). Note, there is also the Manly Fast Ferry which I believe is a bit more expensive and I don’t think the ride to Manly is that much faster than the normal ferry.There are toilets onboard the ferry, otherwise there is one at Manly Wharf. Head towards the wharf exit and then on your right side look for a sign that says “Carpark Toilets”. You can take the lift down but the stairs are faster. The toilets are cleanish a bit like those I would expect at the beach. If you’re along The Corso shops (the main shopping area in Manly) there is also another set of toilets opposite the Fishmongers Manly restaurant.I started off at The Corso and made my way down to Manly Beach, going clockwise. Many stops were made during my almost 3hr hike including Cabbage Tree Bay, Shelly Beach, then following the Shelly Beach to Barracks Precinct Walk path, visited City Lookouts, Third Quarantine Cemetery, North Fort, Memorial Walk, and unfortunately North Head was closed during my visit early December even though the signage said construction until November. Arriving at Q Station, I followed Scenic Drive which becomes Darley Road and walked all the way back to The Corso. Overall, it was enjoyable hike, got to see a different Sydney but remember to bring sunscreen, hat and water.=TIPS=•	There are 2 ferries that go to Manly – one normal, cheaper and the other is the Manly Fast Ferry which is slightly more expensive and I think maybe 5 or 10 minutes faster than the normal ferry.•	There are signs throughout the hike but why not drop by the Information Centre just outside the Manly Wharf to have a chat to staff to find out more and also grab a map to see where you’re going?•	A short while after Shelly’s Beach, if you keep hiking up, you’ll come across a little gate with a sign that says no dogs. This is the gate you can go through to continue your hike. The guy at the Information Centre told me people are hesitant going through the gate but it’s open.

reviews.title: Good pub food at reasonable prices
reviews.text:
Hi Moira M

Manly Beach is one of Australia's most beautiful beaches, located a short ferry ride from Sydney. You are spoilt for choice when it comes to Manly Beach.  There are so many activities on offer, from lazing on the golden sands, surfing the waves or exploring the underwater world whilst snorkelling or diving. You can also explore the surrounding area by renting a bike, or walking one of the many walking tracks on offer. When its time to refuel, there are many restaurants, cafes and pubs where you can sate your thirst or hunger! reviews.title: Always great
reviews.text: It is my favorite beach, when I visit Sydney it's a must to make a trip to Manly at least once. It's a wonderful place with a nice pedestrian zone, beautiful beaches and walkways. It is part of a huge city but the natural beauty is near and easy to reach. Take your time and leave the most visited place. Walk further on and don't stop at Shelly Beach walk further on to the lookout and enjoy the fantastic panoramic view. I enjoyed my last visits and enjoyed swimming at the guarded beach, walked to the lookout near Shelly Beach and strolled through Manly. It was great and worth to visit again even. The easiest way to go to Manly is by ferry.

reviews.title: Always a must visit
reviews.text: Every trip to Sydney, we make at least a few trips over to Manly by ferry. Arriving in Manly Cove is lovely and protected swimming beaches. Walk through the main mall to Manly Beach which is fabulous. My favourite is to walk around to Shelley Beach and have lunch and drinks at the Boathouse Restaurant. Keep an eye out for happy hours. Another great place is the Manly 16’ Skiff Club, especially Monday, Tuesday and Thursday nights. Make sure you book, it’s very popular. In saying that there is so many great places to eat, relax and take in the scenery. Manly has everything, great walks along the harbour and ocean sides.

reviews.title: An enjoyable experience at this beach

It was lovely!Manly Beach is not very broad, it's a rather narrow stretch of sand, but flanked by the lovely trees, it's a sight for sore eyes. The water is crystal clear and on sunny days, the sea seems so inviting. Whether to take a swim or surf or to sit and observe the fun and frolic around, the Manly beach is an awesome place; i prefer it to the more famous Bondi Beach.There are a number of decent places to grab a meal nearby. There is also Shelley Beach, which is smaller but no less inviting.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi!
reviews.text: I grew up on Manly Beach and I think the setting beats Bondi hands down with the picturesque Norfolk Island pines. Catch the ferry from Circular Quay and after the delightful 30 minute ride to Manly, stroll along The Corso to the ocean beach. Even if the waves are big there is usually a calmer, safer swimming spot at the very end of the beach where it is more protected. However, always swim between the flags so you are always under the protective eyes of the Life Savers on duty. There are restaurants and cafes all along the beachfront catering to all appetites and pockets.

reviews.title: Don‘t miss Manly Beach and visit also Shelly Beach
reviews.text: The trip on the big ferry from Circular Quai to Manly takes about 30 minutes and is already an experience in itself.  In Manly you walk through the car-free Corso towards the beach.  The walk to the large beach takes a maximum of 10 minutes, if you don't get too distracted by the many shops, coffee shops etc. The mile-wide beach is overwhelming.  "Swimm between the flags" is rightly said here and guarded beach sections are available!  A walk to Shelly Beach, about 20 minutes away, is particularly nice.  A well-developed foot and bicycle path leads there.  Shelly Beach (picture 2) is located in a nature reserve, is protected from the big waves and is particularly suitable for swimming and snorkeling.  Cloakrooms and a restaurant are available.
