reviews.title: Far from the best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Manly gets massive crowds, due to its fame as well as the infrastructure (ferry, restaurants, etc). However, I don't go to beaches to be surrounded by massive crowds. It is hard to enjoy yourself when you have to fight to get your patch of sand or  spot in the surf.Positives: + My wife preferred the option of sitting under the shade of the trees, something you don't get at many beaches. + Plenty of options for getting lunch.Negatives:- The aforementioned crowds.- Good luck finding a parking spot anywhere near the beach.- The sand is very uneven, both on the beach and in the water.- Lots of doof doof music being played.

reviews.title: A good swim on a windy day
reviews.text: Visited the beach the last day on having the hop-on-hop-off ticket for a ferry. It was a bit overcast, but warm weather, so had our swimming suits with us.There was a netted area for swimming and the waves were reasonable size, so had a good swim.The beach wasn't crouded at all, maybe because of a bit cloudy day. Water felt a bit chilly at first, but not too bad to enjoy the swim.There were signs warning about penguins around, but didn't see any.There were changing rooms for swimmers down by the beach.

reviews.title: Manley beach, Sydney
reviews.text: This is by far one of the best beach areas I've been to - better than Bondi - huge beach, great waves, very safe, lifeguards on duty and a lovely walk along the bay ending at another small beach and two very nice restaurants. The shopping area in Manley is also worth looking at. When you get off the ferry at Manley don't think the beach is there, you have to walk straight ahead through the town and come to it on the other side.

reviews.title: A very popular island and beach easily reached from Sydney by boat..
reviews.text: Manly is a beautiful island with a shopping street of small stores, a picturesque crescent-shaped beach, and walking paths. I've been here before during the week. This time, I went on a Sunday in January. I urge that, if you have the flexibility, visit on a weekday for a wonderful day on this very pretty getaway a half-hour by boat from Sydney. Manly is extremely popular with locals and visitors in summer and primarily on weekends. On Sundays, Sydney public transport (which includes the ferries) has a maximum charge for the entire day's transport of less than $3 for those with an Opal magnetic transit card. The Manly boats, which run every 20-30 minutes on weekends, the island, and its beach overflow to capacity. Regardless of when you go, it's a great way to escape the busy city for a day of island breezes, lunch along the water's walkway, lifeguard-protected swimming, easy hiking, and an exuberant friends and families energy. Sit or stand in the rear upon departing Sydney (in the front on the return) for superb photography of the Harbour Bridge, the Sydney skyline, and the Opera House.

reviews.text: With this being our first trip to Australia we were of course keen to see the many amazing beaches that it has to offer and Manly was one that was often recommended to us,well i have to say that it really didn't impress me much.We had taken the ferry over from Circular Quay which was a pleasant journey and the  town itself was nice enough to stroll around but for me the beach itself was not really what i had expected.Yes it has a lovely long stretch of sand and the view of the waves crashing in was pretty impressive but the sight of a long waste pipe going into the sea and not being able to enter the water due to the conditions sort of spoiled things,i get the safety reasons for not being able to go in the water but for me that sort of defeats the point of a beach.I have to add that we also visited Bondi during our stay and for all 4 of us that visited that would win hands down every time.

It's also a short lovely stroll to Shelley beach which is a great place to swim with the kids or enjoy a refreshing drink or lunch at the cafe/ bar. reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: You can travel to Manly beach by taking a ferry from Circular Quay. Depending on if you have an Opal card or paying for a single ticket, a will cost you $5.65 to $9.40.The journey to Manly wharf is nice and takes you past the Sydney Opera house.Once you get to Manly wharf, it's about a 5 to 10 min walk to the beach past a number of food, souvenir, clothes and other shops.The beach itself is beautiful smooth sand and warm water. There are life guards who  duty. When I visited, they had the southern end set up for swimmers and the other areas for surfers. This was due to some strong rips on that day.You can also hire some beach gear. Along the other side of the road, are eateries that you can sit at and enjoy the view. I can imagine how busy this place can get on the weekends.You could spend a lot of time here or just a couple of hours.

reviews.text: Very scenic ferry ride from Sydney Harbour gives you some great views of the harbour and coastline along the way going east towards the ocean.. There are several places to hike along the coast of North Harbor at Manly and the huge Manly Beach itself is a short walk from the ferry. reviews.title: Visiting Manly N S W Australia.
reviews.text: Getting to Manly is a journey in itself!Manly is located on the North Shore of the Sydney CBD and is a coastal city within itself. Manly is accessible by road, however if visiting and you do not have access to a vehicle the most popular way of visiting Manly from Sydney if by water. “The Manly Ferry” runs at approx 20 minutes intervals from Circular Quay going to Manly and the same again leaving Manly heading back to Circular Quay. Once on the Ferry the views you get from the outside deck are some of the most spectacular in the world, Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Opera House, Luna Park, Cruise Ships, beautiful yachts spectacular Homes including Kirribilli House, our “Australian White House” A Fast ferry also services Manly.Once in Manly, if arriving by Ferry you walk out from the Manly Wharf onto the “Corso” Which is a mall that leads to the Manly Esplanade. Walking the Corso you will encounter many cafes, restaurants, gift shops and swim wear & surf shops, if you decide to go for a swim or go body surfing.Manly is known for its surf, sun bathing, outdoor exercising & beach sport. Once you have reached the end of the Corso u have the option of turning Left or Right. My suggestion is if looking at the ocean turn right and if you are up to taking a stroll you can walk all the way along the esplanade up over the hill and view “Shelly Beach” which is a marine sanctuary and on most days home to many scuba divers checking out the marine life. Once finished your stroll head back to the main section of the cafe strip and enjoy a meal of local Seafood or anything else of your choice.The climate is tropical and shorts and tee shirt are normally the standard dress. Manly is a beautiful part of the world and well worth a full days visit as part of your holiday in Sydney NSW Australia

reviews.title: Sun, sand and surf
reviews.text: With sand stretching from Queenscliff Rock Pool at the north end to Manly Life Saving Club at the south end, Manly Beach looked pleasant enough. I'll leave it to others to compare it to Bondi Beach (see my review, "Bondi's up!"). At Manly, shoppers were taking advantage of the beach's proximity to The Corso (see my review, "Sign me up!"), and surfers were taking advantage of a nice break. We quickly broke for North Head Sanctuary, though, and its spectacular ocean, cliff and Sydney skyline views (see my review, "Incredible skyline view"). TIPS:--We took a Sydney Ferries public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly Wharf; the trip is a tourist destination in itself (see my Sydney Ferries review, "Truly a top attraction").

reviews.text:

Glad you had a safe swim, look forward to seeing you again one day.

Cheers

reviews.title: A must do in Sydney
reviews.text:

It's nice to hear that you had a great time here in Manly! It is fantastic place to visit when you're in Sydney; from the scenic ferry trip, relaxing on one of our many beaches and bays to enjoying a delicious bite to eat in one of the many cafes, restaurants and bars. reviews.title: Don’t debate it, visit Manly!
reviews.text: We heard from a lot of locals that Manly was the place to go, so we did our research between Bondi and Manly and found Manly fit more with what we were looking for. We took the fast ferry from Circular Quay to Manly, very easy ride, and once dropped off it was literally a straight shot (short walk) to Manly beach. The sand is lovely, the views are great, not too many people! There was a lifeguard on duty because of strong currents and he was very engaged and ensured everyone stayed safe... we loved the walk from Manly to Shelly (about 15 mins) and found an awesome salt water pool right by the beach where we could enjoy the water even though currents were strong... it’s a really lovely place! We are glad locals told us to do this!!

reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: In my opinion, its prettier than Bondi beach. El Corso boulevard has places for shopping and eating for all pockets. The sand is white and fine. Waves not as big an Bondi and that's a plus for me. There's a path parallel to the shore that is a pleasure to walk.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviews.text: Visited on a Monday after taking the ferry from Sydney. Easy to get to the beach from the ferry terminal. The beach was busy but not too crowded. We had a very nice walk along the promenade towards Shelly Beach and the nature reserve. Both Manly and Shelly beaches were beautiful and not spoiled by over commercialisation.

reviews.title: Exciting and busy!
reviews.text: We visited BOndi by getting off the hop on hop off double decker bus. Had a delicious lunch at the local hotel. Ice cream from a specialty ice creamery! People everywhere, lots of shops and a beautiful, busy beach. Then back on the bus! A great day!

reviews.title: Awesome beach!
reviews.text: I won't say that this is the best beach in Sydney since I only visited Manly and Bondi, but I really enjoyed Manly Beach. It is gorgeous, and there is a lot more going on here than there was at Bondi. There's a better selection of food and shopping at Manly, and there's a small park about a block from the ferry that is nice for people-watching. I also had some of the best fish and trips here that I had during my entire 3 weeks in Australia (and I ate a lot of fish and chips during those 3 weeks). If I am back in Sydney again, I will definitely return to Manly.

The sands golden and clean.

There is so much to do on the Northern Beaches that you can always find a hidden gem where you can enjoy peace and quiet down at the beach.  Just ask us for some hot tips next time!

Lovely Manly beach,shops, pub/cafe/restaurants and walks along the foreshore from the ferry terminal. Just needed more time. Opal card used on ferry ride was very reasonable rate under $3 each way.

reviews.title: There is more
reviews.text: Visit Manly beach. Take the boat from Wharf 3. Go strait to Manly beach, watch the beautiful beach and leave this beach which is mostly overcrowded except in spring weekdays. Take a hike to North head Sanctuary! It takes 1.5 hours: beautiful trip, stunning views of sea, beaches and far away Sidney. Half way visit restaurant Bella Vista. What a spot! Walk down to Manly, but take the direction to Collins beach. A secret, most beautiful and deserted. Toen back to the boat in Manly in 15 minutes.

reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.text: We had limited time in Sydney as it was just a stop over for us, so we decided to take the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly.  The ferry took about 30-40 mins and we were able to take in the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Sydney Opera House and the Sydney skyline. It’s a lovely scenic trip. Once in Manly we made our way towards the beach. It’s not as big as I imagined but there were a few surfers, the sand was golden and the whole area had a magical vibe about it. The shops were ok but along a sea facing stretch of road were numerous sea food restaurants. We ate in one and it was excellent.  Manly is a beautiful place to visit and I would recommend that this should be every visitors to see list.

reviews.title: Day trip to Manly Beach
reviews.text: Get the Ferry to Manly from Circular Key and walk down the corso to beach at opposite end of Ferry to hit Manley Beach. Stunning long beach with great public toilet facilities. Enjoy a gelatto .... yummy as you enjoy the local shops on the corso!! I also had some barramundi and chips in Manley local fish shop/market just off the corso . It is a well known fish shop that also cooks fish to eat or take away. Great little spot to check out while in Sydney

reviews.title: Lunch
reviews.text: The Manly Pavillion a wonderful place to eat. We suprised them with 10 unannounced guests but they able to accomodate us.The food and service tremendous

reviews.title: Good Excursion to spend a day

Thanks for the review - the ferry is a great way to travel here, either take the public ferry or if you are in a hurry, the private ferry takes only 18 minutes. There are several restaurants where you can enjoy seafood, either sit down or take-away. Watch out for those pesky seagulls who will literally steal the food from your mouth!!

Hope to see you back here one day!
Cheers

reviews.title: Great spot to enjoy wine at a cafe on the beach
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quay ( buy the Opal Card and use for travel on ferry ) $ 7.50 each way was worth just the view of Sydney harbor . Get off at Manley and short walk to the beach .Lots of shopping , cafes and restaurants . We enjoyed a bottle of wine facing the beach at Blue Water Cafe . Very enjoyable couple of hours on Manly Beach .

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: Great area. Interesting shops and eateries. Surf school and miles of beautiful clean beach. Manly has so much more to offer than Bondi and is an absolute must if visiting Sydney. Easily reached by ferry from circular quay no need to book. The ferries run regularly and can be paid for with your  Opal card which covers you for bus, rail and light railway (tram). Do it!

reviews.title: Sydney's BEST beach!
reviews.text: Oh well, I could be as it was my birthplace but the sweeping circular golden beach friinged with the stately Norfolk pines is just stunning. Walk around thee point near the Manly Surf club to experience an beautiful walk to a hidden wonder, Shelley Beach which is a marine sanctuary. A fabulous place to snorkel!

reviews.title: A lovely Sunday visit
reviews.text: While staying in Sydney we went to Manly and spent some time walking the foreshore.Being a lovely sunny Sunday it was quite busy, lots of surfers in the water doing their thing and kids playing beach volleyball, looks like you could have lessons there.Only early spring but plenty of people in the water.Had not been there for many years and I was interested to read that surfing in Australia started here at Manly.Have to visit here when in Sydney, plenty of places to eat and a good market on the Sunday.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Sydney Harbour to Manly Beach  and I as so glad that we did. What a beautiful little gem of a place. The tree lined espleanade is great for a shopping spree and the beach at the far end is just stunning. A beautiful bay of golden sand, attracting surfers, sun bathers and beach volleyball players. We had lunch just across the road, which was perfect. There is such a relaxed vibe here,  I could have easily stayed far longer. A must visit.

reviews.title: So romantic and relaxing
reviews.text: Took the ferry to Manly is one tap on only,no need to tap off very easy walk down to the beach just sat there to eat fish and chips. don’t let the seagulls  have your food they will pursue everyone’s food. friendly locals the shopping was quite reasonable

reviews.title: Beautiful 1 mile long crescent beach with active promenade.
reviews.text: We took the crowded noon Manly Ferry($5 US each) for its 1/2 hour scenic cruise through Sydney's harbors. After arriving at Manly wharf, we crossed over the 500 meter 'Corso' to the beach, realizing we had come on the final day of the yearly Jazz Festival. Strolling the Marine Parade promenade, we discovered the south half was also filled with an extended weekend craft market. We continued to the Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve for its beautiful view of secluded Shelly Beach.Returning we stopped to use the public restrooms at the Manly Life Saving Club but the queue was far too long.  A nearby restaurant was the answer as was Ben & Jerry's for ice cream before returning to the wharf for the every 1/2 hour ferry back to the Circular Quay. Wonderful afternoon in active Sydney.

reviews.title: Australia Day
reviews.text:
Hi sherone1958

Thanks for taking time to write a great review. It is so good to hear that people love coming back to Manly and what more could you want for a wonderful day out - beach, ice-cream, good coffee and a beautiful ferry ride!
Cheers

reviews.title: One of the popular beaches in Sydney
reviews.text:
Hi DeshmukhV

Glad you enjoyed your trip to Manly - the promenade walk to Shelly Beach is one of the most beautiful walks in Sydney! Manly itself has a huge variety of cafes, bars and restaurants to choose from. Next time you visit Manly, make sure you call in at the Manly Visitors Info Centre to get some tips from the friendly local staff on where to go!
Cheers

reviews.title: Tremendous Magnetic Appeal
reviews.text: Once you disembarked at the Manly Wharf, you can sensed the magnetic appeal of the  beach. Girls in their bikinis and boys wearing their swimming trunks and roller skates are walking to and fro along the boulevard. The beach itself are full of sun worshippers lying on the sun while others are swimming against the waves. It is a sight to watch.

reviews.title: Must see when in Sydney
reviews.text:
Hi LarryRenoTahoe
Thanks for your review - we are glad you loved Manly beach! The ferry is certainly a fantastic way to travel here, either the fast in 18 mins or the slow which takes half an hour. There are a variety of great walks to choose from. Next time you visit Manly, make sure you pop into the Manly Visitors Information Centre where the friendly staff can organise surf lessons or any other activities you may be interested in as well as give you a free map and explain the different walks on offer.
Thanks

reviews.title: Very peaceful holiday vibe
reviews.text:
Hi genelow16,

Thanks for visiting Manly Beach. If you come on the right day you might be lucky and escape the crowds, which is what it sounds like happened to you guys!

Come back soon,

The Hello Manly Team

reviews.title: Lounge, Walk, and People Watch
reviews.text: Beautiful, long beach (plenty of space to spread out when we were there). Even if you don't plan to swim, you can get beautiful views walking the shoreline with your toes in the ocean. Watch the surfers or the kiddos making sandcastles. Easy access to public restrooms. Can rent your own surf experience if interested as well. There are water washing stations to get all that sand off your feet as well!

reviews.title: simply the best!!!
reviews.text: YOU want sun?? You got it at Manly and ice-creams...mmmmm!With all the bronze curves and tiny clothings!!! I can't resists the temptation of the waters to cool myself...Ladies loves being admired like in european beaches here on Manly!!Fish and chip highly recommended and a few night-life romantic restaurants to chew before retiring to my rented room also at reasonable price.The atmostphere you would want to take home to remember those photos you took backing you to come back time when you're in Sydney.

reviews.title: Manly Beach, a Must
reviews.text:
Hi Kreuzlingen1,

Thanks for visiting Manly Beach and writing such a great review. We're proud of our many restaurants, cafes and shops and especially the ferry. The fast ferry is 20 minutes compared to the normal ferry which takes 30 mins. Sometimes it's nice to enjoy that extra time getting to the beach before everyone else!

Much love,
Hello Manly

reviews.title: Underwhelmed
reviews.text:
Hi Diana B,

Unfortunately Sydney's weather is all over the place at the moment, so one day will be freezing, while the next is a perfect summers day. Although the surfers are here no matter what!

In regard to the pipes, they are actually storm water run off drains which means they are only used when we have an excess of water from rain. 

We're sorry that you were unable to find many restaurants with gluten free options, sometimes you just need some help to know where to look! Around the back of the library on Market lane are a couple good ones such as Verd, Banana Blossom, Momo Bar and more. We also have some more formal restaurants with gluten free, vegan and vegetarian options such as Garfish, Hugos and The Pantry.

We hope you visit again and have a better experience,
The Hello Manly Team

reviews.title: Love
reviews.text:
Hi saveoursouls999,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the great review. So great to hear you enjoyed your time here. The ferry ride from the Sydney harbour is beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Amazingly beautiful
reviews.text: After a short boat ride we arrived at Manly Beach. Don’t be fooled the arrival area is not the beach, you have to walk about a 1/3 of a mile to get to the amazing beach area. We walked up and down the boardwalk area in both directions, the sun was shining, but it wasn’t hot at all. It was perfect weather. We walked to Shelly Beach, which was not far at all. There was the cutest restaurant called the Boat House, the menu looked inviting, but we had already had breakfast elsewhere. This area is a must see when visiting Sydney.

reviews.title: Lovely clean beach and plenty of facilities and harbour ferry os a must.
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Warm and sunny time! Enjoyable
reviews.text: Enjoyed our ferry to Manly beach. Even though it was bright and sunny the pleasant wind made the walk to the beach worthwhile. The small bistros and charming restaurants on way were so inviting ; difficult to resist .Beach was clean and safe with families enjoying time out. Near the ferry stop the tourism centre is super friendly ,ready to offer advice and support. Even gives a clean matter of fact map to walk around.The movenpik ice cream parlour serves yummy ice cream.

reviews.title: Much better than Bondi
reviews.text:
HI Froglit

Thanks for your great review - we too prefer Manly to Bondi, one of the reasons being we have a variety of beaches to choose from; harbour, surf and of course, Shelly Beach which is often protected from big seas and is a fantastic area for snorkelling. Next time you visit Manly, make sure you call in at the Visitors Information Centre to get your free map of Manly as well as local tips about where to eat/drink etc.

Thanks

reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text:
Hi 837cherif

So glad you had an amazing time in Manly, one of the most popular beaches in Sydney. It sounds as though you chose a couple of our most popular eating places, I'm so glad both experiences were great! Manly has a large variety of shops to browse, ranging from popular surfbrand stores to exclusive boutiques.

Thanks

reviews.title: Manley beach
reviews.text: Lovely views of Sydney in the sun from the sea as you sail to Manly.Once there, lots of great places to eat and drink. We strolled on the long lovely beach.Very pretty place.On way back it was dark and Sydney looked spectacular all lit up.Well worth it.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi

reviews.title: Nice Roadtrip to Manly
reviews.text: We've planed this road trip for a long time since we were too busy recently to went on a holiday. We rent an MPV from @EasyRentCars and drove to Manly. Stayed there for 2 nights. Had a great weekend with my wife and kids. Manly is the best place for a short getaway holiday near Sydney city. Warm sunshine and soft surfing. Kids love this place.

reviews.title: Great area
reviews.text:
Hi leonardokirkg

Thanks for your 5* review of beautiful Manly Beach - it is true, you will always find someone in the water where it can be warmer than the air temperature and winter can bring great surf and water clarity!  You can also take a number of ferries from Circular Quay, the public ferry takes 30 minutes whilst the fast harbour cat only 18 minutes. Hope to see you again in Manly one day soon

Thanks

reviews.title: Iconic Aussie Beach
reviews.text:
Hi bevenh

Thanks for the very good tips and advice especially regarding swimming between the flags, the importance of which many people are unaware! If you are looking for a safe beach to swim at, Shelly beach is tucked away in the eastern corner, about 15 minutes walk along a beautiful coastal walk. It is protected from the swell and there are showers and changeroom facilities there as well.

Thanks

reviews.title: Pretty
reviews.text:
Hi L H

Manly is certainly a very popular beach and easy to access, being a short 5 minute walk down the Corso. There are many different restaurants, cafes and pubs where it is possible to enjoy a variety of cusines  from Japanese noodles to fine dining. If you are feeling adventurous, there are many beaches further north which are accessible either by bus or on foot. Make sure you pop into the Manly Visitors Information Centre to have a chat to the friendly staff who can give you a map or local advice on where to go.
Thanks

reviews.title: 7 miles from sydney & thousand miles to care.
reviews.text:
Hi Rusty W

Thanks for your great review - the ferry trip across from Circular Quay to Manly is a fantastic way to get to Manly in either 30 minutes with the public ferry or 18 mins on the fast harbour cat. The Corso is a wide treelined street/pedestrian area which takes you down to the beach in 5 minutes and then there is a beautiful 20 minute stroll along a coastal pathway to beautiful Shelly Beach.

Hope to see you back in Manly one day.
Cheers

reviews.title: Manly gone a little seedy
reviews.text: Fantastic trip over and back on the ferry Freshwaterfrom circular quay. Adele and I are both pensioners now so enjoy tripping around for two dollars fifty  a day on our public transport system.  Manly beach still a fantastic beach.The local eateries are now a bit over the top price wise.  How about one dozen oysters au naturale for forty eight dollars.   But they will sell you 4 oysters for sixteen dollars, a bargain, I think not. We gave the oysters a miss and settled for whoppers and chips from Hungry Jacks.  We did have excellent ice  creams from manly wharf, excellent and reasonably priced.Manly has now sprouted a proliferation of those seedy souvenir shops.   The ones we all love to hate, selling overpriced stuffed koalas and boomerangs made in China.I used to live in Narrabeen back in the late 60s early 70s.    We used to frequent the various  reasonably priced restaurants in the area, and enjoyed our 23 cent Schooners of Reschs at the Steyne Hotel.   Yes I know, inflation, but still it is a shock. Five dollars used to get you a good feed and 6 or more ice cold frosty scooies. Thats schooners or glasses of beer for people not from NSW.Tomorrow we are going to Sydney fish markets where we can have a good feed of prawns and oysters at a reasonable price.  Not the four dollars per oyster they charge in Manly.Roy

reviews.title: What a beach
reviews.text:
Hi gilly s

The Bluewater cafe is a great place for breakfast and very popular with the locals. So glad you found the beach clean and tidy, that is what we love to hear. The ferry is a great way to visit Manly, a 30 minute boat ride from Circular Quay on the public ferry, or if you are in a hurry, the harbour jet cat takes only 18 minutes.  We look forward to welcoming you back to Manly again one day.

Cheers

reviews.title: Great Time
reviews.text:
Hi Compass 15643208782

Hi - thanks for your great review - and it always makes a trip worthwhile when you pick up an unexpected bargain! The markets are very popular with both locals and the tourists and are open Saturdays and Sundays, with fruit and vege markets on Sundays only.  And fantastic to have the sun shining as well!
Cheers

reviews.title: Great beach even on an overcast day.
reviews.text:
Hi Bill291

So glad you had a fantastic visit to Manly - sometimes those overcast days can be very special, especially in winter when the waters are calm and there aren't so many people about. It is also a good time to hire a bike and venture up to North Head to take in the fantastic views of the City and the northern beaches. Maybe even spot a humpback or southern right whale on their migratory path.

Hope to see you back in Manly one day soon.
Cheers

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text:
Hi Jandp768

Glad you enjoyed your visit to beautiful Manly beach. It is certainly good advice to watch out for the seagulls who are also very partial to free fish and chips! The ferry is a great way to visit Manly, no traffic or petrol fumes, just a beautiful scenic boat trip which can be taken in 30 minutes on the public ferry or if you are short of time, the fast ferry takes only 18 minutes. Next time you come to Manly, make sure to pop in to the Visitors Information Centre to grab your complimentary copy of the Manly map and the friendly staff will share some of the local's secret tips.

Cheers

reviews.title: Nice Beach
reviews.text: If you have time, the ferry ride to Manly Beach is worth it. The ferry ride is nice and from the wharf it is a short walk to the beach along the Corso (directly across from the wharf). Passing several blocks of shops on the way, but the walk is nice. Once at the beach you are greeted with a clean beach walk and beach. The vastness of the pacific and the continuous  rolling waves coming to the nice sandy beach. The beach walk and the beach go both directions for a long ways and is nice to walk after putting your feet in the water. Lots of eateries along the beach walk area make this a nice afternoon trip.

reviews.title: Amazing Surfing Beach but Don't go during Bad Weather
reviews.text: My husband and I went to Manly when it was raining and grey, so we weren't able to experience its full glory. Despite this, there were numerous surfers out having a great time and I could tell the beach would a completely different experience if it had been warm out.Along with the beach, there is a great walking path and nature path that leads up to a fort. There are also plenty of little shops and restaurants to choose from, with prices ranging depending on what you feel like.The easiest way to get to Manly is by ferry from Circular Quay, but there is also a roundabout bus route.

reviews.title: Awesome Summer Times
reviews.text:
Hi Austbynature2018

Thanks for your great review - you are right, Manly is definitely a great place to be, winter or summer and the ferry ride across from the city is a fantastic scenic trip regardless of the season. Make sure you visit the Manly Visitor's Information Centre to collect a free map as well as many useful tips from the locals about where to shop, dine or stroll.
Thanks

reviews.title: a great walk!
reviews.text:
Hi Marytimich

So glad you had a great time at Manly Beach, we would definitely agree with the recommendation. The surfers can be very entertaining, especially when the swell is up. Next time you visit Manly, be sure to call past the Manly Visitors Info Centre for more information about all the activities, shops, restaurants etc which Manly has to offer.
Thanks

reviews.title: Sooooo Relaxing!
reviews.text: My wife & I come to Sydney at least once a year for a long weekend & we always spend one day at Manly beach.From the moment you get off the ferry you feel relaxed and like your on a long holiday.A walk along the main drag to the beach is always interesting with such a diverse range of people doing their thing.Once you hit the beach you can sit in the sun on the steps and watch the world go by.There are water stations to fill your bottles and so much to see and enjoy.We always walk around to the right onto shelly beach to a little restaurant there called the Boathouse.It's one of our favs.Whilst walking along the path again you have so much to look at and people watch.When you get back onto the ferry back to Circular Quay you feel like you have been away for a week.If you're in Sydney for a short stay make Manly a priority.You won't regret it.

reviews.title: Nice beach- can get to by public transit - long stretch
reviews.text:
Hi LL-CA-Nevada

Glad you enjoyed your stroll down the Corso and got to explore the back alleyways where some of the shops and restaurants are hidden. Manly Beach is easily reached by a 20 minute ferry ride from Circular Quay, Sydney - they run every half an hour until midnight so plenty of time to enjoy the village.
Thanks for your review.
Cheers

reviews.title: Manly
reviews.text:
Hi Shane Y

Thanks for your great review - we agree with you that Manly is a world-class beach and certainly the 20 min ride with the fast ferry or 30 mins with the public ferry is definitely the way to travel!  There are beautiful beaches are both the harbour and ocean side of Manly as well as several ocean pools. A great way to explore is to rent a bike at the Visitors Information Centre on your right as you exit the ferry terminal.
Hope to see you back here one day soon.
Cheers

reviews.title: Probably better when sunny
reviews.text:
Hi learningand diving

Such a shame you had to visit Manly on a rainy windy day (we don't actually suffer from too many of those!). That can be a good day to visit the local Art Gallery or settle down in one of the many cosy cafes. We hope that next time you visit us, you will be blessed with sunny skies and be able to see how wonderful the beaches are when the sun is shining!
Cheers

reviews.title: Worth the ferry ride!
reviews.text:
Hi Cheysplore

Glad you had a great trip to Manly - in winter/spring the water can actually be warmer than the outside temperature. Next time you visit us, make sure you call in at the Visitors Information Centre so we can share some of the local's tips about where to find cheap eats!
Cheers

reviews.title: A lovely beach without the crowds and hype of Bondi
reviews.text:
Hi Lissel A

Thanks for the great review - renting a bike from Hello Manly is certainly a fantastic way to explore Manly Beach as well as the North Head. The view from there is superb and it is great to jump in the water to cool off after a long bike ride. Winter/Spring time is certainly a great time to visit, less people and the restaurants/bars on the harbourside are an excellent location to watch the sun go down.
Thanks

reviews.title: Beautiful beach close to shopping and great restaurants
reviews.text:
Hi NorthStar161904

You were very fortunate to be able to stay so close to Manly Beach. Winter/Spring time can actually be a very special time of year to visit Manly, fewer people around, clean waves, clear water and the chance of spotting a whale from the shores!

Thanks

reviews.title: Another great beach
reviews.text:
Hi Becs_London_UK

Glad you enjoyed Manly Beach - such a special place to visit in the winter months when there are not as many people about! There are certainly many cafes and first class restaurants to visit, both on the high st (The Corso!) or tucked away in the back lanes. Be sure to try some of the great fish on offer to complement those chips!

Cheers

reviews.title: Perfect wrap up
reviews.text: We took the public ferry to Manly and it was a great way to wrap up our trip.  The ride over took less than 30 minutes and we sat and watched the beautiful views.  Once we arrived, we walked in/out of shops and ended up sitting on the beach and people watching.  We grabbed lunch and Ben & Jerry’s ice cream and made our way back to the ferry.  I would estimate we spent a little over 2 hours here.  The visit was nice and relaxing and exactly what we wanted.

reviews.title: Ferry to Manly Beach
reviews.text:

reviews.text:

reviews.title: Fantastic place
reviews.text: I visited Manley with a few friends on my recent visit to Sydney.  We caught one of the early fast ferry's from circular key at Sydney harbour direct to Manley Wharfe soaking up the views on route there.  When we arrived everyone seemd to head straight to the beach which was just a short walk straight across the road from the ferry terminal and along the main Street past lots of good clothes shops and quite a few restaurants and bars.  The beach is gorgeous with lovely clean soft sand...which reminds me of lots of carribean beaches I have visited.  What made it even better was the fact that it was winter there but still 23 degrees.  Well warm enough to lounge about on the beach for a few hours and soak up the sun.  We had breakfast in a lovely bar on the beachfront and the chef was actually from Birmingham and we had a good chat with him and he made us a great breakfast and then actually paid for us all a drink on him. thanks pal. We had a good walk up and down and had a drinks in a few of the bars.  As the sun was going down we went into a fish restaurant had lovely fish chips and mushy peas.  The fish was Hoki I belive from New Zealand...very nice white fish and very tasty.We all purchased a few aussie shirts and tee shirts and even a couple of jackets. We rounded the visit of nicely with a few more drinks in a nice bar next to the Ferry terminal and then caught the ferry back around 9.30pm.  I would recommend a visit here in fact I would love to holiday here and then catch the ferry in reverse to visit Sydney itself.

reviews.title: Manley Beach
reviews.text:
Hi Heatherjeannette, 
Thanks for the review! 
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 

Glad  you enjoyed to walk along our beautiful beach with Golden sands :) 
Hope to see you again! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information centre

reviews.title: Age old weekender and holiday haunt
reviews.text: Any excuse to go to Manly Beach, a place that brings back sweet childhood holiday memories for my children and I.  World famous, bit more low key than Bondi, probably only because it is not on the Eastern Suburbs.  Great natural beauty, you can go for a walk around to Shelley Beach afterwards.

reviews.title: Must do when in Sydney
reviews.text: Manly is one of our best beaches far better than Bondi in my opinion. We live on the other side of Sydney but often go to spend a weekend at Manly. It’s just like being on holidays beautiful beaches great restaurants shops and things to do. There is also Shelly beach and Manly wharf beaches.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach and great walk
reviews.text:

reviews.title: A Mob Scene
reviews.text: we went on a sunny winter Sunday when the R/T ferry fare was a$ 2.80 on the travel cardFerries were packed (pay the extra for the fast ferry) - town was packed and in our opinion, had little offer- very touristyMay be better during the week

reviews.title: Wonderful day trip with visitors
reviews.text: Not only is the beach beautiful and full of activity, from board riders to body surfers, but there is a superb view of the coastline north and of numerous other beaches. Arrival by ferry from Circular Quay is dramatic and provides an excellent tour of the Harbour and views of the Heads.We walked across the narrow neck of land from the ferry to the sea and ate fish and chips watching the surf. There are rocks to climb and a wonderful walk around the bay to Fairy Bower.This excursion renews the spirit and is a perfect introduction to Australia's best beach for overseas visitors.

reviews.title: Amazing walk
reviews.text: Although it was  a rainy day when we went to Manly beach, it is a not to be missed beachThe fun begins with the ferry ride from Sydney harbour to Manly. The beach is a good ten minute walk through  beautiful road liked with shops.The walking trails Along the beach are very beautiful and scenic. We enjoyed our walks along the coast.

reviews.title: Much Better Than Bondi
reviews.text: I live in the UK and have visited Sydney only twice. Both times I have been to Bondi and Manly beach and both times I have come away with the same thoughts.  I prefer Manly to Bondi!!We took the ferry on a Monday to Manly harbour then walked through the pedestrian area to Manly beach to watch the late afternoon surfers. Girls walk down the road wearing just bikini tops and very skimpy pants!!! We sat on the beach wall eating a snack and a huge seagull swooped down and tried to steal it. Watch out for them they are vicious!!!

reviews.title: Frequent visitor
reviews.text: I just spent the last month in Sydney (Northern Beaches) and frequented Manly. I opted to stay away from Bondi and spend time here instead. The water was great, atmosphere wasn’t overwhelming, and there is a unique crowd of regulars. I highly recommend exploring Shelley beach as well.

reviews.title: Chill out Sunday
reviews.text: Manly Beach one of our favourite place to visit and you can arrived with style by catching a ⛴ ferris from the city. Heaps of coffee shops and resto for a lunch or you can just grab a bite and 🚶 walk along the beach. Great to relax and we love keep coming back here.

reviews.title: Wonderful spot
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Great place to swim and relax
reviews.text:
Hi John M

Thanks for your great review - Manly Beach has recently been voted one of Sydney's top beaches on Trip Advisor. Make sure that when you visit you either swim between the flags or at Shelly Beach which is unpatrolled but very safe. There are a myriad of restaurants, cafes and pubs to visit and many different shops tucked away in back alleys and on the main route (the Corso) to the beach.

reviews.title: eating fish & chips on the sand
reviews.text: we got the ferry over to Manly which was a great ride...great way to see the harbour.  Walking down the mall to the beach was very touristy, but we got some nice fish & chips and went and sat on the beach in front of the water....we loved that...very casual...there are restaurants around, in case people want to sit down to eat

reviews.title: Worth a visit when in Sydney
reviews.text: You can get to Manly on the regular ferry (using the same ticket as for the train) and one advantage is that this gives you views of the Harbour without having to go on a harbour tour. It's a fair trip to Manly, but you do find a seaside town that then faces out on to the ocean and has a feeling of being cut off from big city Sydney. The town itself is a little run-down (though I was there out of season) but the area around the beach is lively and I walked along the front to Shelly Beach and there was plenty of interest. I imagine that at the height of summer it would be packed.I underestimated how much I could do and see there and so it is the one place in Sydney that I wanted to go back to as I had not had enough time to explore.

reviews.title: So clean
reviews.text:
Hi petsiep,

Who doesn't love Manly? Beautiful place, beautiful people, amazing coffee and super yummy food.
We are happy you liked it! 

Make sure you visit us at Hello Manly Visitor Information Center at the wharf next time - we'll give you some invaluable tips about Manly and Northern Beaches area.

Thank you :)
Hello Manly Visitor Information Center

reviews.title: Nice atmosphere
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, with a nice relaxed atmosphere. Surfers, young people with kids, elderly people, good mix. On the boulevard people are jogging, taking a relaxed walk. Personal trainers with sporters, yoga classes, or people just enjoying the sunshine.

reviews.title: On a fine and windless day, so much to 'sea' and do. On other days with a warm jacket, still lots to do and discover.
reviews.text:

Next time you visit Manly, make sure you pop into our office located on the wharf as you exit the ferry terminal and collect a couple of maps detailing other walks that are available such as the Manly Scenic Walk to Spit Bridge and the North Head Walk! Thanks
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Manly is the Classic Aussie Beach
reviews.text:
Hi Christopher,

Hope to see you again soon!

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Nice town to visit when in Sydney
reviews.text: We took the fast ferry from Circular Quay and it took only 25 minutes to get to Manly Beach. We shopped a little and sat on the Beach for a while, the weather was nice so all in all a good day. We also wanted to go to Bondi but there is no ferry to Rose Bay or Watson Bay in the winter, be aware!

reviews.title: Beautiful little beach

reviews.title: A stunning beach and MORE - The place is Electric
reviews.text: Take the Ferry from Circular Quay to get here, takes about half-hour.  After the short walk from the dock, the beach itself is amazing.  I came in August (middle of the winter right) but it was still fairly crowded (60F-70F temps) and surfers were still doing their thing, and lots of swimmers too (in wet suits sometime). I didn't come prepared for a beach, but that's ok because there were many concrete steps to sit at while watching the beach goers and surfers.  I can only imagine how crowded this place gets during their summer.There's more to do here than the beach, as the town is fun to walk around (very touristy) with kiosks/crafts, restaurants/food, souvenir shops, etc.  I also recommend the walk around the right side of the beach, nice walking/jogging trail and in 10 mins you'll hit Shelly Beach that you can see across the way as you walk.Would love to come back here in the warmer months and spend a few nights at Manly - fun youthful environment and a beautiful beach to center your time around.

reviews.text:

Manly can become crowded during the weekends but if you arrive on a weekday, you may be very surprised at the peaceful beach scene you will find and of course the cafes and restaurants will be quiet as well. You may miss out on the wonderful markets though which are held on the weekends in Sydney Road.
Best regards

reviews.title: Pretty but packed !
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Fantastic Beach
reviews.text: Despite being out of season for a ‘beach day’ we were very keen to come here, I have been once before many years ago – however, the memory must be fading as I can’t recall the sand being as gorgeous as it was or is it now that I’ve been visiting beaches in Europe for so many years lately & having to put up with the relative mediocrity that seeing decent golden soft sand again seemed such a luxury. Despite the cold July day, it was encouraging to see surfers enjoying the waves as well as others swimming or messing about in the breakers (braver than I was feeling though) – Great Beach, Great Location & kept so lovely & clean too.

reviews.title: Like it more than Bondi
reviews.text:

Yes!! We do agree with you - Manly is a very beautiful beach with a unique village-like atmosphere, lots of interesting shops and boutiques tucked away in back lanes. If you are in a hurry, you can always take the private fast ferry which speeds along from Circular Quay to Manly in 18 minutes.

reviews.title: Extensive walking path along the beach
reviews.text: Beach is large and clean, with a very long walking path along the beach and up around a bend.  The area seemed very friendly to dogs.  Note that swimming is not recommended for 24 hrs after heavy rain, as drainage from the surrounding area dumps right in the middle of the beach.  When we visited, however, there had not been rain for about a week, and the water was clear.  We found that Manly beach was much less crowded, and the area and facilities cleaner, than Bondi beach.

reviews.title: Perfect Beach Spot for Families
reviews.text: This beach is much larger with more restaurants and shops than Bondi. There is a small coastal walk, not like by Bondi, but if you’re just looking for a beach day, I’d choose here over Bondi. Our boys dug in the sand and played in the surf all day. There is a small downtown pedestrian shopping area with plenty to see. The beach is clean with several life guards and flags marking the safe swimming areas. It’s much easier to access than Bondi as the ferry from the Rocks takes you straight here, no bus or transfers needed.

reviews.title: What a beautiful place to spend a day!
reviews.text: The beach is very easy to get to, which is important with my mobility issues. There are very nice, shaded benches to sit and admire the views. The boardwalk had a very nice selection of shops and eateries. We rode the ferry over, and what a beautiful ride that was....we came home with nice pictures of the Sydney Opera House and Sydney skyline.

reviews.title: Nice day for a walk
reviews.text: I visited Manly Beach on in June, during the Sydney winter. The weather was comfortable—high 50s F—and would warm into the low 70s later in the day. I took the fast ferry to Manly—the farthest point of the harbor from downtown, out toward the ocean—for $18 AU round trip from Circle Quay, Only $2 more than the city ferry that takes 15 minutes more each way.When you walk out of the nice ferry hub and cross the street you enter a pedestrian mall with many types of shops. I stopped at a grocery for food, intending to each lunch at the beach. Great idea. Plenty of picnic tables available. Sat and ate while watching a small group of surfers trying to catch the small waves that day. Being winter, the beach wasn’t crowded, even though the water was fairly warm.There is a paved walking path all along the beach that leads up into and through the Sydney Harbor National Park. If you have 3-4 hrs, decent shoes, and are able to hike, I encourage you to make this trek. In addition to the flora and fauna, you can learn about the Quarantine station that was originally there—it would be similar to America’s Ellis Island, where immigrants would be off-loaded and held in quarantine until they proved healthy or died. The park—which includes North Head, with its fabulous views—was also a military base during the two world wars and a gunnery school.A great day at the beach and more.

reviews.title: Popular, fascinating, magnetic.
reviews.text: The ferry ride is a visual delight, the short isthmus of Manly is bright and busy shopping area and then the magnificent beach and ocean are revealed. Manly is always busy but it never seems overcrowded. It is well overseen by life guards and everyone has a battle with the surf - surfers are here but more for show I suspect.  It is good to follow the coast path - farther on south there are smaller beaches and you can also easily reach North Head for great views of the gap between headlands where harbour meets ocean.

reviews.title: Wonderful visit - worth a half day trip
reviews.text: I probably would not have sought out Manly Beach for itself, had we not combined our visit here with a hike through North Head Sanctuary which gave us stunning views of the harbor and coast.  The beach was nice, but pretty crowded on a Tuesday lunch time in May.Our day started with North Head (easily accessible from the ferry terminal by bus) and we hiked down the Shelley Beach and then onto Manly.  The beach was nice to walk on for a bit, but again it was pretty crowded with a mix of tourists and locals.  We got some fish and chips at the fish market nearby which we enjoyed at a picnic table near the beach.  The corso was okay to walk down, and I'd love to come back and try some of the restaurants in Manly.All in all we spent about 4-5 hours in North Head Sanctuary and Manly and were back in the CBD by 2pm, allowing us time to hang out and do other things.

reviews.title: Great atmosphere on a sunny winters day
reviews.text: Just great to sit and watch the beach life, the wind was blowing strong so a cold wind but the surfers were out having fun, we had Fish & Chips (pricey) and walked to Shelley Headland with lots of ever changing views of the beach. The beach is a short walk from the Manly ferry pier, only 30 minutes from Circular Quay.

reviews.title: Manly Beach
reviews.text: I had Manly Beach on my places to go while in Sydney . I was so amazed by how clean this beach was that i did a small video clip to show my friends and family . the beach was the cleanest beach i have ever been too in my 60 years of living . no rubbish , no glass , no litter , no broken bottles or cans . And I watched a guy raking the beach for an hour . the sand even smelt clean . I could go on and on  but you need to go there to see this marvelous wonder for yourselves . Manly has a great ferry service  and great bus service once your there. lots of nice places to eat and great shopping as well .

reviews.title: Okay
reviews.text:
Hello Cheesey Bugger,

So sorry to hear your visit to manly was not what you expected.

Sydney’s beaches are often accompanied by an ocean pool, but few are as unique as this one at the south end of Manly Beach. Firstly, Fairy Bower rock pool is rectangular in shape, built by local residents in 1929. And secondly, it features a pair of striking sculptures by artist Helen Leete called ‘The Oceanides’, which look like a pair of dancers twirling above the water.

Next time, come and see us outside Manly Wharf for great tips next time you visit.

Thank you,

reviews.title: Very Crowded during a Food and Wine Festival
reviews.text:
Hello KimkX819SI,

Manly is loved by all, and yes, can get very busy especially during the Taste of Manly – Food, Wine and Sustainability festival.

It was on Saturday 25th and Sunday 26th May 2019 and it was our 33rd year of this successful festival. 

This festival is a celebration of wine, food and culture here in Manly, with all the best local restaurants showcasing their goods alongside some of the best regional and international wineries, beer and cider brewers.

Along with the mouth-watering food and drink there were also four stages set up with Live Entertainment, amusement rides for the kids, a sustainable hub and the Manly Market Place set up on Sydney Road.

We hope you will visit us again, maybe on week day when it is much quieter to experience our beautiful beaches and life style.

Please visit us, we are located outside Manly Wharf, for great tips.

reviews.text:
Hi Murray A

Thanks for your great review - Manly boasts a 1.5km beach with various spots to surf, swim or paddleski. The ferry ride is certainly a spectacular way to visit from the City. The food and wine festival is usually held in the middle of May so make sure to coincide your visit with this event and you will get to experience a variety of the different cuisines offered by the many restaurants in Manly.
best regards

reviews.title: Come & visit earli during a weekday morning....
reviews.text: Manly is one of he best beaches in Sydney. It is clean, generally the surf is safe and a nice walk from Queenscliff to Manly and Shelley Beach.Come during the week as its too crowded on weekends and try to come early to see the sunrise. There are lots of good cafes and even restaurants & pubs to eat at.A must if in Sydney

reviews.title: Good Relaxing Place
reviews.text:
Hi Kurtislee

Manly has recently been voted Australia's No 1 Beach - and we have two different coastlines: the harbour beaches which are safe for kayaking and exploring as well as the surf beaches for surfing and swimming. Both have great views and many different bars and restaurants with a huge variety of cuisines and price ranges.

Best regards

reviews.title: Stunning Beach
reviews.text:
Hi Gabriel999

Thanks for your 5* review of beautiful Manly beach - the ferry is truly one of the most spectacular routes in the world! There is always something happening on the Corso, the gateway from the Ferry to the beach and no one is ever disappointed when they arrive there!  Make sure you venture further either west to Queenscliff or east to Shelly Beach.

Best regards

reviews.title: Good place for water lovers :)
reviews.text:
Hi 493srividyar

Manly is much favoured by water-lovers - with clean clear water, great waves, safe harbourside beaches, it's the perfect destinations. So glad you had a great time.

Best regards

reviews.title: Had to Sea
reviews.text:
Hi ScottScooterW
Thanks for your great review of our coastal village of which we are very proud! The fast ferry is a great way to travel but if you are not in a hurry, be sure to try the traditional route on the green and yellow ferry. Manly is enjoyed by families from all walks of life, clean water, good waves and a great vibe. Glad you will return one day.
All the best

reviews.title: A Summers Day in May
reviews.text: 26 Degrees in the sun, and could not stroll down the walkway  without stopping for a dip in the ocean. Swam with the locals for a good half hour and really enjoyed the medium sized waves of the surf, the warm sun, the salt and sand between my toes. It took me straight back to the days of my youth. After my half hour rejuvenating soak in the sea, we ventured off to our next happy place, across the road, Manly Novotel for a cool beverage. A great place to sit and people watch, have a cold beverage or two and still enjoy the sun and surf.

reviews.title: All the Beaches
reviews.text:
Hi Thomas V
Thanks for your excellent review which of course we agree with! Manly boasts one of the best beaches in Australia, with great waves, good snorkelling as well as a safe harbour for kayaking or paddle boarding. Hope to see you back here again one day!

Best regards

reviews.title: Nice ferry trip
reviews.text: I took the fast ferry to Manly on the recommendation of a resident of the town. It is a lovely beach town with a strip of a street dedicated to pedestrian traffic with shops on both sides. The beach area has a wide pathway for pedestrians and several restaurants across the street. It was a fun way to spend a little time.

reviews.title: First choice beach
reviews.text: We had limited time in Sydney, but wanted to spend at least part of our time on a beach so we asked our friends who have already been what beach to visit and Manly was nearly unanimous.  After spending a morning on the beach, I would agree.  Take the time to visit this attractive beach.

reviews.title: Yeah its a beach...
reviews.text: Glad you enjoyed the ferry ride. Manly Beach has won Trip Advisor's Best Beach in Australia two years running, so do come back another time if we didn't meet your expectations first time around.

reviews.title: Perfect location by the beach.
reviews.text: I stayed at the Sebel Manly Beach which was a great spot to be . A friendly comfortable hotel with very pleasant young staff,clean spacious rooms and served by the Manly Wine restaurant for superb breakfast of fresh fruit and yoghurt with comb honey plus a wide menu to suit all tastes. Handy to very good shopping area and a fun place to be.  Pleasant walk along the beach to other very good restaurants and cafes.

reviews.title: Lovely manly
reviews.text:
Hi SusanMiss

Thank you for your great review of our beautiful seaside village of Manly, indeed, one of the best areas to visit. Next time you visit Manly, be sure to pop into the Visitors Information Centre on your right as you exit the ferry terminal and we can let you know some of the secret local's tips!
Best regards

reviews.title: Wonderful day
reviews.text: This beach is stunning in our opinion it was well worth the short trip across. Lovely golden sand with restaurants overlooking it. manly is a lovely place visit seriously  recommended

reviews.title: Great beach for all ages
reviews.text:
Hi Silv712
Thanks for your great review - if time is not an issue, why not try the iconic manly green and yellow ferry, a 30 minute ride from Circular Quay. Weekends are a good time to visit Manly with markets on both Saturday and Sunday and the Cabbage Tree Bay Coastal walk is one of the most splendid walks in Sydney. We hope to see you back here soon!
Best regards

reviews.title: Lovely setting
reviews.text:
Hi alseward53,

Thank you for visiting Manly and taking the time to review. So glad you had a good time in Manly, there is lots for everyone to do and see here. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Lovely ambience
reviews.text:
Hi Lawrence,

So glad you enjoyed your time in Manly. The ferry is a very relaxing way to get here and the Norfolk Pines along the beachfront are beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Busy and worth the visit
reviews.text:
Hi Llewellyn53,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the great review. So great to hear you enjoyed your time here. The Norfolk Pines along the beachfront are beautiful. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Sunday hang outs
reviews.text: We had friends over from France and we decided to go to Manly for a few hours.We all know it’s best to go to the beach when it’s a sunny and slightly more warmer day - but the day we went, it was pretty chilly and with some clouds.Nevertheless, Manly is a pretty beach - does remind me of Bondi but a lot more chilled.

reviews.title: A Really Fun and Relaxing Area
reviews.text: I went to Manly Beach twice during my business trip to Sydney in April 2019.  I took the fast ferry from Circular Quay and walked on The Corso.  Manly Beach is a really fun and relaxing place.  There are many restaurants on Steyne Street which is near the beach.  I enjoyed sitting on a bench and watching the beach and people passing by.  It was very relaxing.  There were many people on the beach and many surfers.  There was an area full of people playing volleyball.  I also enjoyed the pathway which is parallel to the beach and ocean.  I have been now to both Manly Beach and Bondi Beach.  Bondi is a beautiful place with a famous hiking trail.  But Manly Beach is the place to go if you want to have fun and just relax.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text:
Hi 928ozzied,

Thank you for visiting Manly and the great review. Manly is definately the right place to come to relax. So glad you enjoyed your time here & hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Good people watching
reviews.text: We spent several hours at this beach.  There are bath houses you can change into/out fo baithing suits.  In addition, there are several resturants that overlook the beach..  Perfect place to enjoy a beer and do some people watching!

reviews.title: The most enjoyable beach
reviews.text: The beach was very clean and the waters inviting. Had a great time playing in the water along with kids. The sand on the beach is lovely and wants you to be there all day. It was buzzing with life and also had a small wedding taking place. But the place is so big for everyone that you can still find your place.

reviews.title: What a Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: Manly Beach is a very beautiful beach.  It‘s beautiful sands fill most of the bay.  Just accross the street are a number of coffee houses and small restaurants, along with shops and bars.  It’s a very nice beach town atmosphere and would recommend experiencing it to my family and friends.

reviews.title: A must see
reviews.text:
Hi SteveandVince,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the fabulous review. The ferry is a lovely relaxing way to get here and see Sydney Harbour on the way. So glad you enjoyed your time here and hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: fun at the beach
reviews.text:
Hi Gary, 
We are so happy you enjoyed your time exploring Manly and you had a great time playing in the waves. 
Thanks for the awesome Review! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Ok, But
reviews.text: The beach itself was nice. But there was no place to sit except in the sand.  The waves that day were small, so not surfers.Went across the road to Manley Wines restaurant, food was awful, tasted of propane (the bar-b-que) service was not to say the least.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: In my opinion Manly Beach was more impressive than Bondi Beach. The ferry was really easy to catch and they even offer a fast service. Manly didn’t have the crowds that most other areas of Sydney draws and the beach was impressive too. Could easily spend a few hours exploring the beach, town and local market here.

reviews.title: Worthwhile
reviews.text: There were 3 things I liked about Sydney: 1) the Waterfront, 2) Blue Mountains, and 3) Manly Beach.  Manly Beach has it all--a beautiful beach, a walking path to Shelly Beach (which is another beautiful beach!), and a sea coastal town.  The boat ride from Sydney's harbor to Manly Beach was great too!

reviews.title: Pretty but busy
reviews.text:
Hi Irene, 
Thanks for the review! 
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Best Beach, great location. Walking trails close by, food and bars are of abundance and is a lot more chilled than the eastern suburb beaches. More calming especially after jumping off a ferry.

reviews.title: Its a hidden gem
reviews.text: It starts with a ferry ride, or a long way car journey. The boat takes you past the opera house, up close and personal, and all the bays along the way to the heads. Then you walk through the streets a short distance, past the gelato bars etc, then cross the beach front road and you're on the sand. It has sun and surf, the lifesavers are out looking out for bathers. Its got the pavillions and old style milk bars. A great place to have a swim and spend the day. You can stay overnight right at the beach if you want to. I was tempted.

reviews.title: Iconic Manly
reviews.text:
Hi Stephen
Thank you for the awesome review! 
We are proud of our beautiful beaches and we are glad you enjoyed your time here in Manly. 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: You can travel all around the world and then hefe in our backyard is the most lovely beach with excellent restaurants and such a magical atmosphere.  Buy and ice cream and some fish n chips and sit down and watch the serenity of this lovely area.

reviews.title: use the ferry to go to manly
reviews.text: to go to manly beach you can catch the bus from chatswood station or the ferry from circular quay.The Many beach has a good Place for Swimming and has excellent Hotel.

reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.text: I love my day at manly beach, it is stunning to vist via the ferry from sydney.  the beach is long and beautiful.

reviews.title: Excellent long stretch of beach
reviews.text:
Hi Mark,
We are happy you enjoyed Manly and our beautiful Manly beach!
Next time pop into our Information Centre at the wharf and we will give you some great tips about the best walks and coffee shops in the area ;)

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: Manley beach
reviews.text:
Yes, the views of Sydney Harbour from the Manly ferry are definitely amazing! Did you know that our beautiful Manly beach has been voted the number 1 beach in Australia two years in a row? 

We are happy you enjoyed your time here and hope to see you back soon :) 

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: Take a ferry here!
reviews.text:
Yes, yes, yes! Manly is definitely a perfect place to admire the views on our beautiful Sydney Harbour! 
We hope you enjoyed the beaches as well: the impressive Manly beach, the cosy Shelly beach (perfect for snorkeling), the secluded Collins beach, the haunted Quarantine Beach and many more.
If not, make sure you come and visit us soon again!

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: Sun, Sand & Surf
reviews.text: Took a day out to Manly and what a fantastic day it was. Great town and a lovely promenade to stroll along and stop to watch all the surfing activity on the pristine beach. Had a coffee or three on the front and Fish & Chips for lunch. Took the harbour City Ferry from Circular key which took 30 minutes and cost $15.oo return. One of the highlights of my stay in Sydney.

reviews.title: A clean beach
reviews.text:
Hi Beatrice,
You are so right! Our beautiful Manly beach is the best place to relax and connect with nature while having a nice coffee or lunch. Have you walked to Shelly Beach? It's only 20 minutes from the Manly wharf on the way to North Head - another amazing place to visit. Maybe you will feel like exploring it next time?

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: Worth a stopover.
reviews.text:
Hi Fathimad,
You had a very good idea with hiring bikes - it is a great way of visiting Manly! You can ride along the beach side or/and explore North Head: beautiful views and exercise all in one. Our Manly ferry is iconic to us - we are happy you enjoyed the ride :)
Make sure you visit our information center at the wharf next time you're in Manly! We promise to give you some great tips on how to best explore the area.

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: A must-do!
reviews.text: A trip to Sydney is not complete without getting the ferry to Manly from Circular Quay!When you arrive and get off the ferry, head up through the main  pedestrianised street towards the ocean and the beach.It’s a very chilled beach in my opinion. Tree lined and plenty of room to sit and enjoy the views and the sea.Lifeguards patrol the beach and watch the swimmers swimming between the flags.Plenty of places to get food and drink or take a picnic!

reviews.title: Ferry to Manly
reviews.text: Our family of 6 visited Manly by taking the ferry from Circular Quay. The journey was half the fun. It was great to visit this iconic beach, The Corso and take in some of the walks. The weather was not kind though - a bit blustery and cool. It was enough for me to avoid the water, but the kids were not put off. I recommend doing the Cabbage Tree Bay coastal walk and even get to North Head if you have the time.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text:
Hi Kevin,
Thanks for a great review! It's true - we are very lucky to live in such a beautiful, relaxing and safe place and we are very happy to share it all with our visitors!
And yes, we've got around 150 great coffee shops and restaurants in Manly! 
Have you walked from Manly to North Head or to Spit? If not, make sure you do next time! And don't forget to pop into our visitor information centre at the wharf for more tips about exploring Manly :)

Much Manly Love

reviews.title: Sooo many beaches
reviews.text: Once you get off the ferry the map is your best guide. It tells you what beaches are close and how far the walks are if you plan to explore. Whats great is the smaller beaches are filled with locals not overly crowded. You can pick a spot grab some lunch or read a book.

reviews.title: The ferry ride is fun too.
reviews.text: You go to Manly to see the surfers and the famous beach town.It is full of backpackers and beach shops along with a good choice of restaurants with ocean views.

reviews.title: Just beautiful
reviews.text:
Hi Tina
Glad you enjoyed your stay in Manly. It's true, we have one of the most beautiful beaches in Sydney. If you come back, make sure you pop into the Visitors Information Centre for some secret tips on where the locals hang out!
Cheers

reviews.title: Lovely ferry trip over.
reviews.text: It was a HOT HOT day and the ferry ride was refreshing but it was too hot to sit on the beach and most people we snatching up the little available tree-shaded areas. Sat under the trees in Manly Square and watched several pairs of large Cockatoos - very entertaining even though it gave me a stiff neck looking high in the canopies!!

reviews.title: Beach Drive
reviews.text:
Hi Tracyann
Thank you for your lovely review of our beautiful laid-back beach. Another option could be to drive to Watsons Bay and hop on a ferry to Manly. It's only 15 minutes! Make sure you pop into our friendly Visitors Information Centre on your right as you exit the ferry terminal.
cheers

reviews.title: Warm water, friendly atmosphere,  limited safe swimming area
reviews.text:
Hi  Chris
So glad you had a lovely time on the beach - if you have young ones, Shelly Beach (a stunning 20 minute walk) or one of the Harbour beaches provide very safe, calm waters for paddling. Umbrellas can be easily hired at the beach if you are struggling with the heat. We hope to see you again one day.
Cheers

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text:
Hi WorldwideReviews1
Thanks for your 5* review - it's true - we have over 150 cafes to choose from and a wide-variety of ice-cream shops. Great beaches to swim at and some stunning scenic walks. Hope to see you back here again one day!
Cheers

reviews.title: A not-too-crowded spot to enjoy the Sydney beach scene.
reviews.text:
Hi Harry
Thanks for your 5* review and great summary of our beautiful seaside village, Manly! If you return, be sure to pop into the Visitors Information Centre on your right as you leave the ferry to grab a map and some secret local tips on where to go!
Cheers

reviews.title: A quick Ferry trip
reviews.text: This was a lovely day trip on the ferry. The collection of shops is interesting to look around and the beach is fantastic. Although we did not swim we wish we had! Lots of surfing to watch and lovely eateries.

reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.text: Go there on a weekend - lots of people but it gives you an insight into the "Aussie way of Life". Families, singles, students, all on the waterfront enjoying the sea and the beach.At the end of Manly beach you find the Life Saving Club - most interesting!

reviews.title: beautiful location
reviews.text:
Hi vicpk

Glad you enjoyed your ferry ride to our beautiful seaside village, Manly. Make sure you wander down the side alleys as there are a large variety of shops tucked away.
Cheers

reviews.title: To See and be Seen
reviews.text:
Hi 
Pedro00

Glad you had a great time appreciating our iconic beach life! There is so much going on in Manly from beautiful scenic walks, water activities or experiencing culinary delights at the many restaurants and cafes.
Cheers

reviews.title: Fun Place to Visit!
reviews.text: My husband and I took the ferry out to Manly Beach on our last day in Sydney and we're so glad we did. The ferry ride from Circular Quay gave great views of the different parts of the city and the shops on The Corso were fun to pop into. We spent a couple of hours people watching from the walkway adjacent to the beach and then had a FABULOUS lunch at The Pantry with a great view of the beach and surfers.

reviews.title: Give it a go
reviews.text: Take the ferry to manly only 20 minutes. Well worth the trip, you get to see the harbour and the ferries are great take the slow or fast one.When you arrive at manly only a short walk to the beach.Plenty to see heaps of shops and eatery’s. If you want a swim take your togs and a towel.

reviews.title: Really good!
reviews.text: We visited manly beach and really enjoyed it. Benches are lined up behind the beach and lifeguards are scattered ever so often. In addition you can hire body/surf boards.

reviews.title: Manly
reviews.text:
Hi Phil, 
Thanks for the great review! 
You are right we have a lot more activities than Bondi. 
We are the best beach in Australia for a reason. 
Hope to see you around Manly again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Don’t go to Sydney without visiting Manly
reviews.text: We hopped the fast boat to Manly because we had been advised to do so. Really glad we did. Visiting Manly adds a whole different dimension to your stay in Sydney. Once you’ve done the iconic photos around the harbour etc etc it’s time for a change of pace. Manly is a really cool and interesting resort town with a great beach and a cool atmosphere. We really loved it. Manly was definitely a high point of our stay in Sydney.

reviews.title: "My beach"
reviews.text: Watching the waves roll gently on the beach, a lovely sandy beach. A great place to walk, sit on the boulevard, watching people enjoying it all.A very nice great beach, space enough to sit, lay down. Or take a walk to shelly beach.

reviews.title: Big busy, sandy beach.  Loved the walk over as much as the beach
reviews.text:
Hi Nedelakttraveler, 
Thanks for the review! 
We are glad you had a great time in Manly! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Worth the trip!
reviews.text: I heard so many folk tell me that Bondi was such a big disappointment, that I decided to investigate Manly instead. And I am so pleased that I did. When you disembark the ferry, there are so many street side cafes and restaurants to visit, plus some interesting shops selling gifts that are slightly more unusual. Then as you walk along, you catch sight of the famous Manly beach. It invites you just to sit and watch the world go by. And I recommend you do just that !!!

reviews.title: Visit Manly
reviews.text:
Hi Jimstarios, 
Thanks for the review! 
You are right, the walk to Shelly Beach is amazing and the swimming there is even better. 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Favourite day in sydney
reviews.text: Take your swimmers and snorkel and mask for a day trip here the food is great you can go snorkeling learn to surf and walk amongst nature it is lovely there

reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.text:
Hi John, 
Thanks for the review!
You are right the Manly Ferry is the easiest way to come to Manly! 
Hope to see you in Manly again soon! 
Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Best Beach
reviews.text:
Hi Lauradc13,

We have been voted the best beach in Australia for the last couple of years. 
Next time try wondering our beautiful  side streets. 
Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Don't miss this stop!
reviews.text:
Hi Medisec1, 
Thanks for the review!
