We hope to see you again soon! 
Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Beautiful and well developed
reviews.text:
Hi shanenz,

So glad you had a great time here and enjoyed what Manly has to offer. The ferry is a very relaxing way to get around. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Fun excursion
reviews.text: Took the ferry from Sydney to Manley Beach. Fun day of exploring. Stumbled upon a yacht club that offered day memberships, where we enjoyed wine & lunch.  Busy beach where we waded knee high (forgot our suits) in the Tasman Sea. BEAUTIFUL.

reviews.title: My favorite beach in Sydney
reviews.text:
Hi ttocsnodrog_2000,

So nice to hear you felt welcome and had a nice time in Manly. we are very lucky it is a special place. Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you, 

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Lovely day out.
reviews.text:
Hi Nick C,

Great to hear about your Manly experience and for taking the time to review. It sounds like you had a good day.  The ferry is a very relaxing way to get here for both travellers and locals.

Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Lovely walk along the beach
reviews.text: We got the ferry over from Sydney harbour, which was easy and quite cheap at $7.51 each way. We got off the ferry and walked straight to Manly beach, it is lovely walking from one end to the other- lots of places to eat and drink. The beach wasn’t too busy which was nice. Swimming flags at two ends of the beach and also lifeguards along the whole of it. Felt stay going in the water

reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.text:
Hi Badgaroo, 
Thanks for taking the time to leave a review! 
We are glad you had a great time exploring our beautiful Manly Beach. 
Hope to see you again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Recommended!
reviews.text: If you have the time, definitely take the Fast Ferry to Manly. Just lovely to be out of the busy city in a beachy area. In the weekends it is crowded at Manly, but still enjoyable. Some nice restaurants and shops if you walk from the ferry to Manly beach itself.

reviews.title: Vacation in Australia
reviews.text:
Hi Jodeed2013,
We are glad you had such a great holiday in Australia! 
Hope to see you again here soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Well worth the visit
reviews.text: Have visited Sydney many times . Always enjoy the trip to Manly. Your'e in a different world over there. The ferry trip alone is well worth the price and the atmosphere in Manly is totally different to Sydney. Value for money and to experience something different  I thoroughly recommend this trip.

reviews.title: Very nice beach and location for walking around
reviews.text:
Hi NatganSin, 
Thanks for taking the time to leave a review! 
It sounds like you had an amazing day in Manly! 
Sunday is one of our busiest days as it is the cheapest day to travel on the Opal card. 
We hope to see you again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Fantastic beach
reviews.text: Said to be the best beach in Sydney (better than Bondi) we made a couple of trips there.To get there you take the fast ferry  across the harbour to Manley wharf and walk about 300 m across to the ocean side. The beach is magnificent stretch of golden sand.When we  were  there the ocean was relatively calm but on a good day it would be packed with surfers. There were many shops,cafes,bars and takeaways on the road that runs alongside the beach.Fish and chips is just as popular thrre as in the UK.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Manly is an iconic beach on the Northside with a great walk from Queenscliff to Shelley beach. Great pubs and restaurants close by and great people watching

reviews.title: Take the ferry to Manly
reviews.text: When we landed at Manly we saw a small beach and thought "Is this it?" A little disappointed. However after speaking to a lovely lady in the Information Centre she directed us to the main shopping street and to the "real" beach. It was beautiful! The beach was clean and well looked after. We walked along the  promenade around the headland. Make sure you do not stray onto the bike path as they ride quite fast. Just have your wits about you, otherwise a lovely walk. Lots of nice shops and fish and chip restaurants.

reviews.title: One of Austrailia's best beaches
reviews.text: While visiting Sydney we kept hearing that Bondi Beach was the best around.  Well, we found Manly to be much more exciting and vibrant than Bondi.  Manly was much easier to reach from downtown Sydney, where you can hop a ferry for a short ride across the bay and disembark in a fun beach resort town.  sorry also to say that Bondi is not that easy to reach via public transportaion.

reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.text:
Hi Jsncruz, 
We are sorry you didn't enjoy your time in Manly. You must of caught Manly on a bad day. 
There is loads to do here in Manly. There are awesome walks or bike routes up to North Head or to Shelly Beach or towards the Spit Bridge. We also have Markets on the weekends and a gorgeous snorkeling area. 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Happy Day
reviews.text:
Hi reddim2016,
We are glad you enjoyed your time in Manly! 
You are right! It is such a great way to get a break from the City! 
The ferry is one of our favourite way to get to get around. 
We hope to see you in Manly again soon! 

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: Nice beach in Australia
reviews.text: Though we were not in Sydney for beach experience, but Manly turned out to be a decent experience. Nice surfing waves and horde of surfers made a great spectacle to watch. We enjoyed the food in a nearby restaurant and there are lots of them near the beach. Try to avoid weekends as it can get crowded.

reviews.title: Simply Stunning!
reviews.text: Visited Manly today after a long absence and was struck once again by how beautiful it is and how picturesque the long beaches and cafes are. Great place to visit and enjoy the best of Sydney Harbour whilst enjoying a gorgeous drink with a good friend.

reviews.title: Not great for chilling
reviews.text: Manly beach lets you rent out umbrellas and a sun lounger, but the waves are quite strong and so the swimming isn't really relaxing and better suited towards surfers.Shelly beach down the path, is better for swimmers, but doesn't have any umbrellas or sun loungers to hire so it's not as relaxing when you are not swimming.

reviews.title: One of the best things you can do in life anywhere, ever
reviews.text: Taking the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly Wharf and exploring Manly is not only one of the nicest things you can do in Sydney and Australia, but in my opinion anywhere in the world. The ferry trip gives you some of the best views of the Opera House and the Harbour Bay. Manly itself is super relaxed, with one of the cleanest beaches, good for surfers, nice restaurants and hotels around. The walk to Shelly Beach and North Head is simply a lovely experience. Would recommend it to everybody.

reviews.title: Tourist trap
reviews.text:

So glad you enjoyed the iconic ferry ride across to Manly - you should have popped into the Visitors Information Centre located on the Manly Forecourt for some fantastic tips about some of the great world-class restaurants and wine bars that can be found in our beautiful seaside village. Best regards

reviews.title: A great place to relax
reviews.text:
Hi SunnyOli
There are so many different beaches to visit in Manly, make a sure you head down to Shelly Beach or perhaps in the opposite direction to Queenscliff Beach if the main beach feels too crowded for your liking. It's true there is a huge variety of restaurants in both directions and fantastic bars/cafes to grab a drink. Very relaxing!

Best regards

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text:
Dear witcheshouse

Thank you for your fantastic review - so glad you had a fantastic time in our seaside village called Manly. We do have a huge variety of restaurants, bars and cafes serving a huge variety of cuisines from Vegan to kangaroo burgers - there is a food type for everyone. If you are heading here from the City, make sure you take the spectacular scenic ferry ride.
Best regards

reviews.title: Iconic historic and busy beach.
reviews.text: Love visiting Manly Beach, it is always buzzing with people. The Norfolk Pines lining the shore, the lifeguards on duty, the busy cafe life and street markets make this always interesting. There are often little children learning to surf (in classes). The walk to Shelley Beach is a Must-Do. Swimming at Shelley Beach is safer as it is more protected, but one can snorkel along this coast, or swim in the sea-pool, or eat at the cafes along the walk.

reviews.title: Ferry was on time and well worth it
reviews.text: Love going over to Manly it is a beautiful ferry ride...the staff on the ferries are great and helpful......buy a return ticket.....you can walk down the Main Street to the beach and it is promenade is rather great taking....well worth a visit

reviews.title: Loved everything about it!
reviews.text: With only 2.5 days in Sydney we chose this as one of our stops, and I’m so glad we did!  From hotel in The Rocks area, took #3 ferry to Manly. Beautiful harbor views! Short walk to beach. Beach itself was busy but it didn’t feel crazy uncomfortable. Lots of locals. Still plenty of room to yourself on a Wednesday afternoon. Swim areas separate from surfing. Rented boogie boards for 1hr from a beach vendor. So much fun!!!!! Waves were absolutely perfect. Had a blast! Fresh water showers available right off the beach. Walked to deVita pizzeria & took it to go. So good! On way back at sunset we ate by the ferries on the grassy area & watched people play Supball (played in water on paddle boards) - very entertaining !

reviews.title: Huge Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: The beach appears to be one of the favorites of the people of Sydney.  It is a huge beach with a nice promenade. There are sections for swimmers and for surfers.  The beach is easy to get to from Sydney CBD via the Manly ferry which runs every 30 minutes and is a 35 minute trip which in itself has beautiful views of the city, the opera house, the bridge and the harbour opening to the ocean (beautiful cliffs). There are restrooms on the beach and plenty of places to eat in Manly.

reviews.title: Nice but don't get out of your way to visit.
reviews.text: Nice beach with various activities. Can get there via public ferry from Circular Quay (35 min. trip). We've seen nicer beaches so if are not looking for places to visit try another beach or activity.

reviews.title: Manley Beach
reviews.text: Manly Beach in Sydney, Australia is a beautiful beach and well worth the ferry ride from the Sydney Harbour to Manley.  The shopping area reminded me of LaJolla, Calif., with many restaurants and lovely shops.

reviews.title: Just perfect for a Couples Day out
reviews.text:
Hi Toni G,

Thank you for visiting Manly and for the wonderful review. 

The beaches in Manly are perfect for learning to surf or spending the day swimming and relaxing.

Along the foreshore , there is a selection of cafes pubs and wine bars with excellent cuisine.

An excellent way to experience Manly is to rent a bike and explore the dedicated bike paths and off road trails.

The North Head National Park is another must-see.

And yes, the ferry is a great way to get here.

Hope to see you again soon.

Thank you,

reviews.title: Nice ferry ride from Circular Quay
reviews.text: We took an afternoon ferry from Circular Quay to Manly and walked along the store lined promenade to the beach.  Easy ten minute walk to the beach.  We had dinner at a hip Japanese restaurant along the beach and then took the ferry back at night for a completely different view of the Sydney skyline.  If you plan two or more ferry round trips, it is worth it to get a Opal card at the transit center in Circular Quay.  The card is free but you are required to purchase at least $10 worth of value to start.  It can be used on all public transport and provides discounted fares.  It also has a daily cap of around $15  which would really save you a significant amount on the aforementioned ferry trips if they were both the same day.  Turango Zoo and Darling Harbor would be potential trips.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text:
Hi Jan H

Thanks for your great review - Manly is so easy to access from the City and the ferry is an iconic trip across the water. Glad you enjoyed all that Manly has to offer, beaches, surf, shops and cafes to name a few. Next time you return, be sure to pop in to the Visitors Info Centre for some local tips!

Cheers

reviews.title: Cosmopolitan Excellence,
reviews.text:
Hi Mary O

Thank you for your great review. Manly has recently been nominated one of Australia's favourite beaches - did you know that it is also possible to try surfing yourself? There is an excellent surf school where one can either join a small group or have an individual lesson. Next time you come to Manly, make sure you call into the Visitors Information Centre where this can be organised for you at no extra charge!

Cheers

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text:
Hi Charles K

Did you know that there are three ferry options to take to Manly from Sydney? If you are in a rush, the private ferry takes 18 minutes and if time is not a problem, take the leisurely 30 minute public ferry. As well as many interesting and varied restaurants on the waterfront, there are also a host of small cafes and pubs tucked away in the back streets of Manly.

Hope to see you back in Manly again one day!

Cheers

reviews.title: Too many people
reviews.text:
Hi Tranzactnow,

Thanks, 
Manly Visitor Information Centre

reviews.title: So relaxing and refreshing
reviews.text: If you want a quick out of City getaway, then one ferry ride away you’ll be in Manly beach. We bought our tickets the day itself and didn’t have any issues going in and back to Sydney. I find it so relaxing and refreshing to just walk around the beach, do a little shopping at market/mall area if you get tired of walking in the sand. So much to do in this lovely town. It was their fall season when we came in April but we still managed to swam on the beach. We braved the chilly water!

reviews.title: Manly Beach
reviews.text: One of must-see places when you are visiting Sydney even for 2 or 3 days. It's easy to reach by taking a ferry from the wharf near Sydney Opera House by using Opal card. It's a very beautiful beach that you will want to swim in, walk along the seaside or just seat on a bench and relax.

reviews.title: Surfers
reviews.text: As I had a busy schedule and so much to fit in I spent an hour at the beach watching the surfers in the waves.Its very clean, wasnt that busy and lots of blue jellyfish washing up with the tide.There were plenty people sunbathing and it's got a nice pedestrian footpath above it.Looked like they were erecting temporary stands in the middle for an event, possibly volleyball. Wish I'd had longer to spend here, my friend told me this is better than Bondi as that's were all the tourists go to.It has lifeguards

reviews.title: Seaside wonder downunder
reviews.text: Manly Beach is a gem. It is about 30 minutes ride by passenger ferry from Circular Quay in Sydney. The ferry ride is great with many picture taking opportunities. Unlike Sydney, Manly is far more laid back. A ten minute walk along a traffic free street ends in Manly beach. Shops, bars, and coffee shops are plentiful. Surfers, sailors and sun bathers make a good floorshow. A great half day visit from Sydney.

You Come visit us and truly live like a local - with so many delicious food options for every taste and loads of amazing outdoor activities to enjoy and explore!

Manly is such a beautiful natural wonderland to relax and unwind.

Thanks

reviews.text:

reviews.title: A Great and Safe Sydney Beach
reviews.text: Manly Beach is one of my favorites. Very popular but lots of space for all. Great waves for adults and children. Moderate waves for surfers. Great safety patrols with lots well-maintained equipment and well-trained people. Great facilities at the beach, including shady spots amongst the Norfolk Pine Trees and seating lots of seating benches. Great restaurants and shopping just across from the beach. Great transport from Circular Quay and return by NSW Ferries. .

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text:
Hi Celero, 

Thank you for taking the time to write a review. We are glad you enjoyed your visit to Manly. We completely agree, Shelly Beach is awesome for snorkeling - next time you could do a snorkeling tour to see the best of Shelly Beaches waters. 

We hope to see you next time! 

Love,  
Manly

reviews.title: Lovely spot to enjoy some sun
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly and walked across to the beach. The beach is lovely, seemed much nicer than Bondi especially since there are shops and restaurants right across from the beach. We had a very nice fish and chips lunch. The ferry ride to and from is spectacular with some of the best views of Sydney from the water.

reviews.title: A Gem
reviews.text: A wonderful sheltered beach just a short walk from the Sydney harbor Manly ferry station.  Manly Beach is not a popular - yet as Bondi Beach, but is every bit a nice - if not nicer.  A must see if you have the time when you visit. Remember to swim between the flags.  It also has a natural water preserve for snorkeling.

reviews.title: Friendly and fun
reviews.text:
Hi Florence195
Thanks for your great review of Manly Beach - so glad that it made your trip even more special. We are very lucky to have a lovely community of caring people (including those at the surf club) and the vibe can definitely be felt by visitors!
Cheers

reviews.title: Used the ferry system to get there from Circular Quay
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quay over to Manly Beach, a very enjoyable ride with beautiful scenery. Lots of stores and restaurants located in the area of the beach. Lovely beach.

reviews.title: Beauty and Sun
reviews.text: Manly Beach is so beautiful. There are walks you can take along the beach and there is Shelley Beach which is especially for families. You must spend the day there.

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: Went to Manly on the Fast Ferry from Circular Quay, great trip seeing the Sydney skyline, Opera House and Bridge. Ferry port very clean and well signposted somyou find your way around quite easily.  Manley is great for shopping with a shop where you are able to buy items made by the Aboriginal people, spent quite a long time in there selecting pieces! Had lunch at one of the many pavement cafes and the food was excellent. The beach is lovely and on the day we were there had a lovely light ocean breeze. Lovely town with something for everyone

reviews.title: A Great Beach and Atmosphere
reviews.text:
Hi boloca
Thanks for your great review - there are so many activities on offer as you discovered, as well as bike riding, snorkelling in the protected waters of Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - the list is extensive. We also have over 150 different eateries to try out!
Please come again one day soon!
Cheers

reviews.title: Walk From Shelly Beach Manly to North Curl Curl
reviews.text: This is a fantastic walk with great walk ways unbelievable views and even coffee shops all over the place if you need a break. Clean water fountains are provided free for you to refill your bottles and your right next to the ocean that is crystal clean. You really need to do this ???

reviews.title: A different perspective
reviews.text:
Hi David A11958

Thanks for taking the time to review Manly Beach - the ferry is certainly one of the most iconic journeys on offer - once you arrive in Manly, the beach is only a five minute walk down the Corso and there are many ocean or harbour view places to enjoy a beer or two!
Cheers

reviews.title: day trip
reviews.text: Able to ferry to beach from the Rocks area had lunch at corner of beach shopping area excellent fish and chips then to the beach for fun in the sun. able to watch surfers and lounge in chairs available to rent.

reviews.title: Fish and chips at the beach.
reviews.text:
Hi GAGASydney

Thanks for your great review - fish and chips always tastes so much better at Manly Beach  - next time make sure you walk down to Shelly Beach to experience the wonderful views from the headland.
Cheers

reviews.title: Amazing place to spend the day
reviews.text:
Hi danielkohen
Thanks for your great review - Manly Beach is a great place to be even if you are on your own!  Shelly Beach which is a short walk along a stunning promenade, is nearly always a very safe place to swim, protected by a beautiful headland from any dangerous rips. There is also a full enclosed sea pool along the way.
Hope to see you again one day soon.
Cheers

reviews.title: Breath taking
reviews.text:
Hi shaunr464
Thanks for your great review - Manly is certainly one of the most popular beaches but... there are more and some within walking distance or a short bus ride away once you arrive here. Be sure to visit some of the incredible eateries/cafes where you can sample a huge varieties of cuisine, from poke bowls to Japanese delicacies at one of our 5* fine-dining restaurants.
Cheers

reviews.title: Lacking
reviews.text:
Hi Peter R
So sorry you were disappointed with your visit. Next time, make sure you pop into the Manly Visitors Information Centre, where the locals can give you some of their tips on where to go and what to do - yes there are many tourists that visit here but there are still many unique businesses run by locals that we can let you know about!
Cheers

reviews.title: Vwey nice beach, I love the tree lined streets and Volleyball venue.
reviews.text: We rode out to Manly and Manly Beach yesterday, It was nice to get out of the city.  Manly is a very nice beach, I have been to many others that I preferred, but this is definitely the nicest beach I have been to here in Australia.  The city is older, having been revised numerous times over the last 150 or so years (the first white man got here in 1788).  There is a plethora of stores, bars, cafes to choose from, There is a beach volleyball tournament going on so the venue may or may not look like this all the time.  Well worth a look, plus the ferry ride over thru the harbour area is great!

reviews.title: Nice beach for walking but definitely not the best beach in the world
reviews.text: I have been to countless of beaches, I won't agree Manly to be the best beach in the world. I was living in Sydney, walking distance to Balmoral beach, which is more quieter and cater more for local and hosted several great event (wine testing).Manly beach is good for surfers but very touristy place. It is good for a walk and exploring the beach while watching the surfers. It is also good for family with kids who interested on exploring Manly Sea life sanctuary. But definitely not a must see place in Sydney.

reviews.title: Definitely one of the best beaches in Australia, if not the world
reviews.text: I guess it comes into a fact that Australians like to whinge, second to British. Manly Beach is definitely one of the best in Australia, if not the world. Take ferry from Circular Quay (Sydney Opera House) to Manly, and enjoy the whole package, the whole experience.

reviews.title: Must see when in Sydney
reviews.text: Felt compelled to write this after seeing this beach getting a bad review. From my experience, it is safe to swim, the water is crystal clear and facilities excellent. I feel lucky to have access to this piece of heaven, and hope that every visitor has the time to visit.

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quay to Manly, it’s easy to find the beach once out of the ferry terminal cross the road and walk straight down the street and you will find the beach.It’s a decent sized beach and has all the facilities required for a day at the beach.The Volleyfest stadium is set up ready for the 1st of March.There is a great selection of restaurants and cafes close to the beach.

reviews.title: Surfs up!
reviews.text: Take the ferry to Manly from Circular quay, crops straight over the main road and five minutes later you are in surfers heaven. Now I'm not one of those but just to sit down and watch is great, especially if you have just had some fish and chips. The views out to sea are glorious and is a picture perfect Australian csene

reviews.title: Very nice day at Manly
reviews.text: We didn't have time to do both Bondi and Manly so we had to choose. We ended up going with Manly because it was easily accessible by ferry. We never did get to Bondi but we throughly enjoyed at day at Manly. Great restaurants and coffee shops and we enjoyed strolling the walkway along the shoreline. Very beautiful.

reviews.title: Nice beach with some good restaurants nearby
reviews.text: On a hot day, you can't beat a cold beer and a walk along Manley Beach. The ferry drops you off about 1K from the beach (just walk through downtown Manley).

reviews.title: Windy beach
reviews.text: We came here using the manly ferry and enjoyed sitting on the bench. Nice to enjoy our fish and chips while taking in the sea views and enjoying the cool sea air.

reviews.title: A fine day out
reviews.text: The town and beaches are great and easily reached from the city by ferry. Lots of places to grab lunch or dinner and some good walks - grab a map from the information centre just outside the wharf.

reviews.title: Great Beach. Better than Bondi!
reviews.text: Worth a trip from Circular Quay on the ferry. 10 min walk along The Corsica. Plenty of shops, bars and cafes near to the beach. Esplanade and a grass area behind the beach if you don’t like the sand.

reviews.title: Ferry to Manly
reviews.text: Lovely trip across the harbour.  Ferry packed but still seating available.   Every ferry that came in was packed.  Hot Sunday afternoon lots of bare skin on display

reviews.title: Stunning beach!
reviews.text: Manly beach is both relaxing with stunning views around.. its a great place to take in and watch the world go by.. highly recommend a visit for lunch and a relaxing day at the beach..

reviews.title: If you can only do one - do Manly!
reviews.text: Great beaches come in many forms.  This one is not quiet and secluded for sure, but it is everything else you might want.  Beautiful, swimming, surfing, hundreds of easily walkable promenade shops, fun local vendors and artists, restaurants that span from simple / local to upscale - but dozens of delicious options.  Seems that Manly is always busy and crowded - but it’s all about energy, buzz and attitude.  An ideal beach town atmosphere.  Candidly, if you have time to visit only one beach.....take the ferry to Manly, it’s 100x better than Bondi.  Pls let me know if you find this helpful.

reviews.title: Give me Manly over Bondi any day
reviews.text: Manly has a lovely laid-back village atmosphere and a gorgeous beach. In my view Manly brings you everything Bondi can without having to battle the crowds.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: If you're looking for a beach in Sydney to visit then Manly in the one. Get the ferry from Circular Quay and it's super easy to reach. It's a far nicer beach than Bondi and you can set yourself up at one of the pubs and easily spend a day watching the world go by. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: Iconic Bondi Beach is known around the world, but Manly residents claim that their beach knocks the socks off Bondi.It actually stretches from Queenscliff Beach to the north, through Manly Beach proper, and ends in Shelley Beach, a very popular spot for snorkeling among the reefs.Many Beach is lined with stately Norfolk Island Pines.The beach is hugely popular with locals and tourists, and at weekends the Manly Ferry is kept busy transporting hundreds of tourists to Manly, where they plod their way through The Corso to Manly Beach.Swin, sunbath, or just sit and take it all in.

reviews.title: A Lovely Ferry Ride to this Paradise Part of Sydney
reviews.text: I have come to Manly many times and loved each visit. The sandy beaches are picture perfect. Just love to walk around the harbor for a leisurely walk, shopping and dining. The ferry ride from Circular Quay is just a short 30 minute cruise for under $8 U.S. The ferry terminal is just a few steps from the cruise ship terminal and runs on the half-hour. BOTTOM LINE: Beautiful area to visit. Ferries can run very full to this port on weekends and holidays. Love shopping in the area for souvenirs and groceries. I could live here! The Pacific ocean is only a short walk away to even more beautiful sandy beaches. Almost paradise! Worth your visit. MY RATING: 10/10.

reviews.title: Now that’s a beach!
reviews.text: We took the fast ferry from the circular quay to Manley today. Having been to Bondi Beach on the Hop on Hop off and finding it hugely disappointing, Manly is amazing! Three beaches, every restaurant and souvenir shop imaginable and mikes of sandy beach! The surf is incredible and there was every kind of surfer there from kids to ancient. Would love to give the water a try but beware, it’s cold! The water in Maui is about 85 deg. The water here is about 70 deg. Would think you need a wet suit, but maybe I’m a wuss.

reviews.title: Ehjoy the Day or night
reviews.text: Manly beach is a short ferry ride away from Sydney. Something different if youre looking to get away from the city. Cute little shops, great food, and beautiful waterfront. If you want to avoid crowds I highly recommend going sooner than later

reviews.title: Shop and Eat in Manly Beach!
reviews.text: Take the ferry from Sydney to Manly Beach!  A wonderful way to see it all!  Once you arrive take time to stroll the cross and shop and then hit the beach for eats!  I loved The Pantry at Manly Beach with an oceanside table.  It was a spectacular afternoon.

reviews.title: Sydney Harbour or Pacific Ocean?
reviews.text: Has to be done, ferry from Circular Quays to Manly, the short walk through the town to the magnificent sandy beach on the Pacific side. Good toilets and plenty of shade to sit in on the prom by the trees. Plenty of restaurants, ice cream, bars and shops to suit all. Flat walks along the prom and round to Shelly Bay maybe to see water dragons. Beautiful area.

reviews.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Manly was by far our favourite beach. So much to do there as well as the bay were it's not so rough. We did a surf lesson had fish and chips and then waited to catch the ferry back just before sunset (our guide the day before gave us this top tip). It was a fantastic day we also visited Bondi but it was to crowded and the ferry to manly is much nicer then the bus and train to Bondi.

reviews.title: Nice cozy beach
reviews.text: Nice cozy beach, on a far end of Sydney, easy  to reach by ferry, good for cooling down on a hot summer day

reviews.title: The best beach we saw!!!
reviews.text: We enjoyed a day of play at the beach and couldn't get over the beautiful Manly beach. Lots of things to do, but the best by far was playing in the surf. Coming from California where the water is cold, it was great to be in warmer water which allowed us to stay and enjoy it. We rented a few lounge chairs and umbrella ($35 for 4 hours) and loved our day spent there. We ate at Manly Grill and enjoyed some yummy food. Staff was friendly and view was even better. Great day spent at Manly Beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful and scenic
reviews.text: But very crowded on weekends in Summer. We found this to be too much for us and decided to hop on a bus to the National Park.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, trendy shops, great food.
reviews.text: Wow! Manly Beach has it all. A beautiful beach with soft sand and turquoise water. Snorkeling spots. Surf. Trendy boutique shops- I came back with 2 bags of darling beachy stuff. The food is really good. Lots of choices- and great outdoor seating areas to enjoy the seaside view. The Walt from Spit Bridge to Manly is fun as well.

reviews.title: Party Atmosphere
reviews.text: Nothing to dislike. Manly is perfectly situated with everything you could want within a short distance. From the ideal beachside with plenty of shops, hotels, pubs and good restaurants. The beach side is an ideal location to chill and relax, do some surfing or go for a walk to Shelly beach. The ferry side offers great bars, more restaurants, great place to sit and picnic and a short ferry ride to the City. For the adventurous you also have the Spit to Manly walk or a shorter walk to North Head look out. Plenty of private beaches in and around Manly. Manly has plenty of buses including the free Hop, Skip and Jump service, car parking can be expensive.

reviews.title: Nice beach with shopping nearby
reviews.text: Pretty beach and loved the nearby street with all the shops and eateries.  There was a tourist souvenir shop with bargains.

reviews.title: A trip to the beach in February
reviews.text: We stopped at Manly Beach on our annual February “ Escape Winter for a Fed Days” adventure. The beach was amazing. A series of 5 beaches that all appear to be joined by a seaside walking path.  We didn’t have time to follow the path from start to finish because we got to the beach in the middle of them. We took the southerly path and enjoyed the weather and the beautiful people.

reviews.title: Loud music and expensive parking
reviews.text: Wow, this place is so overrated. More and more people are bringing speakers, so if you expected to have a nice, relaxed day at the beach then be prepared to be disappointed. As in the whole of the Northen Beaches, the parking is ridiculously expensive.

reviews.title: Japanese with a view
reviews.text: Experience manly beach sparkling in the afternoon sun while eating beautifully prepared Japanese food. Lots  of choice on the menu at Minato- all presented  simply. A relaxed chilled atmosphere- with the staff eager to pleas.

reviews.title: An added bonus after a ferry trip to Manly
reviews.text: Jump on the ferry in the city, when you alight in Manly it’s a few hundred metres and you are at the beach. Iconic, open and welcoming, Manly beach is great for those who want to couple a good beach experience with a few options for good food and bar/cafe activities.

reviews.title: Manly beats Bondi
reviews.text: In my humble opinion Manly beats Bondi ANY DAY! The town, the Beach and the ferry there everything is amazing! The trip is a small cruise of the harbour for the price of a train ticket! Get on the boat first and sit outside do the weather allows for it! Get a beer and some pub grub on one of the hotels, you cannot go wrong! On a sunny day, the Pacific is friendly and the Beach is unbeatable and by far my favourite Sydney beach! Though farther than Bondi, easier to reach. Spend a few hours there.... swim, tan, relax! BUT lather up guys, the SUN is out to get you! 😉🌞

reviews.title: A perfect ferry visit
reviews.text: Loved visiting Manly beach. Nice promenade and the beach itself was not crowded like Bondi beach. Well connected by ferry.

reviews.title: outstanding earlier this week!
reviews.text: Manly Beach, rips and all, was just superb this week! The water was cooling and refreshing amidst the heatwave and the waves as they crested 'gnarly' and giving one a means of riding in to the foreshore. This beach was full but not impossibly so. It is a long, fine crescent of sand that bedazzles with its beauty. It was great to share time with my son here!

reviews.title: Fabulous place!
reviews.text: Loved it here! You have everything including great shops, yum food venues and restaurants, open beach at one end and quiet beach the other end. All in walking distance of everything! Highly recommend this :)

reviews.title: Sydney - NSW - Manly Bay / Beach
reviews.text: The Christmas holiday season & winter time in the US equals summer in Australia. By the time March rolls around, it's the rainy season in New South Wales, all along the Sydney harbour & southern coastal regions. Manley is a unique and special Beach, much less crowded than Bondi, and just a short ferry ride away from Sydney which in itself makes the trip absolutely breathtaking! as a tourist you can get a week-long rider pass that covers both the fairies trains and the bus system, which is the best deal going that I've ever had touring a country! as you go across the waters on the ferry you passed the opera house, and head over to Manley with beautiful views of the Sydney City in the distance. To me the best part of spending time in manly Beach was taking this scenic ferry ride... There were plenty of bars, Cafe's, and lovely restaurants over in the Manly Bay area. This is a must SEE & DO while visiting Sydney. Remember hot & humid is name of the game in Ozz, so remember H2O +sunscreen :)!

reviews.title: Amazing place to hang out and relax.
reviews.text: Manly beach is such a vibrant, colorful and full of life place. You can swim or surf, you can walk or ride a bike, you can grab a coffee or enjoy good food, you can take the ferry or you can just take some pictures. Just name it!

reviews.title: Cool spot to play
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and beautiful people. Food is awesome and lots of surfing options. Quick ferry from the city.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: This is an amazing beach and a great location. Easy to get to from Sydney Harbour via the ferry. Plenty of shops, bars, and restaurants. Always plenty going on.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: Took the fast ferry from Circular Quay to Manly. Short walk from ferry to the beach through a shopping district. great beach.

reviews.title: Really pretty spot
reviews.text: Loved our visit to manly. Really pretty location. We enjoyed fish and chips on the beach from one of the local shops along the walk down to the beach. The ferry was easily accessible and well worth the trip as well. It was a lovely day out

reviews.title: Great Outing for the Day
reviews.text: We ventured to Manly Beach via the ferry from Sydney Harbor and had a great brunch at the waterfront restaurant, “White Water Seafood Grill & Bar.” There were 950 people on the ferry and in mass they all headed to the shore. This is a beautiful beach with shady pine trees hovering over the promenade. We followed the foot path to Shelly beach, another lovely cove.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and town
reviews.text: we got the ferry to Manly from Sydney a couple of times, lovely clean beach and great for swimming but watch out for the Blue Bottle stingers if the wind is blowing into shore as they get washed up on the beach. A must if you are in Sydney.

reviews.title: Love love lived our afternoon here in the 1950s
reviews.text: Like a blast back in to the past, this tiny city w/i city is soooooo refreshing after throngs of Sydney. Walk to "beach" , get a gelato , pull up a oark bench and people watch. Much more fun than Bondi for seniors!

reviews.title: Great Day Out
reviews.text: We took the Manly Ferry here early one Sunday. On arrival there were not too many people on Manly Beach which looks divine. We settled on Shelly Beach for a while and then returned to Manly Beach. Here we had plenty of options for food and drinks. Later that afternoon we went to the roof top of Hotel Styne where we had a great view of Manly.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: A beautiful place to visit. Beautiful beaches a very active beach, lots of surfing. Plenty restaurants to visit and shopping.

reviews.title: Great popular beach and surf
reviews.text: Great beach, very popular and has some good shopping. Great walkway along the coast too. Manly beach is easy to get to from center of town using the public transport ferries from Circular Quay. Recommended ferry ride for the scenery alone as it passes the Sydney Opera house. Best photos at twilight.

reviews.title: Beach
reviews.text: Got on the ferrie from Sydney to manly beach amazing food place amazing and plenty of shopping then back to Sydney and spend the night in Sydney

reviews.title: Far superior to its noisy neighbour!!
reviews.text: Jumped a 30 min boat ferry from Circular Quay and strolled down a pleasant street to the side sandy beach,backed by palm trees and a boulevard, and just relaxed watching the world and surfers go by, great stuff.

reviews.title: well worth a visit
reviews.text: We took the ferry to Manley beach When you get off its a short walk to the beach Well worth a visit lots of shops bars and a lovely beach

reviews.title: Lovely Clean & Friendly
reviews.text: Took the ferry over to Manly from Circular Quay. Wuick only took 20 minutes. Stunning views from the boat of Opera House and Harbour Bridge. Manly has lovely beach, nice and clean with plenty of places to eat and drink.

reviews.title: Xmas day on Manly beach
reviews.text: What a fantastic Christmas Day on Manley Beach box of fruit and in and out of the sea absolutely fantastic Christmas morning

reviews.title: Picnic and walk at Manly
reviews.text: Manly Beach is accessible by train 🚞 and ferry ⛴. You can drive and spend a wonderful day going for beach walk or having coffee around the shopping centre. It has a holiday atmosphere and is very relaxing to have picnic with friends and family.Children love 💕 to spend time during school holidays or on the weekends.

reviews.title: Relaxed Vibe
reviews.text: Everyone doesn't experience it, but there's no better way to "approach" Manly than by ferry, whether high speed or "normal".  Ferries transport one across the harbour, enhancing the expectation of relaxed Manly. With the added advantage of both harbour and surf beaches, Manly is unique. On arrival there is no end of possibilities ...  swim, eat, relax, enjoy the walk to Fairy Bower. Because of the competition, prices are generally very competitive, and the choices endless.

reviews.title: The journey on the ferry is worth the visit
reviews.text: Lovely beach the water is very cold, lots of surfing and very pretty town. The ferry journey was lovely well worth the trip

reviews.title: Love Manly Beach!
reviews.text: You can't miss coming to Manly if you are a visitor to Sydney. It's easy to get to from the city by ferry. Manly Beach is popular with surfers and there is a section which is patrolled by life guards which are usually marked by 2 flags. It's a great beach and very popular with locals and tourists alike. Saw now that you can rent boogie boards, umbrellas, deck chairs in this Summer season. There is a lovely walkway along the beach.

reviews.title: Watch the surfers
reviews.text: It’s easy to take the high speed ferry from Circular Pier and a short walk to the promenade, where there are some benches and public toilets.  The best swimming are appears to be at Shelly Beach.  An ocean pool is a good flat water option for children

reviews.title: Discover Manly
reviews.text: As an avid Sydney loving couple we decided to venture over to Manly as we hadn't been for quite a while.What a delight.The Manly Pacific Novatel Hotel staff were warm and welcoming,the rooms were clean air con worked well[it was 40degrees]and across the road the surf was wonderful.There was an abundance of great coffee shops and Restaurants but the in house Dining room and bar proved too inviting to miss.The early morning walk on Marine parade is not to be missed around to Fairy Bower as it winds around the rocks and the surf edge.It is also easy walking and is bike ,pram  and wheelchair friendly.There is an exciting retail environment for the shoppers or if you prefer jump on a ferry for a beautiful cruise to the Sydney CBD and back.Give Manly a try you will love it.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Manly is a beautiful place from the beach to shopping. Ferries leave Sydney Harbour on a regular basis.

reviews.title: A perfect day in manly.
reviews.text: I spent a beautiful day in manly whilst travelling in sydney. It was perfect and only a short ferry ride away. The beach and bay were beautiful, peaceful to relax and a lovely town to look around.

reviews.title: Best Beach Town
reviews.text: My wife and I visited Manly for a day and thoroughly enjoyed our visit. Manly offered a nice combination of beach activities, restaurants and shops. This area is clearly a favorite of Sydney as we saw many people; however, we never felt overly crowded. As we walked towards the beach (from the ferry wharf), we walked through the many stalls of independent artists selling their wares. We then walked south along the beach on the promenade toward Shelly Beach. This was a very pleasant walk with the beach on one side and various shops or rock cliffs on the other. We did have lunch at Shelly Beach. This area was alive with beach going young people and families. In my view, Manly is a must-see for those visiting Sydney.

reviews.title: Crowded with little Ozzie nippers
reviews.text: A great beach and my visit was same day as junior surf club training on a massive scale. Fun to watch the enthusiasm

reviews.title: pleasantly surprised
reviews.text: If you want waves then Manly is your beach. Take the ferry from Circular Quay walk down the mall to be pleasantly surprised by the pristine appearance of this beach.

reviews.title: Amazing area
reviews.text: Very nice and quiete area, there are many beautiful houses, it's peaceful. It's a shame that it is a long way to go over there (we had to take the ferry!)

reviews.title: Classic Australian Ocean Beach
reviews.text: Manly beach is sufficiently large for the large crowds it attracts during the Austrlalian summer. We were there on the Sunday or Australia Day weekend and there were 10's of thousands of people there. Swim lanes were well marked and patrolled and the surfers were kept in their lanes off to the north and south of the main swimming areas.Water was clear and refreshing and the waves relatively benign but still crashing and pounding on the beach with monotonous regularity. We enjoyed our day at the beach and then a quiet cold beer in one of the bars just back off the beach afterwards.

reviews.title: Spectacular beach
reviews.text: Great for surfing, nice view of mountains,beach play,kids play,streets buzzing with restaurants&shops

reviews.title: A MUST DO FOR OUR OVERSEAS VISITORS
reviews.text: As a Sydneysider, a fun experience remains the trip to Manly Beach on the ferry. The trip is cheap, takes approximately 30 minutes and leaves from wharves 3,2 and sometimes 6 (the information boards are very clear) and is particuallrly good fun for children. Manly has a lot to offer with plenty of cafés, ice cream shops, restaurants, good quality clothing shops, weekend markets and lots more. The beach is well patrolled and most days offers safe swimming. The beach is clean. There are plenty of tables and benches along the esplanade where you can sit and enoy your take away breakfast, lunch or dinner and get a a good glimpse of Australians at play. A must do

reviews.title: Beautiful beach in surprising setting
reviews.text: After taking the Manley fast ferry from Circular quay we arrived at Manley and assumed the small beaches around the jetties were what we had come to see.  However upon exploring a little further and checking with a local, we were advised to take a short walk through the pedestrianised precinct and see what awaited us at the end.  Well worth us checking as the view of the beach on approach was amazing.  Beautiful golden sands and turquoise sea beckoned us.  Spent some time on the southern side of the beach watching the surfers, then took a stroll around the headland to the next beach where we had refreshments and a shade break at The Boathouse before returning to Manley Beach for a little more sun.  Finished with a cold beer in one of the local bars before taking return ferry back.  Manley itself is lovely, very chilled atmosphere and although we didn't eat there we observed lots of eating places.  Couldn't swim on our part of the beach due to currents, (you could further around) but did enjoy a paddle.  Just watch out for the blue bottle jellyfish which did seem prevalent following earlier storms.

reviews.title: Take the ferry to Manly Beach !!!
reviews.text: A lovely, inexpensive & not too long ( 30 min.) ferry ride across the Sydney Harbour is the nice little suberb of Manly....which happens to have one of the nicest & most well-kept public beaches in & around Sydney. If you are a beach-goer , it's a great place to go,, enjoy the sun,salt & sand ...... &, of course, people watch !

reviews.title: Just amazing
reviews.text: Food beaches street market.what a day out with the family full of fun and joy.  Had the iron man comp today was great.  People behaved and we'll mannered it made the day

reviews.title: A great first place to visit by ferry from Sydney
reviews.text: A major streetcar project is underway at Circular Quay and we just wanted to get out on the harbor. The best option for ferry or other public transportation is obtaining a card at any convenience store near the ferries. We started with $10Aud cards which one can “top up” as needed. We had a lovely ferry ride to Manly Beach and decided to walk to a recommended restaurant. This was a great decision as it took us away from the commercial section and provided a nice walk through leafy and lively neighborhoods. Coming back, we followed a path around Manly Harbor, checked out a few shops and took the ferry back to Sydney.

reviews.title: A Beach!
reviews.text: A pleasant beach - a nice place for families to visit.   A promenade to walk along.  Lots of wind surfers.

reviews.title: Nice day out
reviews.text: The beach is just 10-15 minutes' walk from the Manly Wharf that was connected to Circular Quay by the speed Manly ferry. 30 minutes' ride costing $9.2 a single journey was fine but traveling on Sunday would be much more economical as the fare would be capped at $2.5 for the whole day.  This sand beach was really beautiful with clear turquoise water. The current was not too rough but good enough for surfing. Not crowded and very relaxing for sunbathing.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is a gorgeous beach which so epitomises Australian beach culture. We visited on a very hot day and the beach was packed. The sea was pretty dangerous especially on the outgoing tide but there are lots of warnings about swimming between the flags, which were not particularly well headed. They could do with some more changing facilities.

reviews.title: Great day on the beach
reviews.text: Took ferry to Manly beach then took long walks along the waters edge and along many beaches once there and loved it... so easy to do so beautiful and so enjoyable!

reviews.title: The "other side" of Sydney!!
reviews.text: Do yourself a favor and visit Manley Beach! It's an easy and fantastic ferry ride from Sydney Harbor with great views of the greater Sydney area and terrain.Manley Beach is a world unto itself with many who live there commuting to Sydney. Gorgeous beach and an urban beach community meets good living......

reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.text: Got the ferry from Circular Quay, very quick and easy, lots of eateries and bars which are reasonably priced and a couple of beaches, not overcrowded and less known than Bondi, a  good day out

reviews.title: Day trip
reviews.text: Gorgeous beach with a nice little shopping area.Much preferred here to Bondi. Easy to get here on a ferry. Would visit again.

reviews.title: Best thing to do in Sydney!
reviews.text: Great walks, wonderful beaches. Do not spend too much time in the city, be more adventurous! Take the ferry in Darling Harbour and on your way back stop at Watson’s Bay for a lunch at Doyle’s.

reviews.title: Great fun
reviews.text: Spent a couple of hours here at manly wharf enjoyed a beverage and fantastic pizza on wharf watching bthe world go by..beach crowded and lots of activities going on..enjoyable easy and great day trip hybferry from circular Quay

reviews.title: A wonderful beach area
reviews.text: We loved spending the day at Manly Beach. It was fun to take the ferry from Circular Quay and head over. There are many shops and places to grab food and drink. The surf is a lot of fun to play in! It was rough the day we were there, and the lifeguards had swimmers limited to a smallish area. It didn’t take anything away from the experience. A great time indeed!

reviews.title: Ferry visit to manly
reviews.text: Caught the ferry to Manly beach from circular Quay. 30 minutes on the boat and your there. Busy area with lots to see and do. Market on sunday was nice.

reviews.title: Lovely Beach
reviews.text: We enjoyed our visit to Manly Beach especially just walking along the promenade and people watching.  It was late afternoon when we arrived but it was still busy.  It was fun watching the young children attending the surf lessons.  No matter the age, they all seemed to be enjoying what they were doing.

reviews.title: Nicer than Bondi in my opinion
reviews.text: A good day or half day trip from Sydney and a perfect excuse to ride the ferry.  Nice beach, nice promenade along the beach and plenty of restaurants and shopping.  Even a craft brewery by the ferry.Really worth it on a nice day!

reviews.title: Great beach and shops/cafes
reviews.text: Visited Manly Beach a couple times on our trip and rate it as one of the better beaches I have visited.  I rented a chair which made it very comfortable.  Definitely take some time to eat at the many local cafes and visit the shops nearby.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach!
reviews.text: It was one of the only beach days we had - we were so happy we chose to go to Manly. It's very convenient to get to - Manly Fast Ferry!

reviews.title: lovely beach, with plenty of food options
reviews.text: beautiful beach with great waves. Very limited swimmable area when we were there because of high currents, and a few blue bottles in the water. But there are facilities to rent umbrellas and chairs, decent public toilets, showers and changing rooms.Between the arrival of the ferry and the beach, there is a nice road, closed to traffic with plenty of food options for all tastes.

reviews.title: Beautiful, but
reviews.text: Manly is such a great big beautiful beach that it is a great day to take the ferry and go over.  The sand is great and the beach is clean.  There was a nice breeze off the water to keep things cool but pleasant.  Due to the weather, the area for swimming in was quite restricted.  Later, the beach was essentially closed to swimming as blue bottle jellyfish came in.  My recommendation would be to check first before going if you plan on going in the water

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We liked the vibe and feel of this beach over Bondi.  The beach is beautiful, very clean, restaurants and shopping close by.  We stayed in circular quay so we rode the fast ferry there and it cost us $9.70 on our Opal card, which is the card you will get to use for transportation on the ferries, buses and trains. The fast ferry gets you there in 12 min and worth the extra $1.50 over the slow ferry.  We went twice and ate once at a Mexican restaurant and the other time at a southern restaurant. There is a place to rent chairs, umbrellas, surfboards.  The chairs rent out quickly. We went on a Tuesday and first time we went they were sold out by noon and we went a week later at the same time and got lucky and rented a chair. The chair cost $10 for 3 hours or $15 for all day and $15 for an umbrella if you want one and $25 for 2 hour surfboard rental.  The chairs are very nice.  There are lifeguards here.  I would recommend a visit here. We did a coastal walk down to another very small beach and it is a nice walk about 30-45 min. Along the walk there is a place to rent snorkel gear, shops and restaurants.

reviews.title: Great beach, Harbour & surf
reviews.text: A great day out on the Harbour to travel to Manly by Sydney Ferries where you alight on the Harbour side, and enjoy all it has to offer. Then walk down “The Corso” Street to the surf side of the ocean of Manly & enjoy all it has to offer as well. This street joins the 2 areas of water bodies. Lots of shops to browse, places to eat, drink & but ice cream & even a hotel or two along “The Corso”to have an alcoholic beverage in if you so  desire. Lots of water fountains for kids to play in the water along “The Corso” so bring the kids a change of clothes or let them wear their swimmers. Great fun, kids always love water fountains coming out of the ground where you walk!! Highly recommended, great for visitors, tourists & Oz residents  as well!

reviews.title: Favorite beach
reviews.text: I was here years ago and loved it then and loved it this trip too. Not as big and busy as Bondi. It is such a great beach area.

reviews.title: Safe swim beach, great cafes, and relaxed atmosphere
reviews.text: Very good lifeguard service, so safe swimming in the waves. Large but cosy beach with plenty facilities to shop and/or eat.

reviews.title: Lovely beach but not much space between flags for swimming
reviews.text: Beach is beautiful which stunning water and sand. Unfortunately there were quite a few rips when we went and we were advised by life guards to remain between the flags. Unfortunately for us the flags weren't placed very far apart due to the volume of rips on the day.  We just stayed knee level outside the flagged area which was fine. You can hire beach umbrellas for about $20 which was a godsend in the heat. The toilets aren't ideal and smelt strongly of urine but that's a common issue with toilets at beaches. Otherwise an enjoyable experience, especially coupled with a lovely ferry ride and gelati.

reviews.title: BEST Beach!
reviews.text: We LOVED Manly Beach!  We were there for NYE and it wasn't too terribly crowded.  We got there around 11 each day and still were able to get rental lounge chairs and umbrella.  The water was super cold though!  Lots of shops around plus places to grab food.  Not to mention Coles supermarket is nearby.  Great place for kids to play in the sand.  Bring your sunscreen though!

reviews.title: Amateur Hour
reviews.text: Beautiful beach but massive amounts of tourists on the main streets and the beach. Lots of screaming babies, etc. some very nice places once you get off of the main streets. Nice for a very quick ferrry ride and brief visit, but definitely not quaint or relaxing.

reviews.title: Great to visit whatever the season
reviews.text: Go for a walk along the promenade. Beach volleyball lessons - even in winter, dogs being taken for walks (one even carrying its' own lead). Catch the Ferry from Circular Quay and see the Harbour from a different perspective then have lunch in Manly. A great day out.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: Manly has a lot more to offer in terms of dining, shopping and general sightseeing than the famed Bondi, so if you have time to just "do one", this is the one.

reviews.title: manly beach
reviews.text: lovely area with a great beach and shops. beach is attended by lots of lifeguards but beware of strong currents

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: May be less iconic but I prefer it. Also easier to get to (ferry). Has everything you need plus some good walks.

reviews.title: A crazy place!
reviews.text: A bustling beach even during the week with many toursit and local bodies taking in the sunny day. Just the right amount ot eateries, picnic tables, and a cooling breeze to make this a must-be-visited place during a Sydney Holiday.

reviews.title: Beautiful, but way too crowded on weekends
reviews.text: We took the Manly ferry over on a Sunday and it was super crowded.  No free spots on the beach.  Tons of people, prams, surfers and sun worshippers.  Try to visit during the week versus weekend.

reviews.title: Better than Bondi
reviews.text: We went here one evening from Sydney harbour for dinner and drinks. A very nice boat trip from town and only takes around half hour. We were very impressed by Manley. Having been to Bondi the day before we both agreed we preferred Manley as it had a much better feel to it, beach looked bigger and nicer and there was loads of choice for drinks and food. The ferry back to Sydney was nice in the evening as you can see the bridge and opera house all lit up. Highly recommend a visit here! Tip - on a Sunday the ferry charges are capped at $2.50 which is great value. They also accept contactless / pay wave payment which makes buying a ticket really easy as you don’t need to buy a ticket just tap your card!

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach!
reviews.text: I stayed and me only with a friend, just a short walk from the beach. The beach stretches for a very long distance, with beautiful white sands. Lots of people out enjoying the water, which was warm even on an overcast day. The beach also has activities such as surfing, snorkeling, scuba diving, kayaking, with vendors along the way that you can rent from or take guided tours with.

reviews.title: A popular location with Sydneysiders and tourists
reviews.text: Packed on the weekend in Summer, this beach offers an iconic Australian experience - white sand, surf and beachside restaurants  It can be reached by a ferry ride from Sydney followed by a short walk from the terminal.

reviews.title: A world class beach near the heart of Sydney
reviews.text: Spectacular beach with a gentle break and plenty of room to spread out. We'd always heard about Bondi but, in our opinion, Manly is its equal.

reviews.title: Busy sunshine day out
reviews.text: Such a busy place, full of tourists walking from the boat towards the beach. Lots of shaded areas to sit, and also changing rooms and toilets provided.  Sell worth a visit

reviews.title: Really nice
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our day in manly.. We spent the first few hours sittin on the beach. Then we got a takeaway lunch and sat on the grass looking out to the sea witj it.In the evening we walked around the shopping area stopping off for a drink and some ice-cream. Well worth the visit..

reviews.title: My favourite beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Great shopping, great food if you walk around to Shelley beach.Lifeguards in designated spots.  Volleyball.  Surf school.  This beach has everything.  Also the trip over on the ferry gives great views of the opera house and bridge.  When you get off the ferry walk along the high street to the beach.  A lot of people make the mistake that the Wharf is Manly beach.

reviews.title: A perfect complement to the bustle of Sydney
reviews.text: This is a delightful day trip from central Sydney. Take the ferry from Circular Quay, the slower one, not the fast ferry. More leisurely, runs every 20 minutes throughout the day, and is a few dollars cheaper. Make for the beach, barely ten minutes walk from the wharf. But give yourself time during the day to soak in the atmosphere of The Corso, full of surfy shops, boutiques and fast food. Then jump on the ferry for the half hour cruise back to Sydney. Enjoy! We did.

reviews.title: Manly is NOT better than Bondi. Not at all. Sorry.
reviews.text: I'm very sorry, but at Manly Beach there is almost NO infrastructure. You cannot rent a towel (at Bondi you can). There is NO safe or locker (Bondi Beach offers that). You cannot rent body boards (Bondi Beach does).And there are more restaurants and bars at Bondi Beach next to the beach with a view OF the beach.

reviews.title: Manly Beach - Sydney - didgeridoo music
reviews.text: We took the ferry to Manly Beach from Darling Harbour. Great way to see alot of Sydney from the Ferry - including the Sydney Opera House, Circular Quay, Sydney Harbour Bridge.I found Manly Beach very interesting. So an aboriginal play the didgeridoo. I love this musical instrument. It is like a looooooong wooden pipe, and from my understanding not an easy instrument to play. The music is very soothing to hear.Lots of visitors - very busy place. Nice spot to spend half a day at the beach.

reviews.title: Better Than Bondi
reviews.text: I wasn't in the Manly Beach area very long, but if I ever get back to Sydney it is somewhere I wold go again, if only for the sunset ride across the harbour back to Circular Quay, that is amazing. I liked the beach better than Bondi, it was quieter and nicer looking. The area around Manly is nice too, with many shops and places to eat.

reviews.title: beach plus crowds
reviews.text: everybody has heard of Manly beach the world over you can drive ,catch the bus or catch the ferry from circular quay ,ferry is the best way to see Sydney harbour though it can get very busy,manly is very touristy with the usual collection of fast food places,ice cream shops etc,the beach is great clean with a great vista ,there a good walk north and south,unless you want to spend the whole day here ,1/2 a day should do you ,worth a visit though

reviews.title: ROLLERS BAKEHOUSE- WOW!!!
reviews.text: Manly is a stunning place to visit- walks, swims and eats.I found a fabulous cafe with a wonderful pastry concept in Rialto Lane with the most amazing croissant and pastries with wonderful new flavours. I highly recommend monkey bread, almond croissant, a pavlova croissant and savoury pastries as well and the coffee is lovely too.A lovely place for breakfast and lunch and many young children were loving it and eating happily.

reviews.title: Avoid it if you like to relax
reviews.text: I guess this beach is even more crowded than any other beach I have been to.... even in Europe...Only allowed to swim between the flags, which is a good thing... but on this beach looks likes packed sardines....

reviews.title: Almost a mini cruise
reviews.text: A trip on the Harbour ferry provided spectacular photo opportunities of the Opera House, Bridge and Circular Quays. An absolute must for photographers.When you arrive at Manly it is a very pleasant stroll through boutique shops and restauarants. Some are a little touristy but well worth the stroll.The beach itself is great. Less crowded than Bondi and much more comfortable. A great way to introduce yourself to Sydney, just a morning or afternoon will sufice.

reviews.title: Great beach for families.
reviews.text: We went here to check out the beach.  It was a lot of fun with a small town feel and lots of restaurants to choose from.  We took a ferry there which cost $60 return for our family of 4.  It departs every 20 minutes.  Manly Beach is very big, but the water was very cold.  It's definitely worth a visit.  People were playing beach volleyball on the beach.  You can walk the entire length of the beach on the walk way as well.

reviews.title: Best beach in Sydney!
reviews.text: Make sure you get a day in Manly - skip Bondi if you are short on time - this beach is so much better!!

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Lovely white beach with a good surf for sports. It is monitored and flags and warnings are given if the sea turns too rough during the day.  You can walk from the beach to a park or up to the headland.  Lots of cafes and restaurants for food choices.  Plus shops and supermarkets to buy picnic food.

reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.text: Combines with a nice ferry ride, this is worth a visit. Busy, but not so busy as Bondi. A lot of surfers, but the rescuers limit where you can swim without a surf board.

reviews.title: Lots to do, but get away from the Corso.
reviews.text: There's so much to do in Manly, so get away from the Corso!!   The walk along the beach to Shelly Beach is always great.  The Boathouse at Shelly beach is often overcrowded, but there are some great cafes near Fairy Bower with great food.  It's usually best to swim at the Ocean Beach in the morning before the onshore wind kicks in.  East Esplanade or Shelly beach are usually better in the afternoon as they're out of the wind.  In Manly itself, check out the laneways, that's where you'll find the best food and shops.

reviews.title: Too many Bluebottle jellyfish to enjoy the water, but the beach is nice
reviews.text: We took a ferry from Circular Quey to Manley beach Which is a nice way to see Sydney harbor from another perspective. The walk from Manley harbor to the beach takes about 10 minutes, passing many shops and restaurants along the way. You can pick up cheap towels, toys, sunscreen, bottled water, etc as you go. At the end of the main street you’ll find the beach. Manley Beach Rentals has umbrellas, chairs, boogy boards, etc to rent and they’ll set it all up for you. We got there by 10 on a holiday weekend and shortly after that there were no more umbrellas. The beach is large and well-groomed. There’s a snack shop at one end selling toasties (sandwiches), smoothies, soft drinks and snacks, all reasonably priced. There are public bathrooms, showers, and lifeguards. Our only complain is that there were so many jelly fish that the lifeguards warned against swimming. Also, there is only a small area where it’s sage to swim due to rip currents. If you just want to relax on the beach, but not venture out into the water, then this beach works.

reviews.title: Favorite beach in the entire world
reviews.text: I have been coming to Australia every two years since the mid 1990’s, and Manly Beach is always a required visit at least once.  It is beautiful, family friendly, plenty to do for everyone, and has lots of shopping and food options. It doesn’t have that sleazy beach town feel that some beach towns get.  It has a special charm.  Sorry I don’t have a lot of photos.  All my photos have my family in them, and I don’t want to post those.

reviews.title: Nicest city beach near Sydney
reviews.text: This beach has it all. High waves for pro surfers, white sand, surrounded by a promenade where you will find picnic benches in the shade, shops and hotels across the main road, free beach volleyball courts, a section where you can rent umbrellas and sun beds. Parking comes at AUD 10/hour, needs a bit of patience in high season to find a spot.

reviews.title: Worth the trip...
reviews.text: Great way to see more of Sydney while on the boat. The beach is great if you are into swimming and sunbathing big time.

reviews.title: Nice and Laid Back
reviews.text: Manly Beach is a quiet laid back beach community not as bustling as  Bondi but I really enjoyed the views, the shops and restaurants and the strolling.  Wasn't a good beach day the day we visited but we sat on the benches right on the beach and just relaxed.

reviews.title: Surfing to snorkelling to scenic walk, manly is a full package
reviews.text: Take the fast ferry from Circular Quay at Sydney Harbour to Manly, the beach and the walkway is just 5-7 min walk. On a beautiful day, the sea is awesome and the walk is scenic. There is a harmony between the locals and tourists. From kids to elders a day in Manly is really enjoyable

reviews.title: A great swimming beach with huge expanses of sand
reviews.text: Do yourself a favour after ticking Bondi (and Coogee) off your list and jump on the ferry across to Manly to enjoy this sprawling beach. Far fewer people and a more relaxed atmosphere give it a different feel. There mightn't be much in the way of facilities, but it's a beautiful spot for a swim and to soak up the sun. The promenade above has some great shaded grassy areas to relax in.

reviews.title: Wonderful Wonderful!
reviews.text: This is such an excellent place to take a vacation. The hotel we stayed at was superb, the people we met who lived in the area (Bill and Susan) just raved about how this was the best place for them (and they had been all over the world). There are beaches, shops, restaurants, clear blue skies, and really nice people wherever you go. The local people we met did not seem put off by tourists, and were friendly, easy-going, and kind. No wonder Bill and Susan don't want to go anywhere else. Fabulous.

reviews.title: A great alternative to Bondi....
reviews.text: Enjoyed the fast ferry from Circular Quay. Short walk from pier to beach , via a shopping and eating pedestrian friendly street. Beach has lifeguard patrolled sections but....surf can be high so exercise caution and stay between the flags. Shoreline walk to Cabbage Tree Aquatic Reserve area is very pleasant. Lots of eating and drinking spots.

reviews.title: Breakfast over the beach
reviews.text: Had a lovely breakfast, overlooking the beach. It looked clean and safe with lots of sports activities. Quaint place with a ferry to Sydney.

reviews.title: Visit after 30 years
reviews.text: My husband had spent his childhood in Manley 30 years ago and waited to visit Manley while we were visiting Sydney.  We walked along the road where he used to live and walked on the parks and spent the day on Manley beach. Great place to relax and lots of nappy people

reviews.title: Cute area to hang out!
reviews.text: Really nice beach area! Plenty of room for people, with a nice sidewalk and grassy area closer to the road to stroll on and sit to enjoy the view. Tons of shops and restaurants right there, and also places to rent rollerblades and bikes!

reviews.title: Beautiful but  a little boring
reviews.text: Likes: Very quiet. I came here winter time so that explains the quietness. I enjoyed watching the cute pets out for a walk.Dislikes: Nothing much to see. It's quite small and there's not much activity to do or events to see

reviews.title: Beautiful.
reviews.text: While in Sydney we took the Manly ferry to Manly and the beach.The ferry itself is a must as it gives you a fantastic view of the Harbour bridge and the Opera House from the water.Manly is a lovely, laid back place with lots of cafes, bars and eating spots. Also look out for the cockatoos.But the beach is some of the finest sand I have seen. Make sure you try and walk as much of it as possible.

reviews.title: Live in Manly.
reviews.text: Ive lived in Manly for 25 yrs.  Its gone from fantastic to mediocre. Yes its great if you've never been here before, sure, But Ive seen the old Manly just slide away with ridiculous development, just ridding it of the old charm, fast food crap and a million and one surf shops with high prices. The Charm is gone, its turning into another Bondi with loud drunks any given night causing chaos and Brazilians turning into their kind of slum with council not caring.   RIP Manly.

reviews.title: Beautiful day at the new h
reviews.text: Enjoyed the ferry ride from Circular Quay and then the small walk to the beach. The beach is clean and tidy and the water warm. Great place to visit.

reviews.title: Great getaway!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and small enough to enjoy without throngs of crowds.  Access to amenities ie food etc very convenient.

reviews.title: Beautiful Manly Beach
reviews.text: The beach was beautifully clean and games of volleyball being played on the beach was lovely to take in. People having picnic lunches along with beach on the chairs and tables that are along the beachfront. Perfect for swimming or a nice coastal walk.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Not as commercial as I imagined. Very clean beach with lifeguards taking a firm line with any one straying outside designated areas

reviews.title: Lovely family style beach.
reviews.text: Good sandy beach with lifeguard patrols.Promenade with toilet and shower facilities, shops,cafes and restaurants.  Very busy at weekends

reviews.title: Iconic breezy northern beach
reviews.text: One of the larger and best beaches in Sydney, with lesser hype and crowds than its more famous cousin Bondi, and its long stretch of foreshore sand means more people can spread out. The Life Saving Club, public toilets, showers and change rooms at one end, together with a take-away kiosk serving coffee and healthy snacks provide basic necessities for bathers and surfers. There is a small triangular enclosed surf pool as well, which makes for great dipping for little ones. If lying on the beach is not your thing, there are plenty of long benches under the tall pines and some covered shelters with seating and tables for shade. Sitting quietly here looking out towards the Heads and ocean beyond, contemplating life is one experience not to be missed.Best way to get here: Take the normal ferry from Wharf No.3 at Circular Quay to Manly and enjoy the longer ride on the waves looking at the beautiful scenery around Sydney Harbour. If the weather allows, sit outside and enjoy the fresh air, breezes and ocean smells. The other Fast Ferry option is certainly quicker, but costs slightly more and only saves minutes, and the ride itself is not as enjoyable. Note that if you are using the Opal transport card, once you tap on at Circular Quay, there is not need to tap off at Manly Wharf. The return journey is the same. Exit through Manly Wharf and immediately at the entrance on the right is the Tourist Information Centre. You may obtain a free map of the area for walking trails here, otherwise walk straight ahead through the Concourse and past its tourist shops towards Manly Beach.

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: Take the Fast Ferry to Manley $17 return about a 20 min journey which is great. On arrival 2 little sandy beaches each side of ferry netted for safe swimming ideal for kids.Head directly over the road down the Main Street to a fantastic expanse of beach. Great day

reviews.title: A nice beach
reviews.text: A small town. About 20 mins fast ferry from Circular Quay. Quiet and typical surfing town. Enjoy the beach. Good coastal walk. Enjoy the food. Just chill.

reviews.title: Best beach ever
reviews.text: As a local of manly beach it is the best beach ever. It is rarely over crowded and I can always a nice refreshing dip in the water after work

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Manly beach is a short ferry ride from Sydney Harbour and well worth a visit. Lots of shops and restaurants. The beach is beautiful and clean. It was great to stroll the boardwalk and taking the sites! Don’t miss it!

reviews.title: Musst see beach!
reviews.text: When you are in Sydney, you have to go to Manly at least once. I really like being there, such a nice atmosphere!

reviews.title: Forget Bondi. Head here
reviews.text: Forget the hype surrounding the tourist trap of Bondi and jump on a fast ferry at Circular Quay and head to Sydney's best beach. Large, suitable for all ages and pleasing on the pocket as Manly doesn't have the inflated prices associated with the other over-rated stretch of sand. On a note of caution, follow the safe swimming guides as there can be strong undercurrents.

reviews.title: Amazing beach from all angles
reviews.text: We went in Many somehow by chance on a free day in Sydney. It was the highlight pf our presence in Sydney. Manly is beautiful but best of all is Manly Beach, a huge strech of fine sand populated with surfers and sun bathers, very clean and, sometimes, foggy for few hours even in December mid-day. The promenade is also amazing, full of young and old walking, jogging, enjoying the sun, etc. A place not to be missed.

reviews.title: World famous
reviews.text: This prestigious beach was the site of the first Australian surf lifesaving demonstration. On the far side of the Corso from Manly Wharf, this beach has a long stretch of sand with a row of pine trees stretching out along the foreshore.
